The number of quadrature nodes is adapted to what the supplied moments support, subject to prescribed bounds of the phase-space coordinates, and the CQMOM implementation supports an arbitrary number of phase-space dimensions as well as any conditioning order. The principal numerical algorithms of QMOMKit are verified against analytical and manufactured solutions. Standalone spatially homogeneous applications, ranging from aerosol evaporation to particle dynamics and fragmentation, are compared with Monte Carlo solutions of the same population models, while coupling examples with OpenFOAM and deal.II demonstrate how QMOMKit can be embedded in finite-volume and discontinuous-Galerkin simulation frameworks. Together, these capabilities provide a tested and reusable foundation for a wide range of population-balance problems, and a basis for extending QMOMKit to other quadrature-based moment methods.

articles.title: Two-layer conjugate flows in an open channel
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.36242v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate conjugate flows in a two-layer fluid system with a flat bottom and a free surface. These are up- and downstream states consistent with simultaneous conservation of mass, momentum, and energy; and therefore candidate end-states of one-dimensional dissipationless bores. By choosing variables in a specific way, we are able to explicitly parameterize all physical non-trivial conjugate flows in the system, using only rational functions. This two-parameter family can be categorized according to whether the states are compatible with (1) a rising surface, and falling internal interface; or (2) vice versa. In particular, we rule out the existence of monotone bore solutions, consistent with an earlier result due to Chen, Walsh, and Wheeler. However, here we do so already at the level of conjugate flows. Separating these two distinct categories is a one-parameter family of critical trivial conjugate flows. The complete description obtained in the present paper serves as an important stepping stone towards finding actual realizing heteroclinic orbits connecting such conjugate states.

articles.title: DSMC Study of Hypersonic Boundary-Layer Unsteadiness Using Data-Driven Analysis
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.36248v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The prediction of transition remains challenging because the receptivity amplitude is usually prescribed rather than measured. This work uses Direct Simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC) to study an unforced Mach 6 nitrogen boundary layer over a 120 mm flat plate, with no imposed inlet wave, wall signal, modal shape, or disturbance spectrum. The retained unsteady field is the intrinsic finite-particle stochastic fluctuation field carried by the DSMC representation. Changing the DSMC particle count provides an independent numerical control parameter that sets a predictable finite-particle noise floor while preserving the time-averaged boundary-layer flow. Dynamic Mode Decomposition (DMD) is then applied to unforced DSMC snapshots. The DMD eigenvalues and spatial modes estimate the quantities that appear in the LST normal-mode description, including frequency, temporal growth or decay, wavenumber, wavelength, phase speed, mode location, and amplification envelope. LST is used after extraction to test whether the data-derived structures occupy the expected second-mode band. The results show that DSMC data can connect a measured finite-particle stochastic disturbance level to second-mode instability dynamics without imposed disturbance spectra.

articles.title: Neutron-Lean D-3He Fusion by Asymmetric Enhancement of the Primary Reaction: A Spin-Polarized Non-Thermal Hot Tail
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.36310v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper focuses on a modified fuel that combines the theory of spin-polarized fuel with non-thermal "hot-tail" reactions for D-T, D-3He, and D-D reactions. We find that this combination is particularly advantageous for the D-3He fuel in several respects. First, a large reactivity enhancement: one order of magnitude at 10 keV for a small hot tail (F = 0.1), rising to two orders of magnitude for a larger one (F = 0.6), with polarization adding a further factor of 1.5. Second, an ideal ignition energy far below the thermal value: 9.5 keV at F = 0.3 down to 3.2 keV at F = 0.5, which polarization reduces further to 3.8 keV and 1.3 keV, respectively. Third, the asymmetric enhancement between the primary reaction and the secondary reactions in the fuel opens the possibility of a neutron-lean reaction. Quantifying this with a neutrons-per-watt metric, we find that a thermal D-3He plasma at 10 keV is barely neutron-lean at all (90-95% of the D-T neutron rate per watt), whereas a hot tail of F = 0.1 reduces it by 4.7-7.7x and the polarized non-thermal fuel at its ignition point reaches 3.0-5.4% of the D-T value, with only 0.4-2.4% of the fusion power carried by neutrons. The range spans prompt removal versus complete in-situ burnup of the bred tritium. Applied to a 200 MW worked example anchored on the ARTEMIS D-3He reactor design, this is a first-wall neutron loading of 0.008-0.043 MW/m² against 1.45 MW/m² for D-T in the same chamber, extending the time to reach 20 dpa from about 1.5 full-power years to 27.

articles.title: Optically gated transduction enables silicon electrical readout of mid-infrared light
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.36475v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Silicon is the dominant platform for integrated photonics, yet its wide electronic bandgap of 1.1 eV fundamentally prevents efficient detection of mid-infrared (MIR) photons through direct valence band to conduction band excitation. Existing approaches therefore seek to enhance sub-bandgap absorption or introduce external infrared absorbers. Here we demonstrate a profoundly different detection strategy based on optically gated transduction, in which MIR photons modulate a pre-established excitation state rather than directly generating photocarriers. Our device integrates Nd3+-doped lanthanide nanoparticles with an inverse-designed Al/p-Si metasurface supporting dual resonances that simultaneously enhances optical gating in the near infrared and resonantly couples incident MIR radiation. The MIR illumination redistributes the Nd3+ emission pathways, producing an optical-state change that is converted into an electrical signal through a silicon Schottky junction. The device achieves room-temperature zero-bias detection at 6.8 um with a modulation responsivity of 103 uA/W and resolves combined gate and MIR inputs into three electrically distinguishable current states. Rather than extending silicon absorption into the infrared, this work establishes gated optical transduction as a route for reading MIR optical information on a silicon platform, opening opportunities for integrated infrared sensing, signal processing and programmable photonic systems.

articles.title: Rotation-driven suppression and re-emergence of unsteady flow past a circular cylinder
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.36556v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The flow past a rotating cylinder undergoes substantial changes in its wake dynamics and aerodynamic response with increasing rotation rate. This study investigates these changes in two-dimensional compressible flow at (Re_infty=3800) and (M_infty=0.1), with the rotation rate systematically varied over (0.1≤Ω≤10) using 130 high-fidelity simulations. At low rotation rates, conventional periodic vortex shedding is progressively suppressed with increasing rotation. A narrow transition regime around (Ω=2.2-2.8) is identified, where sustained oscillations evolve into intermittent fluctuations before reaching a nearly quiescent state. At higher rotation rates, unsteadiness re-emerges with distinctly intermittent and multiscale characteristics, demonstrating that this instability is fundamentally different from conventional Kármán shedding. The surface pressure and streamwise skin-friction distributions reveal substantial redistribution of aerodynamic loading with rotation, characterized by increasingly intense suction and significant modification of the near-wall shear field. The maximum lift increases systematically with rotation, reflecting the strengthening Magnus-Robins effect, whereas drag exhibits a non-monotonic response with enhanced variability at high rotation rates. Despite the low free-stream Mach number, rotational acceleration produces local Mach numbers approaching 0.5, indicating appreciable compressibility effects in the near-cylinder region. Vorticity-based proper orthogonal decomposition further reveals a transition from wake-dominated coherent structures at low rotation to strongly wrapped, rotation-dominated structures at high rotation. These results establish a direct connection between rotational forcing, surface loading, compressibility, and the suppression and subsequent re-emergence of flow unsteadiness.

articles.title: A regularized lattice Boltzmann model for the solid-liquid phase change
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.36642v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this study, a regularized lattice Boltzmann method is proposed for solid-liquid phase-change simulations. The governing total-enthalpy equation is solved within a regularized lattice Boltzmann (RLB) framework, which enables accurate tracking of the solid-liquid interface while effectively suppressing numerical diffusion. In addition, the multi-relaxation-time RLB (MRT-RLB) model with standard lattices is developed to solve the flow field. To enhance computational efficiency, an efficient multi-GPU (graphics processing unit) implementation based on CUDA C (Compute Unified Device Architecture) is developed, which is particularly suited for computationally intensive three-dimensional phase-change simulations. The proposed model is validated against a series of one-, two-, and three-dimensional benchmark problems. The results demonstrate that the present solver provides a robust, accurate, and efficient framework for simulating solid-liquid phase-change heat transfer.

articles.title: Fast diagonalization for matrix-free inversion of the nodal even-parity operator in hybrid finite element SPN transport
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.36716v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The hybrid finite element method stores a dense inverse of the nodal even-parity operator for every node and energy group, and that storage limits the spatial and angular expansion orders, more tightly still on a GPU, whose memory is smaller than that of a host. This work introduces fast diagonalization for the nodal even-parity operator of the hybrid finite element SPN method: the stored dense inverse is replaced by the eigendecompositions of a planar, an axial and an angular factor, and the inverse is applied without being formed explicitly. Every even-parity moment of the SPN equations obeys an equation of the same diffusion form, with no mixed derivatives, so the angular coupling is the same in every spatial direction. On a node extruded along the axis, the operator is then an exact Kronecker sum of the three factors. The factorization merely recasts the computation, so the discretization and the solution are unchanged, and the nodes are not required to be identical to one another. The method is implemented for CPU and GPU hardware and compared with the dense inverse within one solver. On a pressurized water reactor core in SP3, the two paths agree to within round-off error, the storage falls from 3.76 GB to 821 kB, and the calculation is 4.15 times faster. On a 33-group fast reactor core, the dense inverse would occupy 24.9 GB and the dense path would need more memory than both the device and the host provide, whereas the factors occupy only 1.26 MB, so the solution can be obtained. The factorization thus reduces the storage of the nodal inverse by more than three orders of magnitude and brings multigroup core calculations at their required spatial expansion orders within the memory of a single GPU.

articles.title: DSMC Study on Unsteadiness of Supersonic Flow Over a Cylinder
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.37048v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Unsteady flow over a 30 μm diameter cylinder at Mach 4 is investigated using Direct Simulation Monte Carlo across Reynolds numbers from 270 to 6750, spanning slip-flow to near-continuum regimes. Power Spectral Density analysis at discrete probe locations and Dynamic Mode Decomposition of flowfield snapshots independently characterize instabilities in both the stagnation and wake regions. In the stagnation region, a bow shock pulsation mode at 10-15 MHz frequency is identified across all cases despite a 24-fold variation in number density. In the wake, two distinct instabilities are observed. The canonical vortex shedding mode at Strouhal number St approx 0.2 dominates at lower Reynolds numbers. A second instability at St approx 0.5, consistent with previously reported slipline-driven oscillations in supersonic wakes, emerges at higher Reynolds numbers and progressively strengthens, becoming the dominant mode. In the studied Reynolds range, the wake transitions from no clear unsteadiness, to canonical vortex shedding at St approx 0.20, and reaching a regime where the St approx 0.5 mode becomes dominant, while also having a distinct independent bow shock pulsation possibly governed by its standoff distance.

articles.title: Mapping Artistic Engagement with Quantum Technologies
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.37054v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum technologies (QT) are increasingly being taken up in artistic practices, for example in the form of visual artworks or quantum computer music. However, more comprehensive empirical studies on the temporal development and the different forms of QT-related art are still lacking. Therefore, this study conducted a systematic mapping and classification of QT-related artworks. To this end, a medium-independent corpus was established, and the artworks were classified into four categories: QT-Inspired, QT-Sourced, Simulated QT, and QT-Generated. This classification was LLM-assisted and checked against human-coded reference data as well as through manual review of unclear cases. In total, 281 QT-related artworks from 2010 to August 2025 were identified. The corpus shows a substantial increase in QT-related artworks since 2019, with a considerable share attributed to only a few artists. The different forms of QT relations coexist, while an increasing use of active hardware-based and simulated processes in artistic practices can be documented, particularly since 2021. Although no clear development trajectories between these categories can be identified, the observed development coincides with advances in QT and their improved accessibility. Thus, this study provides an empirical basis for further analyzing the development of QT-related art, the possible emergence of a "quantum art scene," and the reciprocal relationships between art and quantum technologies.

articles.title: Rubidium-Referenced Frequency-Doubled Pockels Laser with High-Speed Electro-Optic Tuning
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.37279v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Narrow-linewidth lasers with rapid frequency control are essential for atomic physics and quantum technologies, yet combining these capabilities in chip-integrated sources at visible wavelengths remains challenging. Here we demonstrate a hybrid integrated InP/thin-film lithium niobate Pockels laser that emits at 780 nm through intracavity second-harmonic generation and supports gigahertz-bandwidth frequency tuning. A periodically poled lithium niobate waveguide is embedded in a laser cavity terminated by an extended distributed Bragg reflector, which provides electro-optically tunable feedback only at the 1560 nm fundamental wavelength. This design yields a singly resonant cavity that enhances frequency conversion while allowing the second-harmonic output to follow rapid tuning without resonance alignment. The laser achieves intrinsic linewidths of 2.7 kHz at 1560 nm and 9.0 kHz at 780 nm, with electro-optic tuning bandwidths beyond 1 GHz at both wavelengths. A mode-hop-free tuning range of 6.48 GHz at 780 nm enables direct spectroscopy of the rubidium D2 transition. Locking the second-harmonic output to this transition reduces the standard deviation of its frequency fluctuations from 135 MHz to 8 MHz and transfers the atomic frequency reference to the fundamental. These results establish integrated frequency-doubled Pockels lasers as compact, rapidly tunable sources that could simplify the optical architectures for future atomic and quantum photonic systems.

articles.title: Mode-2 solitary waves in continuous stratifications
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.37289v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Computed herein are examples of mode-2 internal solitary waves to the Dubreil-Jacotin-Long (DJL) equation. These are localised, fully nonlinear waves in a continuously stratified, inviscid fluid under the Boussinesq and rigid-lid approximations. The equation is solved directly using finite differences on a periodic domain, enabling the computation of both generalised solitary waves, which possess oscillatory mode-1 tails, and embedded solitary waves, whose tails vanish. Two stratifications are considered. The first is a double pycnocline, generalising the three-layer system considered by Doak et al. (2022) by replacing each infinitesimal interface with a pycnocline of finite thickness. The second stratification, a surface mixed layer above an exponentially stratified layer, shows that embedded mode-2 solitary waves are not restricted to double-pycnocline stratifications. These are the first mode-2 solitary waves of the DJL equation computed for stratifications that are asymmetric about mid-depth.

articles.title: Spatial Colorimetric Mapping of pH and Dissolved Carbon during Convective Dissolution of CO₂: Constraints from Domain, Geometry, and Indicator Mix on Measurement Reliability
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.37335v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantifying the dissolution and buoyancy-driven transport of CO2-rich water is critical to understanding solubility trapping mechanism in geologic storage. Analog-fluid density driven convection experiments do not represent CO2 dissolution chemistry or the aqueous CO2 density-concentration monotonic relationship. X-ray tomography does not provide enough contrast to directly measure dissolved CO2. Spatial colorimetry provides an inexpensive method to map pH and estimate total dissolved inorganic carbon (CT) via carbonate equilibrium assumptions. However, the effects of experimental conditions such as domain (free fluid and porous), geometry (2D and 3D), and indicator mix concentration on the reliability of pH and CT measurements remain unexplored. We evaluated how these factors affect the reliability of measurements using two different colorimetric models (hue and spherical coordinates (θ and φ)). Hue was reliable in all domains whereas θ-φ was reliable in free fluid. Lower indicator mix concentration increased the chromatic sensitivity at low pH in free fluid; however, it did not produce sufficient color contrast for pH calibration and mapping in the porous domain. In the porous domain, θ-φ calibration was 33 times more susceptible to noise than hue. Temporal pH noise was less than 0.01 units; spatial noise changed domain-mean CT by 0.6-4.4%. Both models were able to resolve CO2-rich plumes in free fluid; however, θ-φ had sharper plume boundaries than hue. The temporal evolution of CO2 dissolution resolved by the color models agreed more in 2D than 3D. These findings provide a reliability framework for studying subsurface dissolution and mixing of CO2.

articles.title: Development and assessment of a target-ω interfacial turbulence-damping model for stratified gas--liquid flow
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.37376v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Interfacial turbulence damping is required in Reynolds-averaged simulations of stratified gas--liquid flows when strong interfacial velocity gradients are present. In this work, we develop a target-ω interfacial damping formulation for the low-Reynolds-number Wilcox-type k--ω model in a one-field RANS/VOF framework. A gas-side target value of the specific dissipation rate ω is constructed from an effective interfacial wall coordinate determined from the local resolved flow. The constructed target-ω provides a smooth transition between the viscous and logarithmic limits through power-law blending and requires no calibration of model constants against target data. textcolorblack{The formulation is first assessed against three gas-layer DNS cases at Re_τsimeq180 with different interface velocities. The model reproduces the principal features of the mean velocity, turbulent kinetic energy and Reynolds shear-stress distributions, while showing substantially weaker sensitivity to the near-interface grid resolution than the Egorov-type formulation, although some grid dependence remains on the coarsest mesh. The assessment is then extended to the co-current Fabre stratified-flow experiment at a higher Reynolds number and to the counter-current Stäbler experiment}. In both cases, the present formulation provides generally good predictions of the gas-side mean flow and turbulence statistics without case-specific adjustment. For the Stäbler case, in which the liquid level develops as part of the coupled two-phase solution, the predicted mean liquid depth agrees closely with the measured value. These results indicate that the target-ω formulation provides a consistent interfacial turbulence-damping treatment for resolved large gas--liquid interfaces over the range of conditions considered.

articles.title: Surface-Illuminated Interdigitated Ge-on-Si Avalanche Photodiode With Separated Ge Absorption, Si Multiplication, and Lateral Field Engineering
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.37593v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work presents a surface-illuminated lateral Ge-on-Si interdigitated separate-absorption-charge-multiplication (SACM) avalanche photodiode for 1550-nm detection. The intrinsic-region spacing, P⁻ charge-control width, and finger geometry are engineered to suppress high-field penetration toward the Ge/Si heterointerface and localize avalanche multiplication in Si. Simulations show that wider charge-control or intrinsic regions reduce fixed-bias dark current and shift avalanche onset to higher reverse bias. Among the tested structures, the intrinsic-region spacing/P⁻ charge-control width of 0.5/0.15 μm achieved a peak responsivity of 11.81 A/W at 1550 nm. At a -20 V applied voltage, it exhibited a multiplication gain of 3.796, a 3-dB bandwidth of 7.13 GHz, and a matched-bias gain-bandwidth product of 27.07 GHz. Optical-power-dependent measurements also show avalanche-gain compression consistent with space-charge screening. These results demonstrate effective lateral-field engineering for high-speed, surface-illuminated Ge-on-Si APDs.

articles.title: Quantum hydrodynamics from Nambu's unpublished fluid notes
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.36275v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a quantum hydrodynamic theory based on Nambu's unpublished note emphA New Look at Fluid Dynamics. The kinetic action defines a metric on configuration space and a mechanical connection coupling an observable cyclic deformation to unobserved fluid modes. Tracing out these modes yields a quantum channel for the observed deformation. We establish a criterion for the exact preservation of coherence between opposite momenta and show how nonzero connection curvature prevents this coupling from being removed. The leading quadratic decay of quantum coherence is determined by the prepared quantum state. For two shear flows, we identify an exact noiseless sign subsystem. Introducing additional generating flows cancels the initial residual of the Euler equations while producing nonzero connection curvature, governed by the same kinetic integrals that determine the classical correction. At fixed mean energy, choosing amplitudes adapted to the dominant coupling flow substantially reduces the initial decoherence, even along the direction that cancels the Euler residual. This advantage gradually diminishes under conditional evolution, eventually leading to a crossing of the decoherence curves. Our example shows that a preparation with a smaller initial coherence-decay coefficient can have a larger maximum sampled loss over a finite readout interval.

articles.title: Experimental Geometric State Preparation on the Bloch Sphere Via Linear Mechanical Resonator
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.36322v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Bloch sphere representation, familiar from quantum two-level systems, can also describe classical linear systems whose dynamics are effectively confined to two modes. Here, we experimentally realize this framework in a linear two-mass, three-spring mechanical system by controlling superpositions of its symmetric and antisymmetric eigenmodes. The system is driven from both boundaries at a fixed frequency between the two resonances, so that the steady-state response remains within a two-mode manifold. By independently varying the relative amplitude and phase of the boundary excitations, we generate tunable modal superpositions. Scanning laser vibrometer measurements and frequency-domain analysis are used to extract the complex modal coefficients, which are then normalized and mapped onto Bloch sphere coordinates. This reconstruction reveals planar rotations of the state under phase sweeps and continuous steering between eigenstates under amplitude-ratio tuning. These results provide an experimental validation of Bloch sphere state reconstruction and steady-state geometric state preparation in a minimal linear mass-spring platform, establishing a simple classical testbed for exploring two-mode manifold dynamics.

articles.title: Controlled Dark-State Energy Storage and Work Extraction in V-Type Quantum Batteries
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.36704v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The performance of a quantum battery depends not only on its ability to retain stored energy against unwanted discharge but also on the amount of useful work that can be extracted from it. Here, we investigate these complementary aspects in an ensemble of V-type qutrits coupled to a lossy cavity. By applying a finite splitting pulse to the two excited states of each qutrit, cavity-bright excitations are converted into atomic dark states, whose populations remain protected upon restoring degeneracy, even while the light-matter coupling remains active. Simulations with finite-duration pulses reveal a capture window governed by the competition among energy transfer, bright-to-dark conversion, and photon leakage. We further show that if the energy is stored in the fully symmetric atomic subspace, the passive energy is bounded by twice the transition energy for number of atoms N≥2. Consequently, if the stored energy scales extensively with N, the ratio of extractable work to stored energy approaches unity in the thermodynamic limit. Comparing different initial preparations at equal mean input energy, we find that coherent-state can yield greater finite-time ergotropy despite capturing less energy, whereas Fock-state favors greater extractable work in the stationary component. Our results demonstrate how controlled dark-state population trapping in an atom-cavity coupled system can protect stored energy while providing a conditional route toward high extractable work.

articles.title: The impact of the sulfur allotropes and sulfur hydrides on the Venus cloud chemistry
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.36979v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Venus is home to vivid sulfur chemistry, with SO₂ as the major sulfur gas species and a global cloud layer between 47 and~70 km composed of H₂SO₄ and H₂O. The chemistry in the clouds has been extensively studied with 1D models, but none is able to reproduce the three orders of magnitude decrease of SO₂ inside the clouds. Sulfur allotrope chemistry could be a candidate for buffering sulfur atoms, as it can grow into long chains. Sulfur hydrides such as H₂S is considered as one of the main sulfur-bearing compounds, possibly linked to surface reactions or have a volcanic origin like on Earth. In this study, we use for the first time a 3D model to study the climatology of the sulfur allotrope in gas and condensed phase and hydride chemistry in the clouds with an explicit photolysis calculation and updated UV cross-section. H₂S is close to ppmv levels below the cloud base, the third most abundant sulfur-bearing species in this region after SO₂ and OCS. Below the clouds, S₈ gas phase is the most abundant sulfur allotrope. Above, the photolysis and condensation are preponderant, and the gas phase decreases to extremely low values. Polysulfur can therefore not be the unknown absorber at cloud-top altitudes. The condensed phase polysulfurs are present from 30 to above 100~km. S₂ condensed phase is the most abundant due to its low saturation mixing ratios. Polysulfur species represent a substantial sulfur reservoir in the upper cloud, equivalent to a few ppmv.

articles.title: Adaptive Information Mining: Approaching the Quantum Limit of Super-Resolution Imaging
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.37491v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The "Rayleigh limit" is not an intrinsic property of light, but a consequence of sub-optimal measurement of collected photons by the imaging instrument. To overcome this limitation, we present Adaptive Information Mining, a framework that achieves super-resolution by using sequentially refined measurements for incoming photons. Our approach employs a reconfigurable imaging system that dynamically reshapes the instrument measurement responses to maximize the Fisher information and guide scene estimation toward the fundamental quantum limit, even in deep sub-Rayleigh regimes. We demonstrate that this approach achieves an estimation error 2-5 times closer to the fundamental quantum limit than traditional direct imaging when imaging point sources, without requiring any prior knowledge of their positions and brightnesses. Importantly, we demonstrate that AIM can be extended to fully blind multi-parameter estimation in scenarios involving an unknown number of sources or turbulence-induced wavefront distortions. Our approach addresses the limitations of conventional fixed imaging, offering a practical path toward quantum-limited super-resolution imaging.

articles.title: Attention as Lattice Gauge Theory: Relations Interact Only Through Wilson Loops
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.37656v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Relations compose through the entity they share - Alice is Bob's mother and Bob is Carol's father, so Alice is Carol's grandmother - and the order matters, since a father's mother is not a mother's father; verifying a composed relation means closing the loop. We show that if each entity's coordinate frame may be rotated independently (per-entity frame freedom), three things follow. In the pure-gauge sector, relations that share no cycle cannot interact at all. The only gauge-invariant score of a triangle is a class function of its holonomy H = Tᵢⱼ Tⱼₖ Tₖᵢ - a Wilson loop. And the only equivariant update of an edge is U = Ψ(H), Tᵢⱼ with Ψ conjugation-equivariant. Edge attention by Wilson loops is therefore not one design among many but the unique form the symmetry permits. Three communities hold pieces of this form: the commuting-operator embeddings of knowledge graphs are its abelian (commuting) sector; AlphaFold's triangle update and the Edge Transformer have its shape - an edge updated through the third vertex - without its constraints; and lattice QCD builds it equivariantly on lattices. We instantiate the equivariant sub-family on general relational graphs as holonomy attention. With no training and composition alone, it infers unobserved S₄ relations on sparse graphs at 0.88 with a fifth of the edges corrupted, at or slightly below specialist synchronization algorithms, where every commutative architecture is capped at 0.083; its holonomy score flags corrupted triangles at AUC 0.99 where commuting scores are capped at 0.76 by a second selection rule, and it separates clusters without labels.

articles.title: Optimal quantum discrimination at Liouvillian exceptional points
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.37660v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Central to non-Hermitian sensing is the question of whether exceptional points (EPs) can make weak perturbations easier to detect. We show that despite enhanced spectral response, in finite-dimensional Lindblad systems with a unique stationary state and a nonzero relaxation gap, EPs offer no fundamental advantage in how the observation time required for reliable detection of a weak perturbation scales with the perturbation strength. We nevertheless demonstrate that by selectively choosing perturbations that enhance the quantum Fisher information rate, EPs can shorten the observation time needed to reach a predefined detection accuracy relative to a comparable non-EP reference at the same decay rate. As an illustration, we show using an optomechanical model at an EP that we can detect a weak force through the cavity output at the same reliability in less time than a non-EP reference. Our results establish fundamental limits on perturbation detection at EPs and can guide the design of faster non-Hermitian sensors based on optomechanical resonators, superconducting qubits, and trapped ions.

articles.title: Trivial topology-entailed states at interfaces between identical topological phases
articles.abstract: arXiv:2202.03252v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Topological edge states arise at boundaries between bulk phases with distinct topological invariants and are characterized by robust, often chiral transport. When two domains sharing identical bulk topology are brought into contact, their counterpropagating edge modes are generally expected to hybridize and cancel each other out in the process. Here, we show that this cancellation can be lifted by trivial parameter variations at the interface, giving rise to a distinct class of gap-localized inter-face modes, which we term trivial topology-entailed (TTE) states. Using anomalous Floquet photonic lattices as a concrete platform, we experimentally observe the formation of bidirectional TTE states between topologically equivalent domains. In particular, we demonstrate their spectral confinement within bulk gaps, their coherent coupling to conventional chiral edge channels, and their ability to mediate interface-guided transport across composite lattices. Our results establish TTE states as a general interface phenomenon in composite topological systems and provide a unified framework for understanding hybridized boundary modes beyond conventional bulk-boundary correspondence.

articles.title: A Kinetic Study of the Interactions of an Acoustic Vibrating Surface with Hypersonic Boundary-Layer Instabilities
articles.abstract: arXiv:2512.11390v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The response of Mack mode instabilities to a simple acoustic vibrating surface (AVS) is studied using the Direct Simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC) method to capture and analyze spontaneous second-mode instability growth. The DSMC simulations, analyzed with the Dynamic Mode Decomposition (DMD) method, model flow over a flat plate at an unseeded freestream Mach number of 6 and unit Reynolds number Re₁sim 1.18×10⁷ m⁻¹. Power spectral density (PSD) analysis was found to identify the dominant frequencies of 200 to 500 kHz, in line with linear stability theory (LST) predictions. Closed-form kinetic-theory expressions were derived to predict the amplitude of the DSMC fluctuations in the window-averaged snapshots. It was observed that the DSMC-simulated flowfield naturally developed second Mack mode instabilities without any external seeding, i.e., arising spontaneously from the kinetic fluctuations of the simulated gas and of amplitude higher than the predicted DSMC fluctuations. Targeted interaction with these flow instabilities is demonstrated for an AVS, where forcing at the unstable frequency of 250 kHz results in amplified waves downstream, while at the stable frequency of 400 kHz AVS-induced disturbances are damped. The AVS thus excites only the waves at its forcing frequency, leaving the instability waves at other frequencies and the mean flow essentially unaltered. The ability of the kinetic simulations to capture and describe linear perturbations at Reynolds numbers corresponding to those of Mach 6 flight at altitudes of sim 20 km suggests that DSMC provides a theoretical understanding of controlling laminar-turbulent transition through AVS materials in hypersonic boundary layers.

articles.title: h1: A Taste of the Bitter Lesson in Automated Theorem Proving
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35962v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: While progress in informal mathematics has come largely from scaling the chain-of-thought and agentic reasoning of frontier language models, formal theorem proving has increasingly relied on human-designed workflows around these models, such as planning, decomposition, and orchestrating specialized provers. This raises a bitter-lesson question: can a simple agentic loop that scales test-time compute match these workflows? The answer matters as formal verification must scale to keep up with frontier models producing research mathematics, yet new workflows rarely settle it, as their gains are often confounded with stronger models or more compute. We study this question with h1, a simple harness that gives a model an efficient interface to Lean 4 and keeps it working through verifier feedback and self-reflection, without imposing a decomposition or search structure. h1 reaches state-of-the-art results on PutnamBench, FATE-X, and FormalConjectures100-Solved, settles eight open problems in FormalConjectures, and, at matched models, matches or outperforms specialized workflows such as Goedel-Architect and AlphaProof Nexus, surprisingly showing that a single attempt (pass@1) can often scale to solve open problems. Through ablations and matched-model comparisons with Claude Code and AxProverBase, we find that simplicity alone is not enough: an efficient Lean interface largely determines cost and solve rate. We thus recommend that future work evaluate frontier models with efficient execution feedback before prescribing workflows, at the risk of bitter lessons.

articles.title: Log-Derivative Trick for Parametric Markov Chains
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.36655v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Optimizing expected rewards and reachability probabilities in parametric Markov chains (pMCs) is central to the analysis and synthesis of probabilistic systems with loops. While traditional symbolic synthesis approaches--such as parameter lifting and rational function generation--suffer from scalability bottlenecks, gradient-based optimization emerges as an effective alternative. However, existing gradient-based techniques still rely on symbolic gradient computation--such as solving large linear systems--over the global state space, inheriting scalability limits. Finite-horizon approximation is possible but introduces uncontrollable bias. In this paper, we introduce a scalable Monte Carlo gradient estimator based on a measure-theoretic generalization of the log-derivative trick. We prove that our estimator provides unbiased gradient estimates under almost-sure termination and standard regularity conditions. Crucially, our method avoids global state-space materialization and linear system solving entirely: it operates purely along sampled trajectories, requiring only black-box evaluations of local transition probabilities (or densities) and their derivatives. Unlike existing pMC techniques that are fundamentally restricted to finite discrete systems, our measure-theoretic framework naturally extends to continuous and general σ-finite state spaces. Empirical evaluations on synthetic discrete pMCs and continuous-state case studies demonstrate that our method scales to state spaces far beyond the reach of existing solvers, significantly reducing execution time without introducing bias.

articles.title: Robust LLM Data Selection via Content-Invariant Gradient Attribution
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.36755v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gradient-based data attribution has become an important tool for high-quality data selection in the instruction fine-tuning of large language models (LLMs), as it estimates the contribution of training examples through their influence on model optimization. However, we find that existing global gradient attribution methods suffer from surface-form bias: minor changes to semantically irrelevant details, such as wording or formatting, can produce highly inconsistent attribution scores even when the underlying content remains unchanged. To address this issue, we propose Content-Invariant Gradient Attribution (CIGA), a robust framework for instruction data selection. CIGA first identifies layers whose gradients are both influential for attribution and stable under semantics-preserving surface-form perturbations, thereby reducing formatting noise in gradient features. It then dynamically fuses these attribution signals with semantic representations of the input, combining optimization-level influence with content-level information. Extensive experiments across multiple benchmarks show that CIGA produces more stable rankings under surface-form perturbations while preserving downstream capabilities and improving average performance. CIGA also reduces attribution cost, offering a robust and efficient approach to data selection for LLM instruction tuning.

articles.title: ORBITAL: Optimization of Robust Brain--Computer Inference Through Architecture-Aware Low-Precision Compression
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.36411v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Compact electroencephalography (EEG) decoders enable embedded brain--computer interfaces (BCIs), but compression can alter adversarial robustness without proportional hardware savings. We present ORBITAL, a robustness-constrained framework combining hardware-realizable structured compression, recovery-aware operating-point selection, multi-attack evaluation, and native edge validation. Across nine subjects and three seeds on BCI Competition IV-2a, S25-TRADES achieves the highest observed mean true-union robustness among compressed EEGNet models (23.06% vs 21.27% for standard Full), with 26.27% fewer parameters and 25.10% fewer MACs. Matched controls identify TRADES as the main source of robustness recovery, improving S25 union accuracy by 6.74 percentage points over clean recovery (p=0.0039), while per-example analysis reveals boundary redistribution rather than uniform margin expansion. On Jetson Orin Nano, FP16 compression reduces board energy by up to 16.20% and latency by 8.00%. Despite 99.3% prediction agreement, native INT8 Q/DQ incurs about twice the FP16 latency and energy, demonstrating the need for joint robustness and hardware-aware optimization.

articles.title: Whole-Body Humanoid Control via Stochastic Motion Tokenization
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.36452v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: While velocity-commanded RL policies are effective for controlling quadrupeds, they are a limited interface for humanoids that need to perform complex whole-body motions. Furthermore, RL tracking policies for whole-body motions typically have limited information about the desired future motion, preventing them from performing controlled deviations to achieve long-term task success; such information is particularly relevant when a controller must prepare for transitions between behaviors. We address these challenges using concise motion representations that can be generated by a high-level controller, given a behavior label or text command. These representations can be fed directly into a tracking policy to provide a detailed motion reference. Our method exhibits a high degree of flexibility in performing real-world robot motions such as dancing, fighting, or walking based on conditional information. At matched capacity, our adopted stochastic motion tokenizer reconstructs motions from the Unitree G1 at a level that exceeds state-of-the-art approaches such as finite scalar quantization (FSQ) and the vector-quantized autoencoder (VQ-VAE). The resulting discrete interface conditions whole-body tracking policies that execute generated dance, fight, and walk motions lasting 16.8 s each and a 35 s fight-to-dance sequence on a physical Unitree G1.

articles.title: MAREval: A Multi-Agent Framework for Evaluating Natural Language Recommendation Explanations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.36389v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Evaluating natural language explanations in recommender systems is essential for fostering user trust, transparency, and engagement. However, existing evaluation approaches like human evaluations, while accurate, are resource-intensive and impractical at the scale required by modern recommendation platforms. Also, automated methods using single-agent LLMs suffer from prompt sensitivity and inconsistent outputs. To address these challenges, we propose MAREval, a structured multi-agent framework for evaluating recommendation explanations using large language models. MAREval orchestrates (i) a planner agent that uses a novel Chain of Debate (CoD) prompting strategy to coordinate agent roles and enforce logically consistent evaluation plans; (ii) a moderator agent that regulates discussions by mitigating prompt drift; and (iii) an arbitrator agent that aggregates outputs from multiple evaluation rounds and (iv) a Monte Carlo sampling method, improving robustness and alignment with human judgment. We conduct comprehensive evaluations on both public (TopicalChat) and proprietary recommendation datasets, demonstrating that MAREval outperforms state-of-the-art baselines. Comprehensive experiments on a public benchmark and a proprietary e-commerce dataset show that MAREval improves alignment with human judgments over strong singleand multi-agent baselines. Stability analyses indicate substantially lower variability across repeated trials. In a large human-annotation gate, MAREval meets production quality thresholds where prior evaluators fall short, and online A/B testing demonstrates statistically significant improvements in engagement and revenue metrics. These results establish MAREval as a scalable and reliable solution for human-aligned evaluation of recommendation explanations in real-world systems

articles.title: CogArena: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents on Interactive Behavioral Experiments
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.36484v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Claims about the cognitive capabilities of large language models are typically tested by translating behavioral paradigms into text prompts, bypassing the visual interfaces and time pressure through which human participants actually engage with experiments. At the same time, AI agents can now complete online behavioral tasks and produce human-like data, which raises concerns that online datasets in the social and behavioral sciences are increasingly open to contamination. We introduce CogArena, a benchmark of ten experimental paradigms from the social and behavioral sciences. Agents complete the experiments through a standard web browser, working with the same visual stimuli and response interfaces that online participants use. A three-level scoring procedure evaluates whether the agent completed the task, how accurately it performed, and whether its data show the behavioral signatures each paradigm reliably produces in people. Across four multimodal models, each run ten times per task, we find that finishing an experiment and reproducing its signatures are different things. Many sessions did not finish, and those that did reproduced some signatures reliably and others not at all. CogArena provides the tasks, scoring code, and a public leaderboard for new submissions.

articles.title: Concordat: Typed Sessions for LLM Agents
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.37461v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agents built on large language models are increasingly allowed to take consequential actions: cancelling bookings, issuing refunds, changing accounts. The rules that govern those actions, such as "obtain the customer's explicit confirmation before changing anything", are usually stated in the prompt and followed only as reliably as the model chooses to follow them. We present Concordat, a Python library that treats an agent as an object whose interface is a finite-state protocol, in the spirit of typestate and session types, and enforces that protocol on the model at run time. On every turn the model is offered only the tools that are legal in the current protocol state, calls outside that set are rejected before they have side effects, decisions reserved for humans can only be requested, and token and tool-call budgets are charged and split linearly across handoffs. Protocols are checked when they are defined, and a subclass of an agent is rejected if it could bypass its parent's protocol, a behavioural form of Liskov substitution. We evaluate a Concordat agent against the standard agent of tau-bench on its 50 airline tasks, adding simulated customers who pressure the agent to skip confirmation. The standard agent made changes without the required "yes" in 13 of 50 tasks with gpt-4.1 and in 29 of 128 task-runs with Claude Haiku 5.5; the Concordat agent made none, with no significant difference in task success. tau-bench's own reward did not detect most of these violations. Concordat is open source.

articles.title: scPyviewer: a Python-native interactive viewer from AnnData single-cell data
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35890v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Motivation: Interactive web tools enabling non-programmers to explore single-cell datasets, embeddings, gene expression, metadata, and marker genes are standard laboratory infrastructure. However, actively maintained tools (e.g., ShinyCell, ScRDAVis, sCIRCLE) rely on R Shiny and require Seurat objects. Python/scanpy, the dominant framework for single-cell RNA-seq and spatial analysis, lacks a lightweight, native option pairing a shareable viewer with a scriptable Python API. Sharing scanpy results currently requires converting to Seurat or sharing code notebooks. Results: We present scPyviewer, a web viewer that ingests AnnData objects directly and reproduces incumbent interaction patterns within the Python stack. In a feature-parity audit against three R Shiny tools, scPyviewer matches or exceeds baseline capabilities (7/7), uniquely offering native AnnData ingestion without conversion and cross-dataset comparison over shared genes and matched cell types. Benchmark tests across three datasets (22,315 to ~313,000 cells) show scPyviewer renders every core view faster (up to 3.6x speedup) using lower memory (5.2x lower on the smallest dataset). On 313,000 cells, scPyviewer completes all views while Seurat exhausts an 8 GB memory limit and fails. Beyond the app, scPyviewer exposes a Python API returning Matplotlib figures and pandas tables for publication-ready output. Availability and implementation: Implemented in Python 3.11 (scanpy 1.11.5, anndata 0.12.19, streamlit 1.59.2, plotly 6.9.0) with a one-command interface to reproduce benchmarks, figures, and launch the app. Source code: https://github.com/xuan13hao/scPyviewer.git

articles.title: SCOPE: Source Credibility and Outlet Profiling Engine
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35929v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present SCOPE, a multi-agent system for profiling news media outlets with respect to bias, factuality, and credibility. Given an outlet URL, SCOPE coordinates specialized agents for article acquisition, content analysis, external evidence search, scoring, and report generation. The system follows an MBFC-style methodology while making intermediate evidence and agent outputs inspectable through a structured demonstration interface. On a benchmark of 200 media outlets, SCOPE outperforms LLM-only, article-only, search-only, and media-background-check baselines on most metrics, achieving the lowest bias and factuality MAE, perfect failed-fact-check detection, and the lowest factual error rate. These results suggest that decomposed, evidence-grounded agent workflows can support more transparent and reliable media profiling. Our code is available at https://github.com/mbaisbay/SCOPE, and a live demonstration at https://scope-demo.streamlit.app/.

articles.title: Generation and Verification: Human-Agent Collaboration for Safety-Critical Automotive Software Engineering
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35982v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Research on coding agents mainly focuses on generation quality. Yet, safety-critical automotive software makes two additional demands. It prioritizes verification, since every change is reviewed, traced to a requirement, and checked against industry standards such as MISRA and AUTOSAR before it can be committed. It is also a narrow domain, written against layered architectures, embedded resource constraints, and organization-specific interface conventions that are scarce in the data general-purpose LLMs are trained on. We present a coding assistant for automotive C/C++ that addresses both demands. First, it exposes three tools to the user over the Model Context Protocol (generate, edit, and verify), allowing developers to run verify on any code on demand rather than relying on the agent to check its own output. Second, rather than using a general-purpose model, we customize the underlying LLM for the automotive domain through prompt engineering and fine-tuning. We construct a dataset from automotive production code of AUMOVIO, where each function is paired with the requirement texts and Unified Modeling Language (UML) behavior it must satisfy. In a two-week pilot on active production projects, developers report verify as the most-used tool and confirm using it on their own code and not only on generated output. Comparing model customization strategies, 75% prefer the faster prompt-engineered configuration. MISRA- and AUTOSAR-inspired pattern checkers indicate that prompt engineering achieves a lower number of violations on C, while fine-tuning shows better conformance with architecture patterns for C++.

articles.title: Log-To-Leak: Prompt Injection Attacks on Tool-Using LLM Agents via the Model Context Protocol
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.36108v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: LLM agents increasingly access external tools through the Model Context Protocol (MCP), but the natural-language metadata used to describe those tools creates a prompt-injection surface. Within this established tool-poisoning surface, we study Log-To-Leak, an additive post-hoc logging attack that induces a separate attacker-controlled call after the final legitimate call. Its payload targets the user query, MCP server name, server response, and agent response. We operationalize the injected directive through Trigger, Tool Binding, Justification, and Pressure, and separately measure call success, payload fidelity, and preservation of legitimate behavior. We evaluate five MCP servers and four LLM agents using five metrics spanning effectiveness, utility, and efficiency. Across 18 model-server pairs with valid tool execution, Log-To-Leak achieves an attack success rate (ASR) of 62.64-100% and conditional logging accuracy (LA) of 76.55-95.64%; 16 pairs have absolute target-task completion changes of at most 6.63 percentage points. Three evaluated defenses leave residual ASR above 55% on GitHub MCP with GPT-4o, while an instruction detector flags 85.53% of benign descriptions. These results show that successful task completion can coexist with unauthorized post-hoc disclosure and motivate host-controlled authorization for secondary tool calls.

articles.title: Replication or Corroboration? An Axiomatic Framework for Evidential Dependence in Multi-Agent Debate
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.36151v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In multi-agent debates, matching reports can arise for two different reasons: agents may repeat the same evidence (replication), or they may provide separate evidential roots that support the same claim (corroboration). A judge must distinguish these two cases. Counting report occurrences gives extra weight to relays, paraphrases, alias resubmissions, and excerpt splits, while merging all matching content avoids this only by also removing genuine corroboration. We formalize this tension as a minimal judgment game in which acquiring new evidence is costly, but replication is cheap. We show that root replication invariance (RRI) is exactly threshold-uniform replication immunity. Under RRI, replication-only deviations cannot change the verdict, and positive-cost replication is strictly dominated, whereas occurrence-sensitive and content-keyed judges admit profitable deviations. We also establish an information boundary: if a judge's observation interface cannot distinguish a replica from a matched fresh root, no judge can both ignore the replica and respond strictly to the fresh root. To preserve this distinction, we introduce the lineage quotient, which removes wording, identity, occurrence multiplicity, and arbitrary root names while keeping distinct roots separate. On orbit-connected domains, it is the coarsest representation sufficient for every deterministic judge invariant to replication and root-label renaming. We further lift this construction to quantitative bipolar argumentation frameworks (QBAFs), characterize strict fresh-root response, prove its propagation along sign-consistent paths under DF-QuAD, and derive a tight closed-form response modulus. Exhaustive audits over 28,224 direct-star profiles, 2,052 multi-layer DAGs, with matched interventions on 277 AVeriTeC-derived profiles, show the predicted separation between replication and corroboration under a supplied partition.

articles.title: Making Self-Driving Laboratories Auditable:A Unified Framework for Hybrid Actions,Measurements, and Safe Execution
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.36761v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Self-driving laboratories (SDLs) are laboratory systems that couple experimental planning, automated execution, and measurement feedback in a closed loop. Integrating flexible robot control with the typed application programming interfaces (APIs) and continuous measurements exposed by laboratory instruments remains an execution-interface challenge. To address this challenge, we propose a traceable framework comprising four components: LAM (Lab Action Model), OpenSDL, Safe-SDL, and L3-Bench. LAM is a proposed measurement-conditioned policy architecture that extends vision-language-action paradigms to generate both continuous robot trajectories and typed instrument API calls. OpenSDL is an execution substrate with an initial control implementation, designed to map role-level operations to heterogeneous devices, coordinate execution, and record timestamped causal events. The proposed Safe-SDL runtime gate combines pre-dispatch schema and resource checks with signal temporal logic monitoring during execution, including extended waiting periods. L3-Bench (Level-3 Laboratory Benchmark) specifies an episode-level evaluation protocol covering physical outcomes, timing, reproducibility, safety violations, and fault recovery. Together, these components provide an end-to-end design for linking hybrid action generation, monitored device execution, measurement feedback, and experimental evaluation, addressing coordination and traceability challenges in SDL workflows.

articles.title: Exploring Hub Dam: An Extensive Analysis of Reservoir Patterns
articles.abstract: Hub Dam is an earth-fill reservoir was established on the Hub River at the Sindh-Balochistan provincial border, 56 km northeast of Karachi, represents one of the most Systematically crucial water infrastructure assets in Pakistan. Designed with a gross storage capacity of 857,000 acre-feet across a 24,300-acre reservoir, the dam serves as the primary drinking water source for Karachi — Pakistan's most populous city — and supports irrigation in the Lasbela district of Balochistan. This study presents a comprehensive analysis of Hub Dam's Physical and hydrological characteristics, temporal flood-drought dynamics from 1983 to 2022, and evidence-based management recommendations. Satellite imagery and GIS-based reservoir mapping indicate that water surface area Shifted dramatically between a minimum of 13.65 km² during the severe drought of 2000, when storage dropped to dead storage level, and a maximum of 69.47 km² during the large flood year of 2007. Five distinct drought periods were identified (1983–1989, 1989–1994, 1995–2003, 2003–2007, and 2007–2020), with the 2007–2018 period constituting the longest recorded drought in the dam's operational history. A strong positive correlation between annual rainfall in Karachi and reservoir water surface area confirms the dam's direct dependence on monsoonal precipitation patterns. The study concludes with 3 Practical management recommendations including additional dam construction, rainwater harvesting, watershed management planning, floodplain management, and public awareness programs to enhance water security for Karachi and surrounding regions.

articles.title: Eddy momentum-forcing redistribution accompanies an equatorward Southern Hemisphere jet response to Antarctic sea-ice–SST boundary perturbations
articles.abstract: Antarctic sea-ice changes modify Southern Ocean lower-boundary conditions, yet the relation between eddy momentum deposition and jet displacement remains poorly constrained in within-model large ensembles. We analyze independent atmosphere-only Polar Amplification Model Intercomparison Project (PAMIP) ensembles from HadGEM3-GC31-MM and IPSL-CM6A-LR, each containing 100 present-day control and 100 treatment members under future Antarctic sea-ice boundary conditions (400 members total). Because the treatment changes sea ice together with prescribed sea surface temperature (SST) where ice retreats, it estimates a combined sea-ice–SST boundary response rather than a sea-ice-only effect. In the two-model equal-weight synthesis, 2–8-day poleward eddy heat flux decreases by 0.123 K m s⁻¹ (95% interval − 0.187 to − 0.059 K m s⁻¹; −0.380 control standard deviation [SD]). Seasonal-departure 250-hPa eddy momentum-flux convergence forms a meridional dipole, with enhanced deposition near 45–49°S and reduced deposition near 55–60°S; the dipole increases by 0.159 m s⁻¹ day⁻¹ (0.060–0.259; +0.325 SD). The perturbation is accompanied by a negative Southern Annular Mode (SAM)-like response (− 0.254 SD) and a 0.447° equatorward jet shift (0.124–0.766°), while peak jet speed changes by only + 0.029 m s⁻¹ (− 0.156 to + 0.211). No latitude in the strict 2–8-day momentum-forcing profile passes false-discovery-rate correction, so evidence for redistribution is strongest for seasonal departures rather than for a fully resolved weather-scale mediation pathway. Momentum forcing, the SAM-like state, and jet latitude covary consistently across the four model–experiment ensembles. The response is therefore better characterized as co-occurring meridional redistribution of eddy momentum deposition and jet position than as uniform weakening of the Southern Hemisphere westerlies.

articles.title: Biases in subtropical low clouds traced to weak sensitivity to surface winds
articles.abstract: Models are known to systematically misrepresent cloud properties over many regions of the globe, with substantial impacts on the energy balance of the climate system. We investigate the causes of model biases in cloud albedo over tropical and subtropical stratocumulus regions using a cloud-controlling factor (CCF) method at daily timescale. We assess the performance of a 15-model CMIP6 ensemble by comparing with cloud albedo computed from CERES satellite retrievals of upwelling and downwelling shortwave radiation at the surface and top of the atmosphere and CCFs obtained from the ERA5 reanalysis. We find large negative biases in three of the major stratocumulus decks over oceans (the Californian, Peruvian and Namibian regions). However, in other areas cloud albedo errors are very small (Australian and Canarian regions). The CCF analysis shows that in all five regions observed cloud albedo robustly increases with increasing surface winds speed, in agreement with theoretical as well as Large Eddy Simulation studies. By contrast, CMIP6 simulated clouds show either small or negative sensitivity to strengthening winds. We also find that the two regions with reduced cloud albedo biases arise as error compensations of different types: excessive cloud albedo associated with ascending motion regimes (Australian), and excessive cloud albedo under weak winds (Canarian).

articles.title: Homotopy surrogate model assisted double-loop approach for efficient structural reliability-based design optimization
articles.abstract: The double-loop approach for structural reliability-based design optimization (RBDO) often incurs high computational costs because reliability analysis in the inner loop typically requires numerous finite element analyses (FEAs) or experiments. As a solution, this paper develops a double-loop approach for RBDO by using the stochastic static homotopy surrogate model (SHSM). In the inner loop, the SHSM is combined with Monte Carlo simulation for reliability analysis of candidate designs. The SHSM model is established through the stochastic homotopy method, which is intrusive and does not depend on training samples. In the outer loop, the parallel harmony search (PHS) algorithm is used to optimize the design variables. To further reduce optimization costs by reusing historical optimization information, this study proposes a SHSM reusable strategy. When the reusable criterion established is satisfied, a number of SHSMs are reused for the reliability analysis of subsequent new candidate designs, thereby efficiently utilizing the established SHSMs. The optimization results for a highly nonlinear benchmark problem, two truss structures and a wing box structure show that the new method achieves similar optimization results while substantially reducing the computational cost than the existing methods including reliability index approach (RIA), performance measure approach (PMA), three Kriging-based methods and so on.

articles.title: First principles investigation of water adsorption, dopant segregation and surface thermodynamics of Mg and Sr substituted CaO(001) for Ca(OH)2/CaO thermochemical energy storage
articles.abstract: The Ca(OH)₂/CaO cycle releases stored heat when CaO takes up water, an uptake that begins at the oxide surface. Isovalent Mg and Sr barely move the bulk equilibrium of the cycle, but their surface effect is unknown. We study water at 1/4 monolayer on CaO(001) with Mg, Sr or both in the top layer, or Mg in the second layer, by density functional theory. On every surface the most stable state we found is split: a hydroxyl bridges two cations and the proton sits on a neighbouring surface oxygen. Water binds by 0.84 eV on CaO, 0.98 eV with Sr, 1.17 eV with Mg, 1.18 eV with both and 0.81 eV with Mg below the surface. Mg acts through the oxygen that takes the proton, Sr through the site of the hydroxyl, and their gains do not add. The stretching frequency of the new surface hydroxyl tracks the binding energy (r = -0.96). On the clean surface Sr prefers the top layer by 0.46 eV and Mg the second layer by 0.29 eV. Adsorbed water reverses the choice of Mg, but in equilibrium with the vapour only below 530 to 790 K at 1 bar. Relative to CaO, surface Sr raises the water desorption temperature by 65 to 105 K and surface Mg by 190 to 250 K, while the same ions move the bulk equilibrium temperature by only -5 to +25 K. Surface doping, most reliably with Sr, thus tunes water uptake almost independently of the storage temperature.

articles.title: Tomography-free quantum diagnostics of dissipative quantum chaos
articles.abstract: Non-Hermitian generators encode both complex spectra and non-orthogonal eigenvectors, but strong non-normality alone does not distinguish chaotic from integrable dynamics. We study the propagator-norm form factor Φ(t;θ)=D⁻¹lVert e^teⁱθLrVert_F² and its excess over a baseline determined only by eigenvalues. A trace expansion relates the short-time excess to Henrici's departure from normality. In the large-dimension limit, we derive the Ginibre curve X/Φ₀=tI₀(2t)/I₁(2t)-1 and an elliptic-family extension with asymptotically linear growth. A planar-order approximation connects the latter to finite-size non-Hermitian Sachdev--Ye--Kitaev models. Classical numerical benchmarks show that profile shape complements excess magnitude in distinguishing selected chaotic and integrable ensembles. A separately calibrated zero-angle rule gives 38 correct assignments and seven abstentions on 45 fresh instances, with no wrong-class assignments within the tested scope. Structured locally dissipative chains expose a limitation: spectral-spacing signatures can separate while the profile slopes do not. We relate Φ to the normalized acceptance probability of a block-encoded propagator and, for physical channels at θ=0, to Choi-state purity. These identities provide tomography-free measurement routes for Φ; classification additionally requires an accurate spectral baseline. We distinguish the analytic results and classical sampling tests from the unimplemented gate-level synthesis and unresolved large-system baseline reconstruction. The resulting framework connects non-normal dynamics, random-matrix theory and quantum measurement without identifying non-normality with chaos.

articles.title: Quantum state reconstruction from incomplete preparation records
articles.abstract: Preparing additional quantum states while retaining a source requires information beyond an arbitrary unknown input. We formulate reconstruction from incom- plete classical preparation records as an identity channel on the source and two output preparations. For a short interval of QPE phase states, we derive the exact record-only minimax fidelity and an attaining endpoint superposition, closing the gap between center replay and an endpoint upper bound. An explicit one-ancilla circuit realizes the optimum with a known success probability, while deterministic synthesis provides a finite-circuit alternative. Shor and randomized-simulation examples expose different obstructions from discrete ambiguity and missing ran- dom choices. In one randomized-simulation setting, optimal conditional fidelity averaged over records was 0.925, although robust fidelity above five sixths was impossible for eight of ten records. Session calibration and resource-controlled comparisons distinguish average performance from worst-case guarantees. Hard- ware diagnostics test operational phase models, source waiting and preparation costs. They do not certify intrinsic gate angles, reconstruction fidelity or physical source preservation. The analysis identifies information and operational conditions without changing universal cloning bounds.

articles.title: Numerical Design and Three-Dimensional Finite Element Analysis of a Conventional RCC Beam and a Timber-Core Composite RCC Beam
articles.abstract: Reducing the dead load and cement consumption of reinforced concrete (RCC) members is an important step towards lower-carbon construction, and lightly stressed zones near the neutral axis offer an obvious opportunity. This paper investigates a timber-core composite RCC beam in which a central 100 × 150 mm Sal-timber core replaces part of the concrete in a 230 × 300 × 1000 mm beam, and compares it with an otherwise identical conventional RCC beam. Both beams (M30 concrete, Fe500 steel, 2–12ϕ bottom and 2–10ϕ top bars, 8 mm stirrups at 150 mm c/c, fixed–fixed supports) were designed to IS 456:2000 by the limit state method and analysed under a service uniformly distributed load of 80 kN/m plus self-weight using a dedicated three-dimensional linear-elastic finite element (FE) model with 8-node brick and embedded truss elements (14,976 bricks, 51,357 degrees of freedom). The FE model satisfies global equilibrium (error < 0.001%), is mesh-converged to better than 1%, and reproduces the analytical Timoshenko-beam deflection within 3.1%. The timber core reduces self-weight by 14.0% and concrete volume by 20.7% while leaving the flexural capacity unchanged (24.04 kN·m sagging, 17.11 kN·m hogging). The cost is a 13.2% larger mid-span deflection (28.8 → 32.6 µm), an 8.3% higher peak concrete tensile stress, a 2.8% lower cracking load and a 6.3% lower (conservative) shear capacity. Per unit self-weight, flexural rigidity, flexural capacity and shear capacity improve by 13.1%, 16.3% and 9.0%, respectively. The results show that a timber core placed in the neutral-axis zone is a structurally acceptable means of lightening lightly stressed RCC beams.

articles.title: Stacked electrohydrodynamic pumps with densely perforated electrodes
articles.abstract: While electrohydrodynamic (EHD) pumps are attractive for soft robotics owing to their simple, solid-state architecture, improving their performance remains a significant challenge. This study introduces a stackable pump featuring EHD layers with densely perforated electrodes integrated into a double-sided clad structure. The high hole density and integrated architecture enable enhanced electrohydrodynamic force generation while maintaining a lightweight structure. A systematic investigation of how the number of EHD layers, hole diameter, and porosity influence performance provides clear design guidelines and reveals that stacking increases both flow rate and pressure, with the pressure increasing almost linearly. Among the tested pumps, the maximum flow rate and pressure achieved are 2041.0 mL/min and 9.3 kPa, respectively. A five-layer pump weighing 0.64 g achieves the maximum power density, 55.0 W/kg (125.9 W/kg considering only the EHD layers), which represents a more-than-90-fold improvement over existing EHD pumps of similar type. Furthermore, the proposed pump successfully drives multiple soft actuators and a gripper, demonstrating its versatility and applicability to soft robotic systems.

articles.title: Microalloying-enabled hierarchical reconstruction of Bi-phase for strain resilience improvement and high strength-ductility synergy of Sn–Bi solder alloys
articles.abstract: In this work, we report a trace Cr/V microalloying strategy that reconstructs the Bi-rich constituent in Sn–Bi solder alloys, achieving a total elongation of 61.64% and an ultimate tensile strength of 79.64 MPa, representing increases of 72.26% and 26.00%, respectively, over the unmodified alloy. The addition of alloying elements alters the interfacial thermodynamics and diffusion kinetics of the Sn-Bi system, thereby changing the solidification pathway, refining the eutectic structure at the mesoscopic scale, and introducing microscale substructures such as abundant dislocation walls, low-angle grain boundaries, and twins, as well as nanoscale Sn-rich regions, within the Bi-rich phase. These hierarchical structural features change the role of the Bi-rich phase during deformation. The reconstructed Bi-rich constituent no longer serves as a weak region for rapid crack propagation, but instead accommodates strain resilience through more dispersed and constrained microcrack activity. This, in turn, improves the deformation compatibility between the Sn-rich and Bi-rich phases. Multiscale calculations further show that the refined microstructure and distributed microcracking alleviate local stress concentration and delay the rapid development of macroscopic cracks. This work reveals a new mechanism about the brittle Bi-rich phase participates in deformation and damage evolution in Sn–Bi eutectic solder alloy, and provides a general design strategy for improving the mechanical reliability of eutectic alloys through internal structural modification of intrinsic brittle phases.

articles.title: Structural ,Chemical , and Dielectric Properties of "Sol-Gel" Auto-Combustion Synthesized Mn-Substituted ZnFe2O4 Nanoparticles
articles.abstract: Mn-substituted zinc ferrite nanoparticles with the nominal composition Zn1+xMnxFe2-2xO4(where x =0.0–0.5) were synthesized by the sol-gel auto combustion method to investigate the correlation between their structural, chemical , and dielectric properties . The crystal structural and phase formation were investigated using x-ray diffraction(XRD),while fourier- transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) was employed to examine the characteristics metal-oxygen vibrations associated with the tetrahedral and octahedral sites of the spinel lattice. Atomic absorption spectroscopy (AAS) was used to determine the experimental concentrations of Zn , Mn ,and Fe and to evaluate deviations from the nominal chemical composition .the   dielectric response was investigated as a function of  frequency and temperature through the real part  of  the dielectric permittivity (e') , the imaginary part (ε''), and the dielectric loss  tangent (tanδ) . The XRD patterns confirmed the formation of a cubic spinel structure without detectable secondary crystalline phases, while the crystallite size and lattice parameters exhibited composition-dependent variations with Mn substitution. The FTIR spectra revealed two characteristic metal-oxygen vibration bands, confirming the preservation of the spinel framework and indicating changes in the local cationic environment AAS results demonstrated a systematic increase in the experimentally measured Mn concentration with increasing substitution level, accompanied by deviation s in the Zn and Fe contents from their nominal values. The dielectric response exhibited pronounced dependence on frequency and temperature, and Mn concentration, which is attributed to changes in cation distribution, charge–carrier hopping, and interfacial polarization .The combined structural , chemical , and dielectric results demonstrate that Mn substitution provides an effective route for tuning the electrical response of ZnFe2O4 ,based ferrites while preserving their fundament al spinel structure

articles.title: Atomic-scale dynamics of water-triggered pathway-selective phase evolution in perovskite nanocrystals
articles.abstract: All-inorganic perovskites, a representative class of water-sensitive materials, offer excellent thermal stability and photostability, marking them promising for tandem photovoltaics. Nevertheless, water-induced degradation constrains their performance, stability, and commercialization. Atomic-scale understanding of degradation pathways in perovskites has been elusive, largely due to technical challenge of synchronizing water exposure with real-time visualization. We employ liquid-cell transmission electron microscopy with a newly designed double-layer strategy to directly visualize water-induced degradation of CsPbBr3 nanocrystals at atomic-scale. Two kinetic regimes emerge: high water content triggers irreversible transformation to non-perovskite-structure CsPb2Br5 with subsequent crystalline–amorphous oscillations; trace water induces a reversible cyclic pathway between CsPbBr3 and CsPb2Br5 with involvement of intermediate molten phase (MP). Transformation frequency is size-dependent: smaller nanocrystals exhibit the higher rate, due to facile MP formation and effective erasure of accumulated defects.
