For finite depth we calculate bulk dissipation using a phase- and depth-resolved quadrature Jₙ(kh) and formulate a separate oscillatory power--law bottom layer. We solve the latter numerically in periodic state, obtaining dimensionless integrated wall losses I₀.₆simeq0.5432 and I₁.₄simeq0.4708 and recovering the exact Newtonian benchmark I₁=1/2. These values make it possible to evaluate conditional finite-depth bulk--wall dominance boundaries rather than only their amplitude exponents. The theory is organized into restoring-force, attenuation, local propagation-length, and dissipation-mechanism regime maps; at fixed wave steepness it additionally predicts a capillary-side maximum of normalized temporal damping for 0<2/3. Grid, time-step, domain, and energy-work checks support the reduced wall calculation, while the coupled bulk--wall approximation still requires independent free-surface numerical or experimental validation. The results provide a reproducible single-fluid reference for subsequent two-liquid interfacial-wave modeling.

articles.title: Is the arXiv Apocalypse upon us? A break in preprint growth coincident with agentic AI
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.34449v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As an experiment in agentic assisted analysis, we used an agentic AI model to analyse the effect of agentic AI on arXiv submissions; data acquisition, analysis and the first draft were carried out by the model under the author's direction. Monthly arXiv submissions have grown exponentially for three decades, at about 9% per year. Fitting a piecewise log-linear trend with seasonal modulation to the full record, we find two post-pandemic breaks in growth rate. The first, in mid-2022, precedes ChatGPT and is carried by the expansion of AI research within computer science (CS); outside CS, growth from 2022 to 2025 remained at 8% per year. The second, between December 2025 and February 2026, follows the release of models capable of extended autonomous work and is absent from the AI categories themselves. Since December 2025 submissions without a CS listing have run 17% above trend, and in September 2026 total submissions reached a record 40,363. The excess is largest in mathematics, where submissions doubled within a year, and follows a gradient from formal and theoretical fields to experimental ones that is not ordered by surveyed rates of AI-tool adoption. In mathematics the increase is distributed across subfields and authors, two-thirds of it arising from a larger number of distinct authors rather than from a few prolific submitters. Across fields the clearest signature is a shift to single authorship: solo-authored papers rose by 70% within a year in mathematics and condensed matter, and by 44% in quantitative biology even as its total output fell, but not in experimental particle physics. The analysis is deliberately agnostic of LLM-detection methods: it uses only submission counts and metadata, with treatment timing fixed by calendar dates, and is therefore free of the outcome-triggered timing bias of author-level studies.

articles.title: Why Emission Spectral Profile of Diverse Fluoro-phores Look Alike with Thick Polymer Overlayers?
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.34864v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fluorescence from fluorophore-polymer overlayers reflects an interplay between molecular photo-physics and thickness dependent optical propagation. Combining spectrally resolved single mole-cule measurements, transition dipole moment orientation analysis and ensemble fluorescence, we show that structurally and photophysically distinct fluorophores can exhibit similar red shifted emission profiles under thick polymer overlayers even without additional reflecting surface. This similarity indicates a common optical transfer function imposed by the overlayer rather than a pure-ly fluorophore specific molecular response. Although local molecular interactions, excited state dy-namics and vibronic coupling govern intrinsic emission, the overlayer modifies detected spectra through refractive index contrast, dielectric boundary reflections, cavity effects and collection ge-ometry. Vibronic energy spacing distributions remain largely preserved as thickness changes, whereas spectral positions and relative intensities vary systematically. Thus, polymer thickness pri-marily reshapes detected spectrum through optical propagation and outcoupling while retaining vi-brational modes. Time dependent density functional theory identifies candidate Franck-Condon and Herzberg-Teller active dye modes contributing to spectral fluctuations and dipole reorientation.

articles.title: Preparing State-Selected Molecular Beams with high Efficiency using Quantum Cascade Lasers
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.34948v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We demonstrate the ro-vibrational state-selective preparation of CO molecules (v = 0, J = 0 → v = 1, J = 1) in an internally cold molecular beam using a continuous-wave, narrow-linewidth distributed feedback type quantum cascade laser, with an output wavelength of 4.65 μm. Using a modulation-free wavelength stabilization scheme, we show that population transfer to near saturation levels can be obtained with sufficient long term stability, as needed for state-resolved scattering experiments. We show preliminary results of CO molecules prepared in the v = 1 state, scattering from a clean Cu(100) surface. This study showcases the promise of QCL based excitation for state-selected molecular beam based scattering experiments, especially involving transitions in the mid-infrared domain (λ > 4.5 μm) which are otherwise difficult to access using conventional sources.

articles.title: Instability of exact finite-amplitude acoustic-gravity waves
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35210v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Godin (J. Fluid Mech., vol. 767, 2015, pp. 52--64) showed that compressible fluids in a uniform gravity field support finite-amplitude incompressible wave motions, in which every parcel conserves pressure and density, and constructed exact Gerstner-type surface and edge waves, possibly carried by currents. Using the short-wavelength instability method for compressible flows, we show that these waves are linearly unstable above a critical steepness. The stability of each fluid level reduces to a Floquet problem depending on two parameters: the steepness mathfrake=eka₂ and ν²=(1-mathfrake²)ν₀², where ν₀²=cos²α,N₀²/Ω², N₀ is the buoyancy frequency of the hydrostatic reference state, α the inclination of the plane of motion and Ω=(gkcosα)¹/² the intrinsic orbital frequency. In an isentropic fluid, a level is unstable if mathfrake>1/3, recovering Leblanc's threshold for Gerstner waves (J. Fluid Mech., vol. 506, 2004, pp. 245--254) and extending it to compressible surface and edge waves; weak stable stratification lowers the threshold to frac13-frac3281ν₀²+O(ν₀⁴). In an isothermal atmosphere, ν₀²=κcosα/(kH), where H is the pressure scale height. For horizontal wavelengths near 5.5,H/cosα, principal subharmonic resonance makes the critical steepness vanish. For the fast airglow wave observed by Hecht et al. (J. Geophys. Res., vol. 107, 2002, D20, 4444), which Godin interpreted with his solution, the lidar temperature places the layer in which this interpretation is consistent on this resonance, where the critical steepness is typically 0.1 instead of 1/3. Instability is confined to a layer beneath the free surface of surface waves and to a wedge at the shoreline of edge waves.

articles.title: Effects of Pulse Duration on Kerr Self-Focusing and Weld Formation in Ultrafast Laser Welding of Fused Silica
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35250v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Kerr self-focusing can shift the laser interaction region away from the geometrical focus, making energy deposition near the joining interface difficult to control. Here, the effect of pulse duration on nonlinear focusing and weld formation is investigated from 262 fs to 10 ps. ICCD imaging shows clear changes in the axial position and shape of the plasma emission. Different pulse durations already produce distinct axial positions during the initial 2000 pulses, and these positions continue to evolve with pulse accumulation. The final weld morphology, weld position, and shear strength show corresponding changes. A ray-optics model including the Kerr effect is used to calculate the focal shift. The simulated trend agrees with the experiment and supports the role of Kerr self-focusing in the observed focal position change. These results clarify the relationship between pulse duration, nonlinear focusing, interaction position, and weld formation.

articles.title: Bistability of ice-shelf cavity circulation and melt under coastal polynya forcing
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35359v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Antarctic ice shelves play a key role in controlling the mass loss of the Antarctic Ice Sheet. Increasing evidence from regional studies suggests the possibility of abrupt transitions from low to high basal melt regimes under future climate forcing. The computational cost and complexity of these realistic simulations yet limit their ability to systematically investigate the steady-state response of ice shelves to incremental forcing, the reversibility of abrupt transitions and the underlying positive feedback loops. Here, we report a detailed analysis of abrupt regime changes in an ice-shelf cavity with idealized geometry, subject to prescribed temperature and salinity stratifications in the far field and near-ice-front surface salt fluxes representing the impact of sea-ice production in coastal polynyas. We show that a cold regime emerges when the buoyancy loss in the polynya is sufficient to trigger deep convection, while a warm regime develops otherwise. The steady response of the system exhibits hysteresis, characteristic of irreversible transitions, and scaling laws are proposed for both melt rates and transition thresholds. We demonstrate that bistability emerges when a gyre recirculates the meltwater within the ice-shelf front area. The bistable forcing range increases with far-field ocean temperature but decreases with background stratification. We also show that increasing horizontal viscosity limits bistability, which may explain the range of behaviors reported in previous studies.

articles.title: HarP: a simulation tool for high-order harmonic generation and propagation in gases
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35440v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurately simulating high-order harmonic generation (HHG) for attosecond science requires connecting the microscopic single-atom quantum dynamics and the macroscopic propagation of intense driving laser fields. HarP is an open-source Python code designed to address this multiscale problem. It solves the wave equations for both the driving laser field and the generated harmonics, using precomputed dipole tables for the nonlinear polarization density. This tabulation enables the direct integration of accurate microscopic models while avoiding costly calculations during the propagation. The methodology builds upon the approach of [L'Huillier et al. (1992) PRA 46, 2778] and has already facilitated multiple studies on phase matching, propagation effects and HHG optimization. This paper presents the underlying physical model, its numerical implementation, and comparison against alternative simulation frameworks.

articles.title: Thermosolutal Marangoni instabilities in a weakly viscoelastic falling film with soluble surfactant
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35481v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We examine the linear stability and nonlinear evolution of a heated falling film containing a soluble surfactant and a weakly viscoelastic liquid. The stress response is described by the short-memory Walters model, while surface tension depends on temperature and surface concentration. An Orr--Sommerfeld analysis and its long-wave limit determine how elastic memory and the two Marangoni stresses enter the instability threshold. A five-field weighted-residual model is then derived to describe finite-amplitude disturbances. The bulk and surface transport equations are written with compatible fluxes, which conserve their combined projected surfactant inventory in a periodic domain. The numerical examples show that solutal Marangoni stress suppresses disturbance growth and reduces the amplitude of the nonlinear waves. Thermal Marangoni stress increases the maximum growth rate, although its effect on the width of the unstable wavenumber band is different. Elastic memory changes both the onset and the finite-wavelength response. The nonlinear profiles develop a main hump and capillary ripples, accompanied by variations in bulk concentration, surface concentration, and interfacial temperature. These results describe the competition between thermocapillary forcing, surfactant redistribution and elastic stress within the retained long-wave model. The larger elastic parameters are interpreted as formal predictions of the truncated constitutive equations, rather than as a controlled extension to strongly elastic flow.

articles.title: Transverse detuned loading for modulation bandwidth enhancement in VCSELs
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35578v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Directly modulated vertical-cavity surface-emitting lasers (VCSELs) are central to short-reach optical interconnects, where modulation bandwidth and power efficiency are critical factors for increasing data transfer capacity. Conventional oxide VCSELs still require power-hungry signal processing to achieve high-speed data transmission above 100 Gb/s. Here we report an experimental implementation of detuned loading in a VCSEL to enhance the modulation bandwidth. The detuned loading is achieved by carrier-induced index variations that reshape an engineered transverse mode so its overlap with spatially selective optical losses decreases with increased carrier density. This produces a negative differential loss reminiscent of that in detuned-loaded DBR lasers lasing on the long-wavelength reflectivity flank. The resulting 850 nm single-mode VCSEL exhibits an enhanced carrier-photon relaxation frequency of 44 GHz, yielding a 3dB electrical modulation bandwidth exceeding 50 GHz. The enhancement persists from 25 degC to 75 degC showing the robustness of the mechanism introduced. The same device supports 106.25 Gb/s NRZ transmission without digital signal processing, transmitter pre-emphasis or receiver equalization. These results establish transverse detuned loading as a robust alternative approach for extending the modulation bandwidth of vertical-cavity surface-emitting lasers.

articles.title: Chirpons: elementary local phase oscillations associated with complex zeros
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35599v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a complex wave, the local phase variation provides the instantaneous frequency in time, the local wavenumber in space, and the local momentum in quantum mechanics. Here we study this quantity from the complex-zero structure of the analytic continuation of the wave. A single nonreal zero produces a localized Lorentzian phase variation on the real axis, whose position, width, sign, amplitude, and integrated phase are fixed by the zero itself. We call this elementary zero-associated oscillation a chirpon. The representation is exact for finite products and finite Fourier sums, and extends to entire and band-limited functions through canonical factorization. We illustrate the construction with superoscillatory sequences and discrete Fourier sums, showing how local anomalous oscillations can be reconstructed from periodic families of complex zeros. We further show how linear systems transform chirpons through the displacement of their associated complex zeros, and illustrate this dynamics for quadratic dispersive propagation and a resonant harmonic oscillator. This establishes a direct relation between local phase structure and the amplitude and phase response of the transfer function, suggesting a zero-based form of spectroscopy in which system parameters can be inferred from the motion, width, and orientation of chirpons. More broadly, the chirpon description provides a unified framework for instantaneous frequency, local wavenumber, superoscillation, backflow, and other local phase phenomena, while offering a new route for probing linear systems through the dynamics of their complex zeros.

articles.title: Critical velocity and dissipation mechanism in finite superfluid ⁴He nanodroplets
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35728v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A hallmark of superfluidity is the frictionless motion of an object below the Landau critical velocity; Whether this concept applies to nanoscale droplets remains unclear. Using time-dependent density functional theory, we investigate the motion of a sodium atom on the surface and inside a superfluid helium nanodroplet. For surface motion, we identify a critical velocity above which energy dissipation through ripplon excitation and the formation of surface-bound quantized vortices leads to rapid deceleration. Inside the droplet, the atom is slowed down to a steady-state velocity that depends on the initial speed, contrasting experiments reporting a critical velocity for dopants ejected from droplets [Phys. Rev. Lett. 111, 153002 (2013)]. Remarkably, the velocity of the ejected atom is nearly independent of its initial velocity. We demonstrate that this behavior results from the bursting of the bubble surrounding the atom at the droplet surface, challenging the previous experimental interpretation.

articles.title: Lunar tidal response-induced clock frequency variations on the Moon
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.33117v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: As clock performance improves, the instability and uncertainty of the clock's fractional frequency shift (FFS) become comparable to the FFS caused by the lunar tidal response (LTR), so the influence of the LTR on lunar time needs to be investigated. In this paper, we used the Keplerian expansions method to study the FFS to the level of 10⁻¹⁸ caused by the LTR between two clocks placed in different positions on the Moon. We consider the case of the Moon orbiting in an elliptical orbit, which is closer to the actual situation compared to the case of the Moon moving in a circular orbit. An interesting phenomenon is found that the longitude difference between two clocks can cause a change in the amplitude and phase of the FFS due to the LTR, but the latitude difference only changes the amplitude of the FFS. We further estimated the clock difference between two clocks near the Moon caused by the LTR. When one clock is on the lunar surface, and the other is on the Earth's surface, the LTR will cause a clock difference of % -5.68× 10⁻⁷ μ s/day between the two clocks. These are significant for the construction of a lunar time and clock synchronization near the Moon.

articles.title: Kaonic Atom Measurements with the SIDDHARTA-2 Experiment at the DAΦNE accelerator
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35399v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Kaonic atoms provide a unique experimental tool to investigate low-energy strong interactions in systems containing strangeness and, through high-lying transitions, to test bound-state quantum electrodynamics. The SIDDHARTA-2 experiment at the DAΦNE electron--positron collider performs high-precision X-ray spectroscopy of kaonic atoms using low-momentum charged kaons produced in φ-meson decays. Its primary goal is the study of kaonic deuterium through the measurement of X-ray transitions to the ground state, providing direct access to the low-energy K^-d interaction. In parallel, SIDDHARTA-2 has carried out a broad experimental programme with gaseous targets, including kaonic helium-4 and kaonic neon, as well as measurements of high-n transitions in intermediate-mass kaonic atoms formed in the materials of the experimental setup. In this paper, the main SIDDHARTA-2 measurements and their physics motivations are reviewed, together with the experimental strategy developed for kaonic deuterium and the future perspectives of the collaboration within the EXKALIBUR programme.

articles.title: From First Principles to Multi-scale Decomposition: Mutual Information as a Segregation Index
articles.abstract: arXiv:2511.23069v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Segregation operates across demographic and spatial scales and requires careful and principled measurement. In this work, we derive mutual information from well-known general approaches to constructing segregation indices and interpret the mathematical properties that are unique to it. The properties relate mainly to its behaviour when demographic identities and spatial units are coarse-grained. Mutual information decomposes into the contributions of regions and supergroups, which reveals insights that would be inaccessible otherwise. We demonstrate this with an exploratory case study of residential ethnic segregation in England and Wales. Overall, we help researchers identify when mutual information is the only suitable segregation index and provide open source software to support multi-scale analysis.

articles.title: A Stable, High-Order Time-Stepping Scheme for the Drift-Diffusion Model in Modern Solar Cell Simulation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2603.09063v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper presents a one-dimensional transient drift-diffusion simulator for advanced solar cells, integrating a structure-preserving finite-volume spatial discretization with Scharfetter-Gummel-type fluxes and a high-order, L-stable implicit Runge-Kutta (Radau IIA) temporal integrator. The scheme ensures local charge conservation, handles sharp material interfaces, achieves second-order spatial and fifth-order temporal convergence, and exhibits excellent computational efficiency and numerical stability. Its accuracy is verified against the classical depletion approximation in p-n junction and validated against four independent software implementations for an organic photovoltaic device under a common protocol. The framework's extensibility is demonstrated by incorporating exciton kinetics in organic solar cells, capturing multi-timescale dynamics, and by modeling mobile ions in perovskite solar cells, reproducing characteristic J-V hysteresis without empirical parameters. This work provides a robust, high-order numerical foundation for simulating coupled charge, exciton, and ion transport in next-generation photovoltaic devices.

articles.title: Hessian-Similar Optimization with Capped Participation: Lower Bounds and Virtual Masters
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.33835v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: What is the round complexity of Hessian-similar optimization when each round can contact at most s of m clients? Prior rates permit a free master or full participation and do not characterize strict caps. We count every one-vector query and reply. A hidden-client chain gives a lower bound for zero-respecting local algorithms with adaptive cohorts and random stopping: on strongly convex quadratics, the required rounds are Ω((m/s)sqrtminδₐ,barδ/sqrt m/μ,log(1/ϵ)) for s≤(m-2)/2 in the high-accuracy, high-dissimilarity regime. Here μ is strong convexity, while δₐ and barδ bound anchor and average Hessian variation. To remove dependence on a poor anchor, virtual-master SVRS uses independent estimator and proximal cohorts and averages the proximal replies. With Catalyst, it reaches relative gap ϵ in tilde O(m/s+(sqrtm/s+m³/⁴/s)sqrtbarδ/μ) expected rounds on quadratics with strongly convex clients, independent of δₐ. Combining this method with charged analyses of existing algorithms matches the lower bound's polynomial dependence for s≤sqrt m and s=Ω(m); the worst gap is O(m¹/⁸). A held-out 12-seed synthetic study finds fewer rounds than tuned SVRP in nine of ten dip-family incomplete-cohort cells, versus two of 30 other cells. The lower bounds concern zero-respecting algorithms and do not cover unrestricted messages.

articles.title: Beyond Exact Recovery: Operational Success Probability and Sampling Cost for Approximate Quantum Optimization under Stochastic Uncertainty
articles.abstract: Approximate optimization algorithms are commonly evaluated through exact optimum recovery or objective-space approximation, although these criteria need not coincide with the quality of the resulting decision in its downstream operating environment. This paper develops an end-to-end evaluation framework that separates three notions of solver success: exact recovery of the mathematical optimum, near-optimality with respect to the optimization surrogate, and operational acceptability under stochastic downstream evaluation. We study the framework using a small binary inventory-control benchmark represented by a calibrated and held-out-validated QUBO surrogate and solved with exact enumeration, greedy search, simulated annealing, uniform feasible sampling, and ideal QAOA at depths p=1,2,3. The results show that mathematical near-optimality and downstream operational acceptability define distinct solution sets. For QAOA, the probability mass assigned to operationally acceptable solutions can differ materially from both exact-recovery and QUBO-near-optimal probability, producing substantial differences in the number of measurements required to observe an acceptable solution. For n=8 at p=2, the median number of shots required for 95% observation probability decreases from 392 under exact recovery to 84 under QUBO near-optimality and 31 under the operational criterion. However, operational success alone can be misleading when acceptable states are abundant. We therefore use a descriptive enrichment comparison against uniform feasible sampling. Statistically supported enrichment is observed only in selected regimes, while classical greedy and simulated-annealing baselines outperform QAOA on these small instances. The results therefore do not indicate quantum advantage; rather, they show that solver evaluation can change materially when success is defined in terms of downstream decision consequences rather than surrogate-objective recovery alone. The QAOA statevector implementation and selected frozen confirmatory cases were independently reproduced with Qiskit and Qiskit Aer to floating-point precision.

articles.title: 21st-century global urbanization drives disproportionate change beyond urban areas
articles.abstract: Urbanization is a critical anthropogenic process with largely irreversible effects on the Earth’s surface. However, the implications of future urbanization for other land-dependent systems, through changes in land availability and prices, remain poorly understood, largely due to simplified modeling assumptions and static urbanization constraints. Here, we quantify the impacts of urban land dynamics with a factorial scenario design combined with enhancements to a global multisectoral economic equilibrium model. We simulate divergent scenarios combining urbanization pathways, socioeconomic changes, and bioenergy deployment levels. Across all scenarios, global changes in non-urban land types by 2100 are almost twice as large as urban land changes. This is because managed land losses from urbanization are offset by expansions elsewhere or increased investment in yield-enhancing technologies or higher imports. These changes can increase crop prices, with some regions seeing up to a 20% increase. These results show that urban land expansion can have an indirect footprint that is much higher and beyond the physically urbanized area.

articles.title: Endpoint definitions and censoring in battery lifetime prediction across sources
articles.abstract: Reliable comparison of battery lifetime predictors requires a common endpoint and explicit treatment of incomplete trajectories. We examine how capacity references, right censoring and access to completed tar get lifetimes affect evaluation across experimental sources. A seven-source registry contains 220 physical cells; 214 contribute 318,707 cycle records. At an 80% threshold, changing from effective nominal to first observation references changes SNL observed events from 50 to 35 and HUST events from 0 to 77. For SNL predictions at cycle 100, event-only mean absolute percentage error is 36.31%, whereas 11 censored cells imply a full-cohort identification range of 45.37–47.80% without imputing lifetimes. At the observed 85% HUST endpoint, three-label calibration reduces allocation-averaged error from 75.64% to 16.25%, compared with 20.25% for a matched target-only constant and 14.23% for ordinary unshrunk calibration. Exhaustive evaluation of all 73,150 HUST and 19,600 SNL three-label allocations reveals consistent im provement on HUST but a harmful tail on SNL, where average event-only error rises to 48.50%. The allocations describe selection variability in fixed cohorts, not independent replications. These retrospec tive case studies support an engineering evaluation procedure that declares endpoint references, separates observed and censored outcomes, reports cohort-level error bounds, and compares adaptation methods us ing identical label budgets and test cells.

articles.title: Tuning in Dielectric and Electrical Transport Properties of CuFe2O4 with Incorporation of Metal oxides (ZnO, WO3 & MgO) Nanostructures
articles.abstract: Copper ferrite (COF) nanocomposites with different weight fractions (10 to 50 wt. %) of metal oxides (MOs; M = Zn, Mg & W) were synthesized by powder mixing method. The phase analysis and microstructure were examined by XRD, SEM and TEM techniques. The XRD analysis showed the formation of required nanocomposites without any other impurities. The examination of microstructure revealed the different morphology like; spherical, nano-discs, nano-plates and nano-spindle etc. The bahavior of dielectric constant (ε′), and dissipation factor (tanδ), of (MOs)x/(COF)1−x are consistent with Maxwell-Wagner polarization and Koop’s phenomenological theory. Moreover, the ε′ & tanδ show decreasing behavior with incorporation of MOs nano-structures. The a.c. conductivity with frequency follow the dynamical law σ (ɷ) = A ɷs. Finally, the incorporation of MOs wt. fractions reduce the conductivity due to substitution of Fe3+ and Fe2+ ions by metal cations (Zn2+, Mg2+ and W3+) from lattice site.

articles.title: Root-gap-dependent process window and weldability transition map for DCEN-GTAW butt joining of 0.08 mm AA3003 aluminum foil
articles.abstract: Establishing a suitable operating region for joining ultra-thin aluminum foil is challenging because small changes in thermal input can cause a transition from insufficient fusion to burn-through. This study experimentally investigates the weldability transition of 0.08 mm AA3003 aluminum foil during butt joining using direct-current electrode-negative gas tungsten arc welding (DCEN-GTAW) with dual argon shielding. Welding current was varied while travel speed, arc length, electrode geometry, and shielding conditions were kept constant. Three root-gap conditions of 0.5, 1.0, and 2.0 mm were investigated. Weld formation was classified as no stable weld, stable weld, or burn-through, with stable welds further evaluated through bead-width measurements and transverse metallography. Nominal heat input was calculated from the measured arc voltage, welding current, and travel speed. No stable weld was obtained at the 0.5 mm gap. At 1.0 mm, stable welding occurred at 5–10 A, while burn-through occurred at 15 A. At 2.0 mm, stable welding was maintained at 5–9 A before burn-through at 10 A. Bead width and HAZ generally increased with heat input. The results demonstrate that weldability is strongly influenced by both welding current and root gap, providing an initial weldability-transition map for parameter selection in ultra-thin aluminum foil joining.

articles.title: Comparative Study on Axial Compression Performance of Steel Tube–RCC–Timber Composite Columns using FEM Analysis
articles.abstract: This study presents a finite element (FE)-based comparative investigation into the axial compressive behaviour of steel tube-confined reinforced cement concrete (RCC)–timber composite columns versus their unstrengthened counterparts. Two column configurations were analysed: a nominal RCC–timber composite column (NTC) and an identical column externally strengthened with a 2 mm thick mild steel tube (STC). Both specimens share a 230 × 300 mm rectangular cross-section, 1000 mm height, four corner longitudinal bars of 12 mm diameter (Fe500), 25 mm nominal cover, M30 grade concrete, and a centrally placed 100 × 100 mm structural timber core extending the full column length. Three-dimensional nonlinear FE models were developed and subjected to monotonic axial compression, with the steel tube, concrete, timber core, and reinforcement idealised using calibrated elasto-plastic and orthotropic material models, coupled with surface-based contact formulations at all material interfaces to capture interaction effects. Results indicate that external steel tube confinement substantially enhanced structural performance: peak axial capacity increased by 33.5% (1128 kN for STC versus 845 kN for NTC), initial axial stiffness improved by 27.6%, and the ductility index rose by 43.2%. Peak corner stress concentration was reduced by approximately 19% relative to the nominal section. Behaviourally, NTC exhibited a brittle post-peak response dominated by corner-concentrated cracking, whereas STC demonstrated gradual, ductile softening characteristic of confined concrete action. The FE-derived load–deformation responses, stress contours, and comparative performance indices establish the quantitative structural benefit of external steel tube confinement in RCC–timber composite columns, offering design-oriented insights for subsequent experimental validation.

articles.title: Towards optimal preparation of triangular quantum cycle shifts
articles.abstract: An algorithm for the optimal preparation of triangular quantum cycle shifts is presented. Through theoretical analysis, it is shown that any optimal sequence of powers of two that sum to the fixed integer shift step must guarantee the exhaustive application of four local exchange rules, leading to the non-adjacent form of that integer step. Based on this, it is shown that the optimal form exists in the search sub-space formed by just considering the two closest powers of two from a given signed integer remainder, and that it can be reached via exhaustive depth-first search but also by a simpler approach, nicknamed “Domino”. Experimental comparisons between Domino and previously studied preparators for triangular quantum cycle shifts verify that the former always identifies the optimal sequence. Notably, the proposed approach achieves the same benefit in quantum cost as the previously studied dynamic programming algorithm, at more than 8 times the speed. Experiments on noisy backends further imply that Domino becomes asymptotically superior in noise resistance to the other methods as the register width grows, retaining a roughly 9% fidelity lead. These results establish Domino as an appealing choice for maximum-performance triangular quantum cycle shift preparation.

articles.title: Influence of Hydrogen Concentration and Point Defects on the Deformation, Phase Transformation, and Dislocation Evolution in Zirconium: A Molecular Dynamics Study
articles.abstract: Hydrogen ingress and irradiation-induced point defects critically influence the mechanical reliability of zirconium-based alloys used in nuclear applications. In this study, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations were employed to systematically investigate the effects of hydrogen concentration, vacancy defects, and self-interstitial atoms (SIAs)—individually and in combination—on the deformation behavior, elastic response, phase transformation, and dislocation evolution of α-zirconium subjected to uniaxial tensile loading. Stress–strain analysis of perfect and defective Zr-H systems revealed that the incorporation of hydrogen up to 5.0% induces only marginal changes in elastic modulus and tensile strength, whereas vacancy and interstitial defects significantly degrade mechanical performance. Vacancies reduce stiffness and promote earlier yielding, while SIAs exert the most pronounced weakening effect, drastically lowering tensile strength and strain at low concentrations and inducing complex deformation behavior at higher concentrations. Temperature and pressure were also shown to strongly modify the onset of yielding and the stability of the hexagonal close-packed (HCP) phase. Common neighbor analysis (CNA) and dislocation extraction algorithm (DXA) evaluations demonstrated that defects accelerate the HCP→“Others” phase transition, modify face-centered cubic (FCC) formation, and promote the nucleation of dislocation loops—especially in systems containing SIAs or high defect densities. Overall, the results highlight the dominant role of point defects, particularly SIAs, in governing the degradation of zirconium’s mechanical integrity, while showing that hydrogen alone exerts comparatively minor influence within the studied concentration range. These insights provide atomistic understanding essential for predicting the performance of zirconium cladding under irradiation and hydrogen uptake conditions.

articles.title: Bayesian Modeling of Corporate Financial Distress Risk in Emerging Markets with Evidence from Moroccan Firms
articles.abstract: Corporate financial distress prediction remains a central issue in financial risk management, particularly in emerging markets where economic volatility, information asymmetry, and limited financial transparency increase uncertainty in credit risk assessment. Traditional financial distress prediction models, including discriminant analysis and logistic regression, often fail to adequately capture uncertainty and parameter heterogeneity in such environments. This study proposes a Bayesian probabilistic framework for modeling Corporate Financial Distress Risk among Moroccan listed firms. The proposed approach employs a Bayesian hierarchical logistic model to estimate the posterior probability of corporate financial distress using key financial indicators, including liquidity ratios, leverage, profitability, and cash flow measures. By incorporating prior information and posterior updating, the model provides a flexible statistical structure for handling uncertainty and improving predictive inference. Parameter estimation is performed using Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) simulation to obtain posterior distributions and credible intervals for risk parameters. The empirical analysis uses panel data from firms listed on the Casablanca Stock Exchange over multiple years. Results are expected to demonstrate that Bayesian estimation improves predictive stability and provides richer uncertainty quantification compared with classical approaches. The findings contribute to applied financial statistics by introducing a robust probabilistic framework for financial distress risk prediction in emerging economies. This study also offers practical implications for investors, banks, regulators, and policymakers seeking more reliable credit risk assessment tools under uncertain market conditions.

articles.title: Pair-Structured Polynomial Rooting in Signal Processing: Polytopic Cascade Design, A Spread Identity for Root-MUSIC, and What It Says About Breakdown Detection
articles.abstract: Two common polynomial-rooting tasks in signal processing, cascade IIR design and subspace direction-of-arrival estimation, carry symmetries that standard rooting discards. We study both through a emphpair-structured parameterization in which the polynomial is a product of second-order sections, each described by a centre and a spread. For cascade design the Schur region of a section is the triangle |c|<1, |2A|<1+c, so the stable region of a whole cascade is a polytope; magnitude fitting subject to guaranteed stability then becomes a smooth problem over a convex set, and we observe roughly an order of magnitude of error reduction per added section. For root-MUSIC the relevant symmetry is conjugate-reciprocal, roots occurring in pairs (z,1/z*) that emphcoalesce on the unit circle in the noiseless limit because the MUSIC null spectrum is non-negative with double zeros at the true angles. This degenerate-pair structure is the central object of the paper. We prove an exact first-order identity, νₖ²=2fₘᵢₙ/f'', relating the pair spread νₖ=log|zₖ| to the residual null-spectrum depth and its curvature, and we verify the resulting scaling law νsim N⁻¹/² to three decimal places across four SNRs. We report three findings, two of them negative and stated plainly because each contradicts a natural expectation. First, the pair-symmetrized angle estimator is emphalgebraically identical to textbook root-MUSIC: symmetry exploitation yields no variance reduction at all, and our Monte Carlo confirms bit-identical RMSE at every SNR. Second, the pair spread is a strong breakdown detector, reaching area under the ROC curve of 0.974 at -6~dB against 0.842 for the eigenvalue gap and 0.575 for an AIC statistic, at literally zero additional cost. Third, and against our own framing, the raw null depth fₘᵢₙ emphoutperforms the spread uniformly, reaching AUC 1.000 at -6~dB; our identity explains why, since dividing by a trial-varying curvature injects variance. The practical recommendation that follows is therefore not the one we set out to make.

articles.title: A Radiometrically-Agnostic SegFormer Framework for Water Segmentation inC-Band SAR Imagery
articles.abstract: Accurate and timely mapping of surface water bodies is critical for sustainable water management, yet automated methods must overcome challenges posed by diverse sensor characteristics and complex environmental conditions. This paper presents a robust and efficient end-to-end framework for water segmentation that addresses these issues. We adapt the lightweight SegFormer Mix-Vision Transformer (MiT) architecture for multi-modal data fusion, combining C-band Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imagery with topographic features (elevation and slope). A key contribution is our per-scene normalization strategy combined with small patch sizes, which renders the model agnostic to the input's radiometric correction (e.g., Sigma, Beta, or Gamma Naught), significantly enhancing its generalization across different sensors. Through a comparative analysis of SegFormer B0 and B1 variants, we demonstrate that the more efficient B0 model achieves state-of-the-art performance, attaining a Water IoU of 0.958 on a held-out test set, slightly surpassing the larger B1 model while being approximately 48% faster at inference. Our findings indicate that for this application, a well-adapted, lightweight transformer provides the optimal balance of performance and computational efficiency, offering a pragmatic and highly accurate solution for operational, large-scale water monitoring.

articles.title: Hydrothermally Derived α-Fe2O3 Nanorods with Local Lattice Distortion for Improved Lithium Storage
articles.abstract: α-Fe2O3 is a promising conversion-type anode for lithium-ion batteries, but sluggish charge transfer and large structural variation limit its cycling performance. Here, α-Fe2O3 nanorods (H-Fe2O3) were prepared by a simple FeCl3·6H2O/Na2SO4 hydrothermal route followed by calcination at 450°C and compared with commercial α-Fe2O3 (C-Fe2O3). H-Fe2O3 consists of short, loosely packed nanorods, whereas C-Fe2O3 contains compact irregular particles. HRTEM reveals locally bent and discontinuous lattice fringes in H-Fe2O3, while C-Fe2O3 shows straighter and more continuous fringes, indicating stronger local lattice distortion in the hydrothermal sample. XRD and Raman confirm the hematite phase, while XPS reveals a more heterogeneous surface oxygen environment for H-Fe2O3.The nanorod electrode also shows a more open porous texture, higher reversible capacity, improved cycling retention and lower charge-transfer resistance. After 150 cycles, H-Fe2O3 retains approximately 0.72 Ah g− 1, compared with about 0.47 Ah g− 1 for C-Fe2O3. The improvement is attributed to shortened Li+ transport paths, interparticle void space, local lattice distortion and faster interfacial kinetics.

articles.title: Design and Experimental Evaluation of a Bifacial Solar Photovoltaic–Based Electric Vehicle Charging System with Rear-Side Reflection Enhancement
articles.abstract: In order to reduce the reliance on the grid and minimize the amount of carbon emissions produced through transportation, the rapid adoption of electric cars (EVs) has enhanced the demand for green and sustainable charging infrastructure. Solar-powered EV charging systems provide an efficient solution; however, the inherent limitation of traditional monofacial photovoltaic (PV) technology is that it depends on harnessing solar irradiance from the front side. Bifacial photovoltaic technology helps overcome this limitation by harnessing energy from the front and back sides of the panel. This results in an enhanced output for the surface in comparison to traditional photovoltaic technology. The reflectivity of the surface and the technology can have an enormous impact on the back side. This paper, apart from statistically investigating the impact of different reflexive surfaces on energy generation and EV charging efficiencies, proposes an efficient design for a bifacial photovoltaic technology-based EV charging system. The high-power 545 W bifacial PV module, coupled with the EV battery charging device and a maximum power point tracking charge controller, is adopted to form a comparative experiment configuration. Given the same outside working environment, three efficient rear-side reflected materials, such as white paint, silver paint, and aluminum foil, are experimented upon. Voltage, current, power output, irradiance, temperature, etc., are the important electric and environmental parameters that are continuously monitored to measure the rear-side efficiency and the overall efficiency of the system. According to experimental findings, the efficiency of a bifacial PV system is significantly enhanced through rear-side optimization. Aluminum foil gains the highest amount of irradiance and achieves a power gain of 15–25%. Additionally, the modified system showed increased stability in charging current as well as a reduced charging time under conditions of varying irradiance levels, particularly for EV battery charging. From the result, it is evident that MPPT control in conjunction with low-cost rear-side reflective optimization is a cost-effective, scalable, and sustainable strategy for solar-powered EV charging.

articles.title: Effects of Frying time and Layering of Moringa (Moringa stenopetala) Leaf Powder on Oxidative Stability and Total Carotenoids of Banana Chips
articles.abstract: Banana (Musa-sapientum L) is a typical climacteric fruit that highly cultivated and mostly accepted fruit due to its sensorial acceptability and nutritional value. It is known for its short-shelf stability and developing a shelf stable banana product is essential. The aim of this study was to determine the effects of frying time and layering of Moringa leaf powder on free fatty acid, peroxide value and total carotenoids on banana chips. In this study the two levels of moringa leaf powder layering (3% & 6%) and three levels of frying time (1.5, 2, & 2.5 minutes) were combined. The results showed that the banana chips had free fatty acid (0.19g/100g–1.19g/100g), per oxide value (0.78g/100g–1.79g/100g) and total carotenoid contents (50.59µg /g- 373.10 µg /g). The FFA and PV of banana chips were negatively affected by concentration of moringa leaf powder. On the other hand, the fat content of banana chips resulted higher through frying time due to the replacement of moisture with frying oil. The increased concentration of moringa leaf powder somehow reduces the losses of total carotenoids. The layering of moringa leaf powder during prolonged frying to banana chips improves oxidative stabilities without compromising the total carotenoid contents of banana chips

articles.title: A Unified Continuous Time Framework for Adaptive Smartphone Battery Drain Prediction with Finite Horizon Error Analysis
articles.abstract: Smartphone battery prediction requires a consistent connection between hardware demand, electrical dynamics and capacity aging. We develop a unified continuous-time framework that integrates a second-order equivalent circuit, a temperature-dependent resistance model, empirical aging and adaptive load calibration. A finite-horizon error analysis connects current bias and capacity uncertainty to state-of-charge drift, while exact interval updates provide a reference for numerical verification. Evaluation combines new Android telemetry, 1000 public smartphone workload profiles and five laboratory cell trajectories. On a later ZTE session, static scale calibration reduces power mean absolute error from 1.582 to 0.232 W; a predict-before-update recursive comparator achieves 0.117 W. Across 17 forward temporal blocks, the recursive method yields a pooled error of 0.155 W, with condition-dependent failures. On public Pixel 8 profiles, linear hardware features explain 89.4% of variation in a nominal-voltage power proxy. Dual-exponential capacity extrapolation achieves 0.00651 Ah root-mean-square error on the UCL cell, but offers no general advantage over simpler models on four NASA cells. The results establish a reproducible route from load calibration to charge-balance error assessment and identify the conditions governing model deployment. Complete-discharge validation remains necessary to quantify end-to-end runtime accuracy.

articles.title: Radiation simulation of ⁶⁰Fe in lunar regolith decay
articles.abstract: Supernova explosion is an important site for the synthesis of heavy element nuclei. The radioactive isotope ⁶⁰Fe(half-life 2.62Myr)can be used as a ‘time-scale probe’ for near-Earth supernova activity. When the eruption position is within the solar system tens of parsecs,⁶⁰Fe can be captured by the moon and deposited on the surface of the lunar regolith. Its decay radiation will produce a large amount of γ-rays. In this paper, the γ flux and spatial distribution generated by the decay characteristic lines (58.6keV, 1173keV and 1332keV) of ⁶⁰Fe are simulated, and the reception of γ-rays at different energies is simulated. Based on the mass absorption coefficient of lunar regolith (58.6keV: µ ≈ 0.4228cm² ∙g− 1;>1MeV༚µ ≈ 0.063cm²∙g−¹)and ⁶⁰Fe deposition flux of ~ 10⁷ atoms∙cm− 2, the following conclusions are obtained:༈1༉The low energy 58.6keV spectral line flux is only 6.55×10− 24 erg∙cm− 2∙s− 1, which is dominated by the strong absorption of Compton scattering and decays exponentially from the center to the edge.༈2༉The flux of MeV energy band 1173keV and 1332keV lines can reach 10− 20erg∙cm− 2∙s− 1, which is about 4 orders of magnitude higher than that of 58.6 keV line due to the penetration advantage.༈3༉The total flux of the three characteristic spectral lines is lower than the sensitivity threshold of the existing space γ-ray telescopes, which suggests that direct detection of lunar ⁶⁰Fe decay radiation by current in-orbit instruments is not feasible.

articles.title: Deformation – Entropy Metrics in Si-C-N Hard Coats
articles.abstract: Distorted indented geometries are representations of dissipation of localized locked-in stress on the hard coating surface. The distortions in most occasions manifest themselves in different ways in the load-depth (P-h) plots of nanoindentation like Pop-ins, pop-outs and linear unloads Fracture Mechanical principles applied to those sections provide quantitative fracture parameters like Fracture toughness. As energy is involved in the dissipation, an alternative approach to harness the mechanism involved in the asymmetrical distortions of the indented zones in Si-C-N coatings was established. Novel concepts like entropy mediated energy dissipation, stress localization, non linear stress redistribution and a transition occurring from a stable energy accommodation to instability driven delamination were explored on the basis of some new parameters like entropy dissipation coefficient (Sd), stress gradient (Λs), nonlinear instability function (Φn), deformation, and strain accommodating parameter (Γp) which could provide a more accountable explanation on the distortion occurring in the indent shape than conventional thin film fracture mechanics.

articles.title: Age-stratified associations between meteorological factors and haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome in Shaanxi Province, China, 2005–2020: a distributed lag non-linear analysis aligned with vaccination programme eligibility ages
articles.abstract: Background Shaanxi Province reports the highest burden of haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) in China, concentrated in the Guanzhong Plain. Whether meteorological sensitivity differs across age strata aligned with the eligibility ages of the national vaccination programme (16–60 years) has not been quantified.Methods We obtained monthly HFRS case counts for 27 age groups in Shaanxi, 2005–2020 (26,677 cases), constructed incidence with census-interpolated denominators, and aggregated cases into vaccination-aligned strata: 0–19, 20–59 and ≥ 60 years. Exposures came from 12 China Meteorological Administration surface stations. Quasi-Poisson distributed lag non-linear models were fitted per stratum for monthly mean temperature, relative humidity and precipitation (lag 0–6 months); long-term trends (2004–2024) were assessed by joinpoint regression.Results No statistically significant joinpoints were identified; incidence declined gradually and non-significantly (annual percent change − 0.83%/year, 95% confidence interval [CI] − 4.68 to 3.07), with multi-year cycles and a 60% fall in 2024. Stratum-specific incidence was lowest at 0–19 years (1.77/100,000) and highest at ≥ 60 years (6.45/100,000). Low temperature was associated with elevated risk in all main models (cumulative relative risk [RR] at − 1.2°C: 2.15–3.39; intervals wide and overlapping), with no effect modification by stratum (interaction p = 0.999); cold-temperature estimates attenuated below unity under calendar-year-indicator control, indicating entanglement with epidemic cycles. Hydro-meteorological associations were positive but imprecise in the main models: at 80% relative humidity, cumulative RRs were 2.44 (95% CI 0.44–13.6), 1.92 (0.67–5.46) and 3.16 (0.97–10.2), and 150 mm precipitation gave 3.05 (1.06–8.82) in the 20–59 group, significant only on the original scale. Under the year-indicator specification these estimates strengthened severalfold (humidity 8.70, 3.11, 4.36; precipitation 6.56); the 0–19 and ≥ 60 year humidity associations and the precipitation association survived false-discovery-rate control and are hypothesis-generating. Colder autumns preceded heavier epidemic peaks (exploratory; Spearman ρ = −0.64, p = 0.010).Conclusions Meteorological conditions were associated with HFRS risk across vaccination-aligned age strata in Shaanxi. Humidity and precipitation showed positive but imprecise, specification-sensitive associations, whereas the low-temperature association could not be separated from multi-year epidemic cycles. Adults aged ≥ 60 years had the highest incidence and elevated hydro-meteorological sensitivity. On the basis of incidence burden, these findings support evaluation of extending HFRS vaccination beyond age 60.

articles.title: Dimensional Control of Excitonic Interactions in Exfoliated 2D Molecular Crystals
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.09923v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Excited states in molecular crystals depend on intermolecular coupling, charge-transfer interactions, dielectric screening and molecular packing. How reduced dimensionality modifies these interactions when molecular packing structure is preserved remains unclear. Here we demonstrate that tetracene and three other molecular crystals can be mechanically exfoliated into mono-, few- or multilayer flakes, exploiting the top-down approach established for inorganic layered materials. Electron diffraction confirms that exfoliated tetracene retains long-range crystalline order and nearly bulk-like in-plane lattice parameters. This structural fidelity enables systematic thickness-dependent spectroscopy with limited changes in molecular packing. With decreasing thickness, the Davydov splitting diminishes, whereas the Stokes shift increases to nearly three times its bulk-like value, indicating enhanced excited-state relaxation. The photoluminescence 0-0/0-1 intensity ratio also rises, suggesting greater exciton delocalization. Compared with exfoliated tetracene, assembly-grown crystals exhibit lattice contraction and larger Davydov splitting. Analysis within the Frenkel-charge-transfer mixing framework qualitatively accounts for the Davydov-state energy shifts and splitting in terms of molecular packing, intermolecular coupling and dielectric screening. Our results show that intermolecular interactions, excited-state relaxation and exciton coherence can be systematically tuned by varying layer number, demonstrating the feasibility and utility of extending dimensional control of inorganic 2D materials to molecular crystals.

articles.title: Towards a Metal-Organic Framework with Pore-Confined Electrons
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.13939v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Electrides are an unconventional class of materials in which electrons are localized in crystallographic void spaces rather than solely around atomic nuclei, giving rise to appealing properties such as low work functions, strong electron-donating character, and even superconductivity. Here, we use ab initio methods to investigate metal-organic framework (MOF) electrides, a new class of materials that combines the interstitial electrons of electrides with the permanent porosity and chemical tunability of MOFs. These materials host pore-confined electrons: occupied electronic states localized in the pore space and with bands slightly below or crossing through the Fermi level. Using density functional theory calculations, we establish several design rules for stabilizing pore-confined electrons in MOFs via an anion-electron exchange process and identify candidate MOF electrides. As a proof-of-concept, we also demonstrate that the pore-confined electrons can directly facilitate chemical reactions, substantially lowering the activation barrier for H2 dissociation without requiring adsorption at a surface site. We envision that pore-confined electrons in nanoporous materials may enable a fundamentally new type of catalysis in which chemical reactions take place in the pore space, driven by electron-centered active sites.

articles.title: Toward catalyst-mediated growth of diamond and cubic boron nitride wires
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.33478v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Sustained catalyst-mediated growth of diamond and cubic boron nitride (cBN) wires has yet to be established reproducibly, although related methods produce carbon and BN nanotubes and many elemental and compound nanowires. I hypothesize that a retained contact between a catalyst and an existing tetrahedral crystal can sustain wire extension under conditions that do not nucleate that crystal on an otherwise comparable unseeded catalyst. The prediction is repeated, vapor-derived target-phase extension during an interval in which matched unseeded contacts do not nucleate that phase. I develop tests using diamond seeds, SiC starter wires and cBN seeds, separating the conditions used to establish the contact from those used for continuation. Worked estimates distinguish bulk precipitation driving forces from sidewall costs and show why increased carbon activity alone cannot select diamond over graphite. Comparisons with established synthesis identify the roles of pressure, hydrogen and activated nitrogen that must be retained or replaced. Isotope tracing, local structural measurements and time-dependent growth distinguish continued incorporation from seed consumption, conversion and etching. Nanometer, micrometer and larger wires could provide electrically insulating thermal connections, mechanical probes and reinforcing filaments.

articles.title: Quantum Counting in the Rydberg Blockade
articles.abstract: arXiv:2506.19298v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We propose a quantum algorithm for approximately counting the number of solutions to planar 2-satisfiability (2SAT) formulas natively on neutral-atom quantum computers (NAQC). Our algorithm maps Boolean variables to atomic registers arranged in space according to a given formula, so that 2SAT constraints are enforced via the Rydberg blockade between neighboring atoms. A quench of an initial computational basis state then produces a superposition of all solutions after sufficiently long evolution. For almost uniform superpositions, a polynomial number of measurements is enough to estimate the solution count up to any constant multiplicative factor via sampling-based counting. Numerical simulations show that the protocol leads to almost uniform solution sampling in 1D and 2D grids and produces accurate counts for small random 2SAT instances on punctured grids. We implement our algorithm on Pasqal's Orion Alpha NAQC and demonstrate approximate counts within small multiplicative factors of the exact count for a planar grid instance with 81 atoms.

articles.title: Unconventional Materials for Light Dark Matter Detection
articles.abstract: arXiv:2507.07164v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We propose the use of several unconventional materials as detectors for dark matter with mass beneath the MeV scale. These include the transition-metal dichalcogenide TiSe₂ hosting a low-energy plasmon in the charge-density-wave phase, Sr₂RuO₄ containing a low-energy acoustic demon mode, and hole-doped diamond with tunable optical and acoustic plasmon frequencies. We perform first-principles density functional theory computations of their loss functions at non-vanishing momenta and establish their reach into light dark matter parameter space. We show that due to intense low-energy plasmon modes -- of different microscopic origin in each -- the reach of detectors based on these materials could surpass existing proposals by several orders of magnitude for both dark matter scattering and absorption on electrons. The anisotropic response of these materials, which enables directional detection, renders them exceptionally strong detector candidates, motivating the design and fabrication of future devices.

articles.title: Anyonic membranes and Pontryagin statistics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2509.14314v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Anyons, unique to two spatial dimensions, underlie extraordinary phenomena such as the fractional quantum Hall effect, but their generalization to higher dimensions has remained elusive. The topology of Eilenberg-MacLane spaces constrains the loop statistics to be only bosonic or fermionic in any dimension. In this work, we introduce the novel anyonic statistics for membrane excitations in four dimensions. Analogous to the Z_N-particle exhibiting ZN× gcd₍₂,N₎ anyonic statistics in two dimensions, we show that the Z_N-membrane possesses ZN× gcd₍₃,N₎ anyonic statistics in four dimensions. Given unitary volume operators that create membrane excitations on the boundary, we propose an explicit 56-step unitary sequence that detects the membrane statistics. We further analyze the boundary theory of (5+1)D 1-form Z_N symmetry-protected topological phases and demonstrate that their domain walls realize all possible anyonic membrane statistics. We then show that the Z₃ subgroup persists in all higher dimensions. In addition to the standard fermionic Z₂ membrane statistics arising from Stiefel-Whitney classes, membranes also exhibit Z₃ statistics associated with Pontryagin classes. We explicitly verify that the 56-step process detects the nontrivial Z₃ statistics in 5, 6, and 7 spatial dimensions. Moreover, in 7 and higher dimensions, the statistics of membrane excitations stabilize to Z₂ × Z₃, with the Z₃ sector consistently captured by this process.

articles.title: 2D pores offer an optimal balance of charge storage and charging kinetics
articles.abstract: Electrolyte-filled conducting nanopores are central to applications ranging from energy storage to neuromorphic computing, yet the influence of pore geometry and structure on ion confinement remains insufficiently understood. Here, we combine theoretical calculations and molecular simulations to investigate how nanopore charging depends on pore dimensionality and morphology, considering nanostructured electrodes comprising cylindrical (1D) and slit-shaped (2D) pores, as well as 3D disordered porous electrodes exemplified by a carbide-derived carbon (CDC) structure. We show that in 1D confinement, the equilibrium stored charge exhibits a non-monotonic dependence on pore size, whereas 2D pores generally provide higher charge and energy densities per unit surface area. Somewhat counterintuitively, charging dynamics in 2D pores can slow down with increasing pore size but remain substantially faster than in disordered 3D electrodes. Although counterion saturation at high cell voltages reduces the energy stored by subnanometer 2D pores relative to CDC electrodes, this limitation can be overcome by matching the pore width to the operating voltage. Overall, our results indicate that 2D pores offer an optimal balance between charge storage and charging kinetics, highlighting their potential for high-performance capacitive energy storage.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Calculation of salt solubility in aqueous electrolyte solutions based on a thermodynamic ion-aggregation model
articles.abstract: Based on a thermodynamic self-association model in salt solutions, new attempts have been made to predict salt solubility in NaCl solutions and other electrolyte solutions by incorporating potential of mean force (PMF) analysis from molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. It was demonstrated that salt solubility is closely associated with critical ion aggregation concentration (CIAC) in the thermodynamic ion aggregation process. The CIAC is determined by estimating effective binding energy between a cation and an anion or a mean equilibrium constant in ion association process. The calculated salt solubilities in various alkali halide solutions are consistent with the experimentally measured values. Combined MD simulations and graph-theoretical analysis revealed that, in NaCl solutions, most ions remain isolated at lower salt concentrations, whereas various-sized ion aggregates emerge as the salt concentration increases. As the salt concentration rises beyond the CIAC, large aggregates are formed, eventually leading to liquid–solid phase separation in NaCl–water mixtures. It is anticipated that this salt solubility prediction approach, based on the thermodynamic ion self-association model, may also contribute to estimating the solubility limit of various solute molecules in aqueous solutions, such as alcohols, osmolytes, and peptides.

articles.title: Intracavity photon statistics from correlated molecular electronic structure
articles.abstract: Quantum optics characterizes light through photon correlations, motivating their connection to correlated ab initio molecular electronic structure. In this study, intracavity photon statistics of cavity-coupled molecules are computed from QED coupled-cluster (QED-CCSD-22) densities and validated against exact diagonalization of the Pauli–Fierz Hamiltonian. A change of coordinate origin or dipole convention displaces the ground state coherently, so second-order and higher cumulants of the cavity field are independent of these conventions even for molecular ions. The photon subsystem of QED Hartree–Fock is exactly coherent, so the invariant statistics describe fluctuations beyond this electron–photon product reference. The field fluctuations are super-Poissonian, and their degree of second-order coherence depends primarily on cavity frequency in the tested weak-coupling regime, falling from 18.5 to 4.9 for H 2 as the cavity is detuned from 5 to 20 eV. The third cumulant identifies non-Gaussian fluctuations and changes sign under reversal of the coupling direction.

articles.title: Correcting basis-set errors due to the absence of the electron–electron cusp using an adiabatic connection
articles.abstract: This article proposes an analytical method to address the slow convergence of electronic structure calculations caused by the inability of finite one-particle basis sets to describe the electron–electron cusp. (Small Gaussian basis set errors are often constructed or used with the objective to reduce computational effort, and may contain other sources of errors.) A model correspondence is established between a calculation using a finite basis set with the physical Coulomb interaction and a calculation using a complete basis set with a model interaction (specifically, the error-function screened Coulomb potential characterized by a range-separation parameter μ ). By leveraging the adiabatic connection formalism, a simple correction formula is derived. It does not contain any fitting to reference experimental or calculated data. It depends only on the on-top pair density and a locally defined range-separation parameter ( μ ) derived from the basis set itself. This “adiabatic connection based basis-set error correction” is derived from the asymptotic expansion of the wave function at large μ for small inter-electronic distances. Therefore, it is applicable to both ground and excited states without the restriction imposed by the Hohenberg–Kohn theorem. Numerical tests illustrate that the method achieves chemical accuracy (energy errors <1 kcal/mol) using smaller basis sets than typically required.
