articles.abstract_zh_full: 从观测数据估计同期双向相互作用很困难，因为每个结果都是内生的，而灵活的回归可能只捕获简化形式的依赖性。本文提出了 SEM-DNN，一种异方差神经联立方程估计器，无需外部仪器即可学习相互的结构相互作用。识别利用条件协方差对角化：当结构冲击的条件均值为零、在给定预定协变量的情况下条件不相关并且表现出非比例条件方差时，只有真实的相互作用系数对特征空间上的条件残差协方差进行对角化。该方法使用结合了联立系统雅可比行列式的对角高斯拟似然来联合近似非线性结构平均函数和特征相关方差。我们建立了轮廓总体标准的唯一识别和正定局部曲率，并表明，在神经轮廓兼容性条件下，尽管网络参数化不唯一，但所实现的神经标准继承了该曲率。当结构方程代表在相关干预下保持不变的自主机制时，系数承认因果解释。使用非线性、高维干扰函数和非高斯冲击进行的蒙特卡罗实验表明，随着信息的增加，SEM-DNN 比参数化、基于核和分离方程神经替代方案更可靠地恢复结构效应，尽管计算成本更高。即食谷物扫描仪数据的应用说明了该方法如何研究同期价格销售反馈并评估识别强度、残差对角化、方差校准和优化灵敏度。

articles.title: From Dueling Bandits to Episodic MDPs: Learning with Adversarial Preference Feedback
articles.abstract: arXiv:2507.11706v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In dueling bandits, the learner compares two arms in each round and observes only which one is preferred. This paper asks what changes when the compared pair also affects the next state, as in a recommendation interface where the pair shown to a user affects the user's next context. We formulate this problem as a state-wise preference-based MDP, an episodic tabular MDP in which the learner selects a pair of arms at each visited state, observes only a noisy comparison between them, and moves to a next state that may depend on the pair. The preferences may change adversarially across episodes, and the loss of a pair is defined through Borda scores. We show that the minimax regret of this problem under known transitions is tildeΘ(minHT,(H³SK)¹/³T²/³), where H, S, K, and T are the numbers of steps per episode, states, arms, and episodes, and that this rate is achieved by an algorithm based on online linear optimization over the set of occupancy measures. If the pair did not affect the next state, each state would be a separate dueling bandit, and the T²/³ term of the minimax regret would be smaller by a factor of H¹/³, demonstrating the cost of having action-dependent state transitions. We also give a policy optimization algorithm with closed-form updates, whose regret is tildeO((H⁴SK³)¹/³T²/³) up to lower-order terms, and we extend both algorithms to unknown transitions.

articles.title: PPO vs. SAC: A Comparative Study for Cooperative Motion Control of Dual-Arm Space Robots
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32034v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The growing population of orbital debris has intensified interest in active debris removal and on-orbit servicing, for which dual-arm space manipulators offer improved grasping stability and load distribution relative to single-arm systems. However, coordinating two manipulators under inter-arm collision avoidance, orientation alignment, and sensing uncertainty remains challenging. This paper develops a coordinated reinforcement learning framework for cooperative motion planning of a dual-arm space manipulator in a target-reaching task with inter-arm collision-avoidance constraints. A centralized state representation combines joint-space, end-effector, and target-relative information, while a multi-objective reward function promotes target-reaching accuracy, orientation alignment, motion smoothness, synchronized task completion, and collision avoidance. Within this framework, Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) and Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) are compared as representative on-policy and off-policy algorithms, and the learned policies are further evaluated for generalization to previously unseen target configurations. Across five random seeds, SAC substantially outperforms PPO within the considered fixed-base simulation scenarios: it reaches an 80% success threshold in every seed (median 1.6M environment steps) whereas PPO does not reach it within a 4M-step budget, and it attains a higher mean success rate (78.6% versus 7.4%) with lower position and orientation errors and tighter bimanual synchronization. Both algorithms degrade on unseen boundary targets, but SAC retains most of its performance while PPO's collapses. The results also expose a failure mode of PPO: under the two-phase shaped reward, it tends to converge to a reward-loitering local optimum rather than committing to the precision task. This behavior highlights the sensitivity of on-policy learning to reward shaping.

articles.title: Spatial Heuristic Strategy based Diffusion Reinforcement Learning for Online 3D Bin Packing
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32241v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Traditional heuristic methods have accumulated mature experience in core objectives, such as space utilization and layout compactness of 3D bin packing, relying on artificially designed rule-based logic. However, they exhibit obvious limitations in generalization ability and adaptability to dynamic scenarios. Diffusion reinforcement learning, which integrates the spatial search capability of reinforcement learning and the data distribution modeling capability of diffusion learning, has achieved certain progress in action distribution modeling and decision compliance constraints. Nevertheless, there remain issues including insufficient perception of the spatial topological structure in 3D bin packing and limited layout optimization capability. To address these problems, we propose a diffusion reinforcement learning method integrated with spatial heuristic strategies, which combines classical bin packing heuristic rules with a diffusion reinforcement learning framework. Specifically, it compresses the action space through heuristic action pre-screening, introduces a graph neural network to model the spatial structure, and designs a composite reward function incorporating flatness to suppress spatial fragmentation, thereby realizing the organic integration of prior knowledge and adaptive optimization. Experimental results demonstrate that the pro

articles.title: Minimum Description Length Unsupervisedly Separates Law-Grade from Statistical-Grade Knowledge in a Self-Improving Science Agent - and Reveals 86% of Its Own Discoveries Are Statistical
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32245v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI systems that discover scientific relations now generate candidate "laws" at scale, but the bottleneck has shifted from generation to vetting: which candidates deserve belief? We show that a deployed self-improving science agent - one that has admitted 252 relations through held-out prediction courts - already computes the quantity that answers this question: the Minimum Description Length compression ratio used for model selection doubles, when read under discrete accounting, as an unsupervised epistemic grader. The compression-ranked top band of the agent's ledger recovers exactly the canonical laws among its discoveries (vis-viva across seven planets, Balmer/Rydberg) plus cross-measurement identities - enrichment p=3.6×10⁻¹² under a hypergeometric test - with zero counterexamples and physically coherent band structure. The same lens retroactively reveals that 86% of the ledger compresses nothing (crapprox 1): the agent had been recording statistical regularities, including a learned predictor with held-out R²=0.541 admitted through the prediction gate, under a narrative of compression as the unified value of knowledge - a narrative that was never true for them. We formalize the resulting dual-axis bookkeeping - prediction value (R²) and compression value (cr) as nearly decoupled axes of knowledge - demonstrate its robustness to quantization, and register forward falsifiable predictions. The episode is, to our knowledge, the first measured instance of a discovery agent auditing its own knowledge ledger by an internal measure and finding itself over-claiming.

articles.title: RSIHub: A Composable Framework for Agent-Evolution Methods
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32253v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agent-evolution methods use execution feedback to improve prompts, skills, tools, and orchestration, but their implementations often rebuild the same experimental machinery. We present RSIHub, an open-source framework for building, comparing, and extending these methods on shared infrastructure. Recipes compose reusable operators and declare mutable resources; RSIHub supplies execution, evaluation, recovery, and lineage. Researchers can focus on evolution policy while evaluation stays outside the mutable surface and results remain tied to candidates and evaluation conditions. We instantiate AHE, Hyperagents, A-Evolve, and GEPA without modifying the framework core, keeping method-specific logic in recipes and operators. We evaluate them with MiniSWE and Codex on Terminal Bench 2 and τ³ Banking under fixed model and evaluator configurations. The largest observed overall pass@1 gain is 13.5 percentage points, while method rankings vary across settings and optimization gains do not always transfer to held-out tasks. RSIHub provides a common protocol for comparing evolution policies, inspectable candidate histories, and reusable components for developing new methods.

articles.title: Adaptive Control of Scientific Instruments with Nonstationary Responses through Multimodal Agents
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32370v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Controlling scientific instruments requires parameters to be adjusted progressively in response to feedback from successive operations. When unobserved operating conditions evolve with operational history, responses become nonstationary, and a static mapping from actions to responses becomes inadequate for decisions across shots. Shot-to-shot tuning of neutral beam injection (NBI) ion sources in magnetic confinement fusion devices is representative of this class of problems: the conditions of electrode surfaces and vacuum are difficult to observe directly, discharge outcomes vary between shots, and experiments are costly and carry operational risks. We propose a physically grounded multimodal agent with three independently auditable components. Deterministic algorithms extract symbolic physical quantities and visual evidence from multichannel waveforms; a memory with two layers organizes trajectories from the current task, experience from earlier tasks, and procedural knowledge, from which a multimodal large language model (MLLM) generates candidate actions; and an independent action feasibility check enforces action constraints before execution. In a strictly chronological replay of 455 shots from four EXL-50U platforms, physical symbols alone outperformed waveform images alone by 0.21-0.32 in macro-F1 for quality classification across all four evaluated models. Retrieved context increased the mean agreement with historical action directions by 22.4-42.7 percentage points, whereas the contribution of visual evidence varied across models. Under supervised operation on five ion sources, the system achieved a beam-extraction rate of 86.80% across 409 executed shots. These results demonstrate the engineering feasibility of the framework for supervised sequential tuning on a physical scientific instrument.

articles.title: IGG: A Benchmark for Interactive GUI Grounding under Visibility Constraints
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32536v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: GUI grounding benchmarks ask whether an agent can localize a target that is already visible in a static screenshot. Real interfaces often violate this assumption: a target may be off-screen, appear only after a state change or hover, remain occluded, or become actionable after a delay. This leaves the ability to recover target visibility unevaluated. To measure this reveal step, we introduce Interactive GUI Grounding (IGG), a benchmark in which an agent must first make the target visible through interaction and then click it. IGG contains 601 tasks across 16 controllable GUI environments and seven visibility-constraint sub-types, with a compact action space of scrolling, moving, dragging, waiting, and clicking. In our human study, participants achieve 94.6% accuracy, while GPT-5.5 reaches 79.4% and the strongest evaluated open-source VLM reaches only 31.6%. To identify the source of this gap, we conduct two controlled interventions. Telling Qwen3-VL which interaction to perform raises its accuracy only from 30.8% to 33.9%, whereas performing the interaction for the model raises it to 81.9%. The bottleneck is executing the reveal interaction, not recognizing the target once it is exposed. We further show that this capability is learnable, demonstrating that visibility recovery can be strengthened consistently across model families.

articles.title: A Foundation Model for Policy In-Context Longitudinal Causal Effect Estimation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32863v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Longitudinal causal effect estimation is complicated by time-varying confounding and treatment-confounder feedback loops. Existing methods generally require data-specific nuisance-model fitting, and many are tailored to prespecified treatment sequences or prediction horizons, leading to time-consuming computation at deployment. We introduce *Policy In-Context Longitudinal causal Effect estimation with Prior-data Fitted Networks* (**PICLE-PFN**), the first foundation model for longitudinal causal effect estimation that supports *dynamic* treatment policies. PICLE-PFN represents target policies through in-context history-decision demonstrations, providing a unified interface for a broad class of treatment policies. Pretrained over synthetic data sampled from longitudinal structural causal models, PICLE-PFN amortizes causal effect estimation across datasets, policies, and horizons. Given a new observational dataset and target policy, it directly predicts conditional average potential outcomes (CAPOs) in one forward pass without task-specific training or hyperparameter tuning. Across synthetic and semi-synthetic longitudinal benchmarks, PICLE-PFN achieves competitive RMSE and substantially improved uncertainty calibration with a fraction of deployment runtime, compared to state-of-the-art conventional estimators trained and tuned separately for each dataset.

articles.title: Modifying the Surface of Silica-Coated Magnesium Cobalt Ferrite with Curcumin to Eliminate Pb(II) and Cd(II) from Different Environmental Water Samples
articles.abstract: Water contamination is a crucial ecological concern impacting aquatic ecosystems and human health, particularly because of heavy metals entering water bodies from the industrial, agricultural, and mining activities. To address this, magnesium-doped cobalt ferrite nanoparticles (MgCoFe2O4@SiO2-CPTMS-Cur) were expanded for effective heavy metal removal from wastewater. These nanoparticles were made initially through coprecipitation technique and then were coated with silica and modified with 3-chloropropyltrimethoxysilane (CPTMS) and curcumin (Cur) to improve the adsorption capabilities. The as-synthesized product was fully characterised by FTIR, EDX, XRD, TEM SEM, BET, TGA and VSM, showing a crystalline structure and a porous surface with a BET surface area of 24.176 m2/g. The adsorption experiments showed an effective removal of Lead Pb(II) and Cadmium Cd(II), with a maximum abilities of 259.50 mg/g for Pb(II) and 208.35 mg/g for Cd(II). Kinetic testing revealed that the adsorption followed a second-order kinetic model, despite the Langmuir isotherm model accurately representing the equilibrium data. The adsorption process was endothermic, spontaneous, and beneficial, according to thermodynamic study. Research on regeneration demonstrated the durability and reusability of the composite over four cycles, highlighting its promise as a frugal and operative adsorbent for heavy metal extraction in environmental cleanup. The effective removal of Pb(II) and Cd(II) metal ions from tap, groundwater, and lake water was achieved utilising this innovative adsorbent.

articles.title: Application of Remote Sensing and Geographic Information System in Groundwater Potential Assessment of Palladan, Zaria, Northwestern Nigeria
articles.abstract: Groundwater is an important source of water for domestic, agricultural, and industrial activities, particularly in basement complex terrains where its occurrence is controlled by surface and subsurface geological conditions. This study assessed the groundwater potential of Palladan, Zaria, Northwestern Nigeria, using remote sensing and Geographic Information System (GIS) techniques. Landsat 9 Operational Land Imager (OLI) satellite imagery and Shuttle Radar Topography Mission (SRTM) Digital Elevation Model (DEM) data were acquired and processed to generate thematic layers, including land use/land cover, lineament density, drainage density, and slope. The Landsat 9 imagery was processed using ENVI software, while ArcGIS was employed for spatial analysis, thematic mapping, and integration of the groundwater-influencing factors. Land use/land cover classification was performed using the Maximum Likelihood Classification technique, whereas lineaments were extracted from enhanced satellite imagery using directional filtering and PCI Geomatica. The thematic layers were reclassified according to their relative suitability for groundwater occurrence and integrated using the Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) and weighted overlay techniques to produce a Groundwater Potential Zonation (GWPZ) map. The results revealed that built-up areas constituted approximately 50% of the study area, bare land 33%, vegetation 15%, and water bodies 2%. The AHP analysis assigned the highest weight to slope (0.5016), followed by drainage density (0.2630), land use/land cover (0.1591), and lineament density (0.0768), with a consistency ratio of 0.051. The resulting groundwater potential assessment identified areas of varying groundwater suitability, with approximately 60% of the study area classified within good to excellent groundwater potential zones. These zones were predominantly associated with gentle slopes, high lineament density, low drainage density, and favourable land cover conditions.

articles.title: The RegTech Paradox: Balancing Compliance Costs and Digital Synergies in Indian Banking
articles.abstract: This study empirically investigates the impact of regulatory technology (RegTech) adoption on the financial performance of Indian commercial banks. Utilizing a comprehensive panel dataset of 32 listed banks from 2016 to 2025, the research employs Python-based text-mining techniques on published annual reports to construct a novel RegTech adoption index, which is bifurcated into Core Regulatory Technology and RegTech Enabling Technology. To account for the dynamic persistence of bank profitability and resolve potential endogeneity issues, the study utilizes a two-step System GMM estimator alongside baseline Random Effects modeling. The empirical results reveal a significant asymmetrical relationship. Investments in RegTech Enabling Technology such as artificial intelligence and big data yield a strong, positive, and statistically significant enhancement to the Return on Assets (ROA). Conversely, Core Regulatory Technology dedicated strictly to automated compliance acts primarily as a mandatory operational safeguard, demonstrating a statistically insignificant impact on overall profitability. Furthermore, heterogeneity analysis uncovers that the financial benefits of foundational enabling technologies are heavily concentrated among large institutions and private sector banks, whereas the substantial capital expenditures required for core compliance systems actively compress the asset returns of large banks. These core findings are rigorously validated through extensive robustness checks, including the use of alternative dependent variables (ROE), lagged effects, outlier removal, and a Monte Carlo placebo test. Ultimately, this research provides vital strategic insights for bank management and policymakers regarding the operational costs and monetization potential of digital compliance infrastructures.

articles.title: Microstructure Evolution and Synergistic Optimization of Mechanical Properties and Thermal Conductivity in Mg-xSn-0.2Ca-0.5Zr Alloys
articles.abstract: To address the challenge of the trade-off between mechanical properties and thermal conductivity in magnesium alloys, Mg-xSn-0.2Ca-0.5Zr alloys (x = 3, 4, 5 wt.%) were investigated in this work. Permanent mold casting, semi-solid rheo-die casting, and heat treatment were employed to tailor the microstructure of the alloys. The inherent correlations between microstructure evolution, mechanical properties, and thermal conductivity were systematically explored. The results reveal that as Sn content increases in permanent mold cast alloys, grain refinement occurs and the volume fraction of secondary phases rises. Nevertheless, excessive Sn induces coarsening of grain-boundary Mg2Sn, thereby degrading both ductility and thermal conductivity. Among the permanent mold cast alloys, Mg-4Sn-0.2Ca-0.5Zr exhibits optimal overall performance, with an ultimate tensile strength of 137 MPa, yield strength of 71 MPa, elongation of 7.6%, and thermal conductivity of 86.12 W/(m·K), and is accompanied by the lowest hot-tearing susceptibility. Near-spherical α-Mg grains are obtained in the semi-solid rheo-die cast Mg-4Sn-0.2Ca-0.5Zr alloy. After T6 heat treatment, fine Mg2Sn precipitates are dispersed throughout the matrix. The ultimate tensile strength, yield strength, and elongation are improved to 202 MPa, 112 MPa, and 11.7%, respectively. Meanwhile, aging facilitates the precipitation of Sn from the α-Mg matrix and reduces electron scattering, contributing to an elevated thermal conductivity of 110.68 W/(m·K). Regulation of the solidification microstructure enables the simultaneous enhancement of strength, ductility, and thermal conductivity for Mg-Sn-Ca-Zr alloys.

articles.title: Synthesis, Structural Studies and Cytotoxic Activity of six Novel Mononuclear Metal(II) Complexes with a Tridentate N3-Donor Schiff Based Ligand
articles.abstract: In this work, Six mononuclear novel metal complexes with octahedral geometry were synthesized using the tridentate N3-donor Schiff base ligand N′-Phenyl-N″(phenyl(pyridin-2-yl)methylene)ethane-1,2-diamine (L) and the general formula of the six complexes is [M(L)2](ClO4)2. 2H2O (M = Cu, Ni, Mn, Co, Zn and Cd). Their structures and properties were characterized by elemental analysis, IR, mass and electronic spectroscopy, conductivity measurements and magnetic studies. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction analysis revealed that [Ni(L)2](ClO4)2.2H2O and [Zn(L)2](ClO4)2.2H2O complexes have distorted octahedral coordination around the metal center. Cytotoxic activity of the all complexes showed dose depended toxicity and among them Cu(II) and Mn(II) complexes have very low IC50 value.

articles.title: Representation-Covariant Scale Exponents under Fisher-Induced Whitening: Identifiability, Profile Likelihood, and Adaptive Estimation
articles.abstract: The KA (Kerimov--Alekberli) model posits that Fisher Information spectral projections obey a Generalized Gaussian Distribution (GGD) whose scale and shape parameters follow power laws of the corresponding eigenvalue, with exponents ν and α. We characterise which exponents are representation-covariant artefacts under Fisher-induced whitening and which are intrinsic. Proposition~1 establishes an exact, finite-sample, distribution-free identity: the OLS estimate of ν shifts by exactly~1/2 under whitening, for any data and any shape parameter. Theorem~1 extends this to the profile likelihood: the profile log-likelihood is equivariant under whitening, so the profile MLE satisfies hnu^P_w = hnu^Pᵣₐw + 1/2 and halpha^P_w = halpha^Pᵣₐw exactly. Thus α is representation-invariant; ν is representation-covariant with a universal +1/2 shift. and power 1.00 for α≥ 0.20. A Monte Carlo benchmark over 360 cells (36,000 runs) confirms all results at machine precision: Gate~1 maximum deviation ≤ 5.6× 10⁻⁹; profile RMSE 4--8× smaller than OLS. The BIS demonstration validates pipeline executability only; the LLM-0 protocol is a prospective specification for future empirical work.

articles.title: Climatological Characteristics and Mechanisms of the South China Sea Winter Monsoon Onset
articles.abstract: The South China Sea Winter Monsoon (SCSWM) plays an important role in shaping the physical environment and ecosystem in the South China Sea (SCS). Based on pentad-averaged data from 1980 to 2024, this study found that the transition from the SCS summer monsoon to the winter monsoon progresses from north to south, at a rate comparable to that of the reverse transition. Therefore, analogous to the established term “SCS Summer Monsoon onset”, the establishment of the SCS winter monsoon can be referred to as “SCSWM onset”. The onset time of the SCSWM can be defined as the first pentad when the northeasterlies are established over the deeper sea in the central SCS (8°–18°N, 110°–119°E), with a climatological mean onset around pentad 57 in early October. Further analyses reveal that the southward migration of the deep atmospheric convection center from the Philippine Islands to Borneo is the dominant mechanism governing the SCSWM onset. This migration is primarily driven by the seasonal southward shift in solar radiation during boreal autumn. Positive (negative) sea surface temperature (SST) anomalies around the Philippine Islands in late August to early September enhance (weaken) local convection, thereby contributing to a later (earlier) SCSWM onset. These local SST anomalies can be traced to the tropical Atlantic SST anomalies in early boreal summer, providing new insights into the mechanisms and potential predictors for the SCSWM onset.

articles.title: SoFIC Orchestrates Physical Barriers and Metabolic Homeostasis to Counter Phage Infection
articles.abstract: Bacteria have evolved numerous defense systems to counter persistent phage infections. In this study, we characterize SoFIC, a protein encoded by E. coli E5 that catalyzes various post-translational modifications and coordinates a multilayed antiviral defense system by reshaping extrabacterial barriers and intracellular metabolism. Our results show that SoFIC is widely distributed across multiple bacterial phyla (particularly Proteobacteria) and exhibits diverse domain architectures; nonetheless, all variants contain a conserved Fic catalytic motif essential for anti-phage activity. Using the native host E. coli E5 and its cognate short-tailed phage DE5 as a model, knockout and complementation experiments demonstrated that the anti-phage function of SoFIC requires an intact Fic catalytic motif. Extracellularly, SoFIC physically hinders initial phage adsorption by maintaining surface structures such as fimbriae and biofilms. Intracellularly, once phages breach this barrier, SoFIC specifically interacts with key host proteins involved in DNA homeostasis (HupA, SbmC), transcription elongation (NusB), nucleotide metabolism (PyrB), and oxidative stress defense (Bfr, MsrA), preventing the host cell from entering a metabolic state conductive to phage proliferation. Furthermore, SoFIC exhibits time-dependent functional interactions with multiple endogenous defense systems, including Septu I, RM III, PsyrTA and Retron VI, collectively enhancing host immunity. Taken together, this study establishes SoFIC as a central coordinator of both physical and physiological antiviral barriers, reveals an extracellular and intracellular dual-layer defense model, and positions SoFIC as a key node in the multilayered bacterial immune network. These findings provide a theoretical basis for understanding the defense mechanisms of Fic family proteins and offer fundamental insights for engineering phage-resistant bacterial chassis.

articles.title: Green ZnO NPs from Trichoderma and Their Effects on Zucchini and Beet
articles.abstract: Zinc oxide nanoparticles (ZnO NPs) are promising nano-fertilizers for improving zinc delivery and crop performance. This study investigated the biogenic synthesis of ZnO NPs using Trichoderma and evaluated their effects on seed germination and early seedling growth of zucchini (Cucurbita pepo L.) and beet (Beta vulgaris L.). Fourteen Trichoderma isolates were recovered from rhizosphere soils across ten Egyptian governorates and characterized morphologically and by ITS analysis. Most isolates were identified as Trichoderma harzianum. Five isolates (1, 2, 4, 6, and 9) showed superior ZnO biosynthesis, and T. harzianum MNF-SHS-Tricho 9 was selected for optimization. Maximum production was obtained using 10 mL cell-free culture filtrate with 5 mM zinc acetate at pH 8 and 28°C. ZnO NP formation and zinc and oxygen composition were confirmed by UV–Vis, FTIR, and EDX analyses. Transmission electron microscopy showed spherical nanoparticles with a mean size of 60.99 ± 26.12 nm. Dynamic light scattering indicated a hydrodynamic diameter of 1038 nm and a high polydispersity index (0.737), reflecting aggregation, consistent with the weak negative zeta potential (− 6.92 ± 3.21 mV). Seed germination and seedling growth showed concentration-dependent responses, with 5 mM ZnO NPs producing favorable effects. In zucchini, seedling vigor index and germination rate increased to 51.0 and 17.4, respectively, compared with 29.7 and 13.4 in controls. In beet, corresponding values increased to 33.3 and 8.5 versus 21.8 and 7.3. Higher concentrations reduced germination and seedling vigor. These findings demonstrate the potential of T. harzianum-mediated ZnO NPs as biological nano-zinc inputs for early crop development.

articles.title: Spectroscopic, Light-Harvesting, and Quantum Mechanical Studies of a TDMIM·BF 4 Ionic Liquid Crystal-ZnO Cluster Hybrid for Dye-Sensitized Solar Cells
articles.abstract: Context- The present study reports a comprehensive theoretical investigation of the spectroscopic, light-harvesting, and quantum mechanical properties of a novel hybrid system consisting the ionic liquid crystal (ILC) 1-tetradecyl-3-methylimidazolium tetrafluoroborate (TDMIM·BF₄, C₁₄MIM·BF₄) and ZnO clusters. The hybrid network architecture combines the electronic properties of the ILC with the semiconducting characteristics of ZnO, with the aim of improving the performance of dye-sensitized solar cells (DSSCs). Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations were performed to investigate the structural stability, electronic structure, and optoelectronic behaviour of the TDMIM·BF4-ZnO hybrid conformations. The influence of ZnO incorporation on the structural, electronic, spectroscopic, and optoelectronic properties of the ILC-ZnO hybrid conformations was investigated. Particular attention was given to changes in the electronic distribution and charge-transfer characteristics using frontier molecular orbital (FMO) analysis and energy-gap calculations, while molecular electrostatic potential (MESP) and work-function analyses were employed to examine the modified surface electronic environment and charge-transport characteristics. The photovoltaic relevance of the hybrid systems was further examined through light-harvesting efficiency (LHE), open-circuit voltage (Vₒc), and fill factor (FF) under AM 1.5G solar irradiation. The study provides insight into the role of ZnO incorporation in enhancing the optical and electronic characteristics of TDMIM·BF₄ and its potential applicability in the design of hybrid DSSC materials.Methods- Density functional theory (DFT) calculations were performed using Gaussian 09 to optimize C14MIM.BF4, ZnO clusters, and C14MIM.BF4-(ZnO)ₙ (n = 2–8) hybrid conformations. Geometry optimizations were carried out using the B3LYP functional with the 6-311 + + G(d,p) basis set for H, C, N, O, and F atoms, while the LANL2DZ effective core potential was employed for Zn.

articles.title: Theoretical prediction of masses and decay constants of bottomonium and bottom-charm mesons with spin dependent Cornell potential
articles.abstract: We investigate the bound-state spectrum and decay properties of mesons using a spin-dependent Cornell potential within first-order perturbation theory. Analytical expressions for the energy eigenvalues are obtained, and the model is validated by considering the spin-independent limit, where the results reproduce the standard Cornell potential spectrum and show good agreement with existing calculations based on artificial neural networks, the asymptotic iteration method, and the matrix Numerov approach. The parameters of the spin-dependent potential are determined by fitting the resulting analytical mass-spectrum equation to experimental data. These parameters are then used to calculate the masses and decay properties of bottomonium and bottom-charm mesons for low-lying quantum states. For the bottomonium states, an average percentage absolute deviation of approximately 0.15% from the experimental masses is obtained, demonstrating an improvement over several previous theoretical predictions while the bottom-charm masses aligned with other theoretic values in the literature. The vector and pseudoscalar decay constants are calculated from the corresponding wave functions at the origin and exhibit a decreasing behavior with increasing principal quantum number, The pseudoscalar di-photon and vector leptonic decay widths are subsequently evaluated using the leading and first-order Van Royen–Weisskopf formula. The predicted decay constants are found to be generally consistent with available experimental data and previous theoretical results. Furthermore, incorporating the QCD running strong coupling at appropriate renormalization scales improves the description of the decay properties, emphasizing the sensitivity to the wave function at the origin. The results demonstrate that the perturbative spin-dependent Cornell potential provides a simple and effective phenomenological framework for describing the mass spectra and decay properties of bottomonium and bottom-charm mesons.

articles.title: Auditable Corridor Shortlisting under Partial Observability: A Systems Approach to Ranking Human Trafficking Origin–Destination Links
articles.abstract: International human trafficking is only partially observed at the corridor level: a small number of origin–destination (OD) pairs appear in public victim-case compilations, while the space of possible corridors is vast. We treat corridor pri-oritization as a systems problem and present an auditable ranking loop that maps sparse observed ODs, country-level covariates, and an explicit graph representation into a shortlist of corridors for subsequent review. The system couples three inference pathways (tabular attributes, graph neural message passing, and a temporal world model) under a frozen holdout and hard-matched negatives. Assurance is provided by a falsification battery (label destruction, structural nulls, graph rewiring, world-model ablations), calibration diagnostics, multi-seed stability checks, and prospective recovery of Counter-Trafficking Data Collabo-rative (CTDC) corridors first observed after year cuts. Across three seeds, the core battery passes on average 6.33 of 8 controls; graph-rewire tests pass on one of three seeds and are reported as unstable, and world-model interventions pass only on training-loss gaps. The tabular pathway is the strongest ranker (edge precision–recall area under the curve, PR-AUC, 0.59 ± 0.17 versus 0.48 ± 0.10 for the graph neural network), but test splits contain roughly a dozen positives and seed variance is large. In prospective recovery, tabular recall@20 averages 0.50 over seeds and cuts, against chance PR-AUC of 0.25–0.37. The deliverable is not a certified map of trafficking routes but a reproducible shortlist with an attached verification record, designed to interface with external review.

articles.title: Wide-Swath Altimetry over Rivers Reveals Natural and Regulated Seasonality Patterns Globally
articles.abstract: The seasonal pulse of rivers migrates across the planet, shaped by atmospheric circulation, basin memory and human control, with river discharge carrying this movement along valley corridors globally. Three years of the Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) mission global discharge product reveal these dynamics, their reorganization by climate teleconnections, and disruption by regulation. Seasonal activation emerges and evolves through the year: tropical activation reaches +64% above the annual mean in the northern Amazon and monsoon activation +52% in the Ganges in 2024. These patterns are undersampled by sparse and transboundary in-situ networks; SWOT's dense sampling reveals a misrepresentation of basin dynamics of up to 27%. The SWOT period spans the transition from the strong 2023 El Niño to neutral and La Niña conditions in 2025, when seasonal discharge shifts by roughly twice its typical year-to-year variation in the northern Amazon-Orinoco system, while the strengthening 2025 La Niña drives the Congo down by about four-fifths of a typical year's variation. SWOT further exposes where regulation breaks seasonal regimes: the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam delays the Blue Nile by 2.8 months and dampens it by 46%, while the Aswan High Dam shifts the downstream Nile by 6 months and dampens it by 59%. SWOT thus opens a new view of the global river network, following water movement as it emerges, shifts, and is interrupted across continents.

articles.title: Influence of Crystallographic and Microstructural Features on Magneto-crystalline Anisotropy and Magnetization Reversal in Al-Doped Ni Thin Films
articles.abstract: The role of controlled doping in tuning magneto-crystalline anisotropy and magnetization reversal in polycrystalline Ni nanocomposite thin films through crystallographic and microstructural modification remains inadequately addressed. This study examines magnetron-sputtered Al-doped Ni thin films containing 0, 2, 3, and 5 wt.% Al deposited on Si/SiO₂ substrates. Al incorporation progressively contracts the Ni lattice and refines the crystallite size while increasing microstrain, dislocation density, and mosaic spread, collectively degrading the crystallographic texture. These structural changes arise from substitutional lattice distortion and solute-limited adatom mobility, which suppress grain growth and promote re-nucleation. XRR and AFM further show that Al reduces film density and produces a non-monotonic surface roughness, with the smoothest and most uniform surface at the intermediate composition. The resulting magnetic behavior is non-monotonic. The undoped film exhibits a preferred 0° direction with a loop displacement of approximately 48 Oe, arising from interfacial exchange coupling with a naturally formed antiferromagnetic NiO layer. At 5 wt.% Al, the balance between reduced pinning and moderate structural disorder produces the most favorable response, with the lowest easy-axis coercivity (80.0 ± 0.5 Oe), highest squareness (0.708 ± 0.003), and highest initial susceptibility (0.0208 ± 0.0005 Oe⁻¹). Beyond this optimum, excessive lattice strain and defect accumulation broaden the distribution of local switching fields, increasing coercivity to 128.0 ± 0.5 Oe and promoting multistep reversal. The results further show that coercivity deviates from classical grain-size scaling and is governed more strongly by mosaic spread and defect density, while surface roughness limits the low-field susceptibility. These findings demonstrate that moderate Al incorporation provides effective control over magnetic anisotropy and reversal, whereas excessive doping destabilizes the reversal pathway through disorder-dominated pinning.

articles.title: Finite-copy optimal cloning of mixed qudit states: exact optima, a closed-form cloner, and the structure of covariant sector channels
articles.abstract: Copying is the most basic operation on information, and the no-cloning theorem is the sharpest statement of how quantum information differs from classical. The best approximate copier of pure states has been known for decades, and the asymptotic theory of cloning mixed states at fixed gain γ=m/n was recently completed by Schur--Weyl methods, which give closed-form limiting fidelities and an asymptotically optimal ``Schur--Cartan'' cloner. Whether those constructions are also good at the finite copy numbers available in experiments, and what the finite-copy optimum is, was unknown. We show that the finite-copy optimum is a concave program over Young-label transition rules and extremal covariant maps between irreducible sectors, solve it exactly for qubits up to n=40 and for qutrits and ququarts at small n, and show that the asymptotically optimal cloners lose up to 0.11 in root fidelity at nle 20, while purify--clone--trace fails at the degenerate spectrum. The loss is entirely in the label rule: the Cartan sector channel is finite-copy optimal for qubits, and in higher dimension it coincides with the lowest-Casimir (minimal Parthasarathy--Ranga Rao--Varadarajan) component, which is within 10⁻³ of optimal. A closed-form cloner, a Knothe--Rosenblatt coupling of the input and target label laws followed by lowest-Casimir channels, is asymptotically optimal, improves the Schur--Cartan cloner by up to 0.115, and comes with Karush--Kuhn--Tucker and Frank--Wolfe certificates bracketing the true optimum to 10⁻³ without semidefinite programming. The analysis isolates a single representation-theoretic question, the pairwise optimality of the PRV channel at intermediate spectral mixedness, settled here in the cold and hot limits and for single-copy inputs, which governs how much coherent cloning advantage survives at the copy numbers of near-term quantum networks.

articles.title: Physics-Informed Explainable Machine Learning for Predicting Wavelength- Dependent Optical Modulation of Neuronal Activity
articles.abstract: Wavelength-dependent optical stimulation may also be a potential method for non-invasive modulation of neural activity, but the effects of this stimulation are controlled by a series of factors that include the energy of the photons, the optical properties of the tissue, the optical dose delivered, wavelength sensitivity, and neuronal characteristics. This work introduces a physics-informed machine learning framework to explore the responses of neurons across different wavelengths and to measure predictive uncertainty, in an explainable manner. Two optical features derived from experimental measurements and physics modelling were combined with the biological sensitivity descriptors and tested on a data set of 100,000 samples across two subsets of neuronal phenotypes and across a 400–700 nm wavelength range using multiple regression models. Wavelength grouped validation and locked test set were used in model evaluation. Using the full mechanistic feature set increased the locked-test coefficient of determination (:R²) from 0.012 for the data-only feature set to 0.035, and the RMSE and MAE for primary endpoint: percentage change in firing rate were 8.00 percentage points and 6.35 percentage points, respectively. The modest increase in predictive value from the mechanistic features suggests incremental value, but the modest (:R²) suggests that there was still significant variation in firing-rate modulation that wasn't predicted. Explainability analysis revealed that the most important predictive features were photo-modulation gain, biological optical dose, wavelength sensitivity, tissue scattering, and peak wavelength. Predictive performance was endpoint dependent; the modulation of membrane-potential was the best with (:R²) 0.388. Split-conformal calibration resulted in an empirical coverage of 90.2% for nominal 90% prediction intervals, whereas increasing the input noise resulted in a reduced performance of the model. In summary, the framework allows for an interpretable computational method to investigate neuronal responses across all wavelengths, to characterize endpoint-specific predictability and to assess uncertainty. It needs to be validated by independent experiments to determine its generalizability to real neuronal systems.

articles.title: Deposit-Architecture-Dependent Trade-Off Between High-Temperature Wear and Chloride Corrosion of Electroless Ni-P-B And Ni-P-B-W Coatings
articles.abstract: Electroless Ni-P-B (ENPB) and phosphorus-graded Ni-P-B-W (ENPBW) coatings were examined to determine how tungstate-induced changes in deposit architecture couple interfacial damage accommodation with electrochemical protection. Previously published as-deposited characteristics and room-temperature wear data were used only as referenced baselines. The present work combines post-sliding X-ray diffraction, reciprocating dry sliding at 300°C, static electrochemical testing, post-exposure microscopy, apparent water-contact-angle measurements, and comparative tribo-electrochemical testing in 3.5 wt. % NaCl. At 300°C, ENPBW reduced the mean coefficient of friction from 0.505 ± 0.10 to 0.415 ± 0.12 and the specific wear rate from 18.5 × 10− 5 to 13.9 × 10− 5 mm3 N− 1 m− 1 relative to ENPB. Static polarization produced the opposite ranking: ENPB exhibited Ecorr = -0.289 V versus Ag/AgCl and icorr = 0.0411 µA cm− 2, compared with − 0.342 V and 0.851 µA cm− 2 for ENPBW. During sliding in NaCl, ENPB also showed a smaller cathodic potential excursion and more complete post-sliding recovery. The opposing rankings reveal a bath- and architecture-dependent trade-off: hierarchical, chemically graded ENPBW better accommodated high-temperature sliding damage, whereas the finer and more uniformly covered ENPB surface provided the more favorable electrochemical response. Because the independent material-loss terms required by ASTM G119 were not measured, the tribo-electrochemical results constitute a comparative assessment rather than a quantitative wear-corrosion-synergy analysis.

articles.title: Diamond defects confirm 80-year-old theory of crystal stress
articles.abstract: For the first time, researchers in Japan have directly mapped several components of the stress field surrounding an atomic-scale flaw in the crystal structure of diamond. Led by Tokuyuki Teraji at Japan's National Institute for Materials Science, the team achieved its result using nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond, whose spin states respond differently to stress depending on how they are oriented relative to the stress field.

articles.title: One extra quantum dot helps balance speed and stability in spin qubits
articles.abstract: Quantum computers need qubits that can be controlled both quickly and reliably. Yet making semiconductor spin qubits faster often makes them more sensitive to electrical noise, creating a difficult trade-off.

articles.title: Supercurrent enables the reading of quantum information without destroying it
articles.abstract: One of the fundamental challenges of quantum computing is obtaining information from a quantum bit, or qubit. Unlike a conventional bit, which can be read repeatedly without altering its content, direct measurement of a quantum system typically causes the state to collapse before it can be determined. In other words, reading the information modifies it.

articles.title: Physics consistent conditional flow matching model as a plasma physics surrogate model
articles.abstract: Physics-informed surrogate modeling for steady-state systems often struggles with data scarcity and optimization instabilities from soft penalty losses. Unlike prevailing physics-informed generative methods that rely on explicit, differentiable PDE residuals during training, our framework targets systems where closed-form governing equations are unavailable or non-differentiable. We introduce a unified continuous-time conditional flow matching (CFM) framework for surrogate modeling and sparse data assimilation, evaluated on low-temperature plasma dynamics. By combining data-dependent interpolants with dynamic masking, our approach handles unconditioned prediction and missing-data imputation within a single architecture. We replace standard velocity matching with a direct state-prediction ( -prediction) objective, eliminating variance-induced sampling inefficiencies in deterministic regimes. For inference, the formulation supports both time-dependent ODE integration (CFM- ) and an autonomous regime (CFM- ) that enables measurement conditioning via anchor substitution. Global conservation laws are enforced via post-hoc geometric projections rather than loss regularizers. Results show that both CFM variants achieve superior accuracy, sample efficiency under data scarcity, and raw physical consistency over standard regressors. Furthermore, macroscopic constraints alone yield negligible reductions in test error, confirming the necessity of a data-driven generative prior over the physical manifold.

articles.title: Lattice Symmetry Remnants in Spatial and Temporal Entanglement of Quantum Critical Spin Chains
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31676v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum critical lattice models carry universal information beyond the bulk data of their infrared conformal field theory (CFT): microscopic lattice symmetries constrain how the CFT is realized. We probe these remnants through the spatial and temporal entanglement of two Euclidean-evolved states from the same critical model. In the finite-length scaling regime, a conformal boundary encodes the long-distance effect of the short-range initial state, and boundary CFT (BCFT) organizes the universal low-lying entanglement spectrum. We formulate the temporal state as a uniform infinite matrix product state evolved by a symmetry-preserving infinite matrix product operator, using a local factorization regular even at arbitrarily small Trotter steps. For the Ising and three-state Potts chains, whose relevant symmetries are onsite, the spatial and temporal constructions approach the same BCFT structure; varying the initial state engineers conformal boundaries distinguishable spectroscopically. The spin-1/2 XXZ chain instead realizes a Lieb--Schultz--Mattis (LSM) constraint between internal U(1) symmetry and one-site translation. A U(1)-preserving short-range spatial state accommodates it through a doubled unit cell and inequivalent entanglement cuts, whereas the temporal state remains uniform along Euclidean time. Successive spatial transfer steps pump the temporal entanglement spectrum between translation-related Dirichlet sectors, equivalently between integer and half-integer compact-boson zero modes. Breaking U(1) removes both the zero mode and the alternation. Continued evolution at fixed bond dimension crosses over from the finite-length BCFT regime to a finite-entanglement regime generated by symmetry-allowed relevant deformations. Thus microscopic symmetry and anomaly data remain visible in universal entanglement by constraining the boundary realization of the infrared CFT.

articles.title: Nonadiabatic vibrational dynamics of CO on Pt(111) studied with first-principles many-body perturbation theory
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31727v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the nonequilibrium vibrational dynamics of CO adsorbed on Pt(111), a prototypical adsorbate-surface system for ultrafast vibrational spectroscopy, using a first-principles framework that combines many-body perturbation theory with density functional theory. Within this methodology we explicitly account for electron-hole pair excitations and electron-mediated phonon-phonon coupling. For the latter mechanism, we evaluate the vertex-correction screening, what constitutes a methodological novelty. Our calculations qualitatively reproduce the transient evolution of the internal stretch vibrational mode observed in femtosecond pump-probe experiments, allowing us to identify in the experimental measurements a small transient blueshift after excitation with a femtosecond laser pulse. As predicted in a previous work, the reduction in the number of electronic states available for electron-phonon coupling when the electronic temperature raises at a group 10 transition metal surface, effectively screens the electron-phonon interaction giving rise to an anomalous transient blue-shift.

articles.title: Low-energy collective electronic excitations in a gold monolayer
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31805v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The low-energy plasmonic properties of a free-standing Au(111) monolayer, frequently referred to as goldene, are investigated by time-dependent density functional theory in the random phase approximation. In the evaluation of dielectric and loss functions the first-principle band structure characterized by a single s-p energy band at the Fermi level is taken into account. In this system with apparently simple band structure around the Fermi surface the calculations show the presence, besides the standard two-dimensional (2D) plasmon mode, at even lower energies of three anomalous branches in the momentum-energy region usually assigned to incoherent electron-hole pairs. This is an unexpected result since the electronic system of the gold monolayer is characterized by a single energy band crossing the Fermi level. The dispersion of these anomalous plasmonic branches is strongly anisotropic in-plane and gapless. A general feature is that at small in-plane momentum transfers the modes have a sound-like dispersion in certain momentum directions. We rely the appearance of these anomalous modes to a notable deviation of the Fermi surface of a gold monolayer from a circular shape. As a result of its almost perfect hexagon shape, there is possibility to realize in a it single electronic energy band a scenario of a multi-component electron system with the carrier groups moving with different Fermi velocities in certain momentum directions. The found modes correspond to the out-of-phase charge oscillations of the carriers at different sides of the hexagonal Fermi surface. Hence our work presents evidence how in a metal system with apparently simple band structure around the Fermi level its shape can result in conversion of single-particle charge excitations into collective charge excitations.

articles.title: 'Dancing' two-dimensional patterns in nematics above the flexoelectric instability threshold
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31849v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Various types of electrohydrodynamic instabilities in liquid crystals (LCs) are a recurring theme in LC research. The nonlinear stage of the flexoelectric instability in nematics remains the least studied aspect of this phenomenon. This work highlights a key advancement in nonlinear physics, providing a compelling example of nonlinear dynamical system behavior. By solving the system of nonlinear equations for a nematic in an alternating external field, we derive from first principles the unique "dancing" behavior of truly two-dimensional patterns above the flexoelectric instability threshold. Our analysis is restricted to liquid crystals with negative dielectric permittivity and electrical conductivity anisotropies. The resulting solution represents a stable limit cycle near above the Hopf bifurcation, valid within the parameters range where the solutions characteristic exponent is complex. The generalized two-dimensional Ginzburg-Landau-like phenomenological theory of the phenomenon is developed.

articles.title: Strontium Titanate Capping Layers as Kinetic Regulators of Redox Phase Transitions in Oxide Heterostructures
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31871v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Oxide capping layers are widely used to protect and stabilize thin-film heterostructures, yet their role in governing phase-transition kinetics remains largely unexplored. Here, we uncover the kinetic function of few-nanometer-thick SrTiO₃ (STO) capping layers in controlling oxidation and reduction processes, using real-time in situ optical spectroscopic ellipsometry. We show that oxygen diffusion through the nanoscale capping layer constitutes the rate-limiting step, giving rise to diffusion-controlled phase transitions in the underlying materials. As a result, both capping-layer thickness and oxygen partial pressure provide effective handles to tune phase transition temperatures. Quantitative analysis yields an activation energy of E_A = 0.64 ±0.06 eV for oxygen diffusion through STO, highlighting its suitability for precise control of redox reactions in diverse material systems. These results establish oxide capping layers as active kinetic regulators of redox-driven phase transitions and offer a general framework for engineering redox dynamics in complex oxide heterostructures.

articles.title: Poly(vinylidene fluoride) under finite electric displacement fields: a removable α!→!δ reorientation barrier and a persistent first-order δ!→!β conformational change
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31926v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The α, δ, and β phases of PVDF are interconverted by electrical poling and mechanical drawing, yet the thermodynamics under a controlled electrical boundary condition has not been established from first principles. We evaluate the zero-temperature free energy at fixed electric displacement D from van der Waals density-functional calculations along two constrained coordinates in a common 24-atom cell: a tilt of the gauche C--C bonds that maps antipolar α onto polar δ (cell change <1%), and a backbone torsion that straightens TG⁺TG⁻ chains into all-trans β (chain-repeat strain 10.6%). As D increases from 0 to 0.30~C,m⁻², the lowest homogeneous free energy switches from α to δ at Dc₁=0.046~C,m⁻² and from δ to β at Dc₂=0.157~C,m⁻². At T=0 with domain-wall energy neglected, a δ multidomain state lies 14.3~meV per cell below homogeneous α at every D. A Γ-point harmonic estimate suggests that vibrations reverse this ordering at room temperature. δ and β coexist for 0.11<0.21~C,m⁻² at E^*=0.69~GV,m⁻¹, independent of the screening constant. The tilt barrier falls from 0.66~eV per cell at D=0 to 17~meV at D=0.30~C,m⁻² (below k_BT at 300~K), while the torsion barrier remains 0.66~eV at Dc₂ and 0.34~eV at D=0.30~C,m⁻², so δ→β stays first order. Much of the difference traces to the path effective charge (0.28e for the tilt, 0.18e for the torsion). Scaling shows the tilt barrier would survive with the torsion charge; the smaller torsion charge accounts for about half the barrier it retains. The landscape accounts for why a field produces δ and why β is reached by drawing, and suggests that raising that charge could let a field alone produce β.

articles.title: Nanoscale origin of thermal anisotropy in monoclinic texorpdfstringβ-Ga₂O₃beta-Ga2O3
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31976v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Monoclinic β-Ga₂O₃ is a promising ultra-wide-bandgap semiconductor for power electronics, but its low and anisotropic thermal conductivity limits heat removal, making it a compelling model system for nanoscale thermal transport studies. Here, we demonstrate a pronounced nanoscale enhancement of thermal anisotropy and uncover the underlying phonon mechanism by combining complementary thermal and acoustic spectroscopy techniques with first-principles calculations. Anisotropic thermoreflectance thermometry determines the full thermal-conductivity tensor from angular measurements within the (100), (010), and (001) crystallographic planes. Angle-resolved Brillouin light scattering reveals that low-frequency acoustic phonons exhibit only weak velocity anisotropy, insufficient to account for the measured thermal anisotropy. Frequency-resolved ab initio Green--Kubo calculations show that the bulk anisotropy pattern emerges only when the accumulated conductivity includes phonon modes above 4 THz, whereas the sub 3 THz acoustic contributions are nearly isotropic. Extreme-ultraviolet transient thermal grating spectroscopy reveals that reducing the grating period to 28 nm strongly enhances the in-plane thermal anisotropy, most markedly in the (001) plane, where it reaches nearly twice its macroscopic value. Reconstructed and calculated mean-free-path (MFP) accumulation functions link this enhancement to the stronger directional contrast of short-MFP phonons. Together, these results identify high-frequency, short-MFP phonons as the dominant origin of thermal anisotropy in β-Ga₂O₃, while low-frequency phonons attenuate the directional contrast at macroscopic scales.

articles.title: Heterogeneous superconductivity emerging from a charge-stripe state in kagome lattices
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32097v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Charge density wave (CDW) and superconductivity have long been recognized as competing orders. However, recent achievements establish that the interplay between these two collective electronic phenomena can be more perplexing, with emergent phenomena arising from their cooperation. Here we report a distinctive case of the kagome superconductors CsV3Sb5-xSnx, in which the characteristics of superconductivity evolve in accordance with the form of CDW order. As the triple-Q CDW in CsV3Sb5 transforms to a short-range stripelike CDW at xc = 0.07, a sudden change in superconducting properties occurs concomitantly. A combination of thermodynamic, electrical transport and scanning tunneling microscopy experiments reveals a heterogeneous superconducting state beyond xc: the superconducting gap exhibits pronounced spatial variation, in conformity with a distribution of critical temperature and the resulted superconducting precursor effects. Moreover, abundant normal fluid persists deep into the superconducting state, as evidenced by remnants of electronic specific heat and zero-energy quasiparticle interference. These observations are unrelated to the chemical inhomogeneity and residual strain effect introduced by Sn substitution. Instead, they emulate the phenomenology that a sign-changing superconducting order parameter is subject to strong pair-breaking scattering with the short-range charge stripes and hence reflect the unconventional nature of superconductivity developing inside the charge-stripe state.

articles.title: Material criteria for angular-momentum transfer from twisted photons to photoelectrons
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32121v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the material requirements for transferring the total-angular-momentum (TAM) projection of a twisted photon to the orbital angular momentum (OAM) of a photoelectron emitted from an n-type semiconductor surface. Within a single-valley effective-mass model of surface photoemission, we calculate OAM-resolved spectra for GaAs, InSb, InAs₀.₃₄Sb₀.₆₆, and Hg₀.₇₆Cd₀.₂₄Te irradiated by twisted photons with Laguerre--Gaussian--like momentum profile. The OAM transfer is characterized by the mean electron OAM, its root-mean-squared width, and the fraction of electrons with OAM-projection equal to the photon TAM-projection. Efficient transfer requires the transverse momentum of the conduction electron to be much smaller than the transverse momentum width of the photon, which favors low temperatures, small conduction-band effective masses, and shallow donor levels. GaAs is less favorable within the present model because of its larger effective mass and deeper donor levels. We also discuss the demanding photon-wave packet parameters, possible extensions to Dirac and Weyl semimetals, and post-emission OAM selection. Although the generation of vortex electrons with a vanishing OAM uncertainty via photoemission seems challenging, we argue that it is still possible to generate single-electron vortex states with a finite OAM dispersion.

articles.title: Bose-Einstein condensate in a shell: nonlinear modes and symmetry breaking
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32249v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The state of a quantum particle confined to a spherical surface is commonly described using spherical harmonics, which play a crucial role in solving many scientific problems featuring spherical symmetry. A mean-field description of a system of many interacting quantum particles confined to a spherical shell naturally leads to nonlinear generalizations of spherical harmonics. In this study, we analyze the emergence of such nonlinear modes in a shell-shaped Bose-Einstein condensate with both repulsive and attractive two-particle interactions. We find several classes of nonlinear modes. The first kind is an analytical continuation of a single spherical harmonic or their superposition for nonvanishing atom-atom interaction. Some of these solutions have planar counterparts in the form of Townes solitons and Townes vortices, which either appear stable even in the case of attractive interactions or can be stabilized by three-particle interactions. The second kind originate from symmetry-breaking bifurcations in the case of a repulsive interaction, and therefore have no linear counterparts. Moreover, we demonstrate the existence of a breathing dynamics that oscillates primarily between an unstable soliton and a stable vortex necklace state. Our findings show that the physics of nonlinear matter waves on curved geometries differs substantially from that in planar systems, suggesting the feasibility of observing these unconventional wave patterns experimentally.

articles.title: Existence and Absence of Spin-Glass Phases on Migdal--Kadanoff Hierarchical Lattices: A Complete Classification
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32291v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the Ising spin-glass model on Migdal--Kadanoff (MK) hierarchical lattices, characterized by the fractal dimension d=1+log s/log b, where s and b denote the number of parallel branches and the number of bonds in series within each branch, respectively. For independent Gaussian couplings, we rigorously establish a necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of finite-temperature spin-glass order for arbitrary integers b,sge2. We prove that a finite-temperature spin-glass phase exists whenever [ fracbsqrts left( fracbsqrts(s-1)bs-1 right)s⁻¹<1. ] In particular, this condition holds for all three-dimensional MK hierarchical lattices (d=3, or equivalently s=b²), regardless of the choice of b. Conversely, we prove the absence of finite-temperature spin-glass order for fractal dimensions d<1+log17/log6approx2.58, as well as in the large-b limit for any fixed d<3. In the intermediate regime 1+log17/log6le d<3, we provide a finite-step procedure to determine the presence or absence of spin-glass order, which depends on b and s. Our results provide a complete characterization of finite-temperature spin-glass order on MK hierarchical lattices.

articles.title: Flexo-Photoresponses from First Principles
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32341v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many functionally important materials, such as silicon, possess high-symmetry crystal structures that forbid even-order nonlinear optical responses, thereby limiting their application in e.g., photonics and optoelectronics. Strain gradients can effectively break symmetries, activating otherwise forbidden optical responses. Although such flexo-photoresponses have attracted considerable interest recently, a comprehensive microscopic theoretical framework is still lacking. Here, we develop a first-principles approach that can systematically evaluate a wide range of flexo-photoresponses in realistic materials. By mapping strain gradients to long-wavelength phonons within the established theory of electron-phonon coupling, our approach captures the nonlocal quantum-mechanical effects of lattice deformations on nonlinear optical responses. Applying the framework to prototypical centrosymmetric materials, including Si, cubic rm SrTiO₃, and monolayer black phosphorus, we demonstrate that a strain gradients of 10⁵sim10⁶~rm m⁻¹ can induce flexo-second-harmonic generation and flexo-bulk photovoltaic effects comparable to the intrinsic responses of non-centrosymmetric crystals. Our work establishes a rigorous foundation for strain gradient engineering of light-matter interactions, opening new avenues for nanoscale optomechanics, optoelectronics, and beyond.

articles.title: Strain-tunable van Hove singularity and superconducting dome in monolayer kagome metal CsTi₃Bi₅
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32359v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The recently discovered titanium-based kagome metal CsTi₃Bi₅, which exhibits superconductivity without an accompanying charge density wave, provides an ideal platform to investigate the intrinsic electronic structure and superconductivity. Moreover, it enables the exploration of superconductivity in the two-dimensional limit of the kagome lattice. Here, we systematically investigate the influence of biaxial mechanical strain (ε) on the electronic structure and superconductivity of monolayer CsTi₃Bi₅ using first-principles calculations. We demonstrate that the prominent van Hove singularity (VHS) at the M point can be monotonically tuned to the Fermi level by tensile strain. Furthermore, the superconducting transition temperature T_C exhibits a dome-shaped dependence on strain, reaching a maximum of 3.6 K at an optimal tensile strain of ε=+2%. The average superconducting gap magnitude is 0.35 meV, with an orbital-dependent and anisotropic distribution. Our results provide a detailed understanding of the superconductivity of monolayer CsTi₃Bi₅ and show that strain is an effective, continuous tuning knob for manipulating the electronic structure and superconductivity.

articles.title: Electronic structure of a persistent excitonic fluid far beyond the Mott limit
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32437v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Excitons are conventionally expected to destabilize at high photoexcitation densities, as screening weakens the electron-hole attraction. Recent studies, however, challenge this paradigm, suggesting that excitons generated by strong optical pumping can remain stable even beyond the onset of population inversion. Here, using time- and angle-resolved photoelectron spectroscopy on 2D hybrid perovskites, we provide direct evidence for such a high-density excitonic state, characterized by a distinctive Mexican-hat dispersion. Remarkably, this excitonic band reconstruction endures for orders of magnitude longer than the optical coherence time, revealing a population-sustained electronic structure that survives well into the incoherent regime. The excitonic resonance also persists far beyond optical saturation, at densities where exciton wavefunctions strongly overlap. Our findings reveal a long-lived, high-density quantum fluid of excitons with characteristics reminiscent of a BCS condensate, an electronic structure markedly different from that of the dilute limit.

articles.title: Interplay of Chemical Disorder, Vortex Pinning, and Electron Correlations in the Mechanically Robust Medium-Entropy Alloy Superconductor Nb₀.₄₅Ta₀.₂₅Ti₀.₁₅Hf₀.₁₅
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32449v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Medium and high-entropy alloys have emerged as a promising class of superconducting materials because their intrinsic chemical disorder can simultaneously enhance mechanical robustness and modify superconducting properties. Here, we present a combined experimental and first-principles investigation of the structural, superconducting, electronic, and local lattice-distortion characteristics of the mechanically robust medium-entropy alloy Nb₀.₄₅Ta₀.₂₅Ti₀.₁₅Hf₀.₁₅. The material shows type-II superconductivity with a transition temperature T_Coⁿset approx 7.8 ~K. A high critical current density of J_c = 0.48 × 10⁶~A/cm² is observed, and this is attributed to strong vortex pinning at grain boundaries. Specific-heat analysis indicates a strong electron-phonon coupling (λ = 1.07) with a large isotropic s-wave superconducting gap. Density functional theory calculations explicitly model the intrinsic chemical disorder, predict a stable body-centered cubic phase. These calculations further reveal a metallic electronic structure with substantial Ti- and Ta-derived states at the Fermi level. Additionally, our results quantify a pronounced disorder-induced local lattice distortion (Δ d = 0.086 A), providing a microscopic basis for the experimentally observed enhanced vortex-pinning landscape. Remarkably, the alloy also exhibits an unusually large Kadowaki-Woods ratio, placing it close to the heavy-fermion regime and indicating enhanced electronic correlations beyond conventional alloy superconductors. Our results demonstrate that entropy-engineered chemical disorder can stabilize robust superconductivity, promote strong flux pinning, and induce correlated electronic behavior, establishing refractory medium-entropy alloys as a promising platform for next-generation superconducting materials.

articles.title: Side-Chain Engineering Controls Molecular Packing and Vertical Electron Transport in Discrete n-Type NDI-T2 Oligomers
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32456v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-efficiency vertical charge transport in multilayer organic optoelectronic devices highly depends on molecular structure and arrangement. Using two T2-(NDI-T2)2 conjugated oligomers with ethylhexyl (EH) and octyldodecyl (OD) side chains as a model system, their effects on electron transport are investigated using, among other techniques, atomic force microscopy (AFM), conductive atomic force microscopy (C-AFM), grazing-incidence wide-angle X-ray scattering (GIWAXS), steady-state optical spectroscopy, and time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT) calculations. The oligomers of both materials exhibit relatively disordered structures in the as-cast state, whereas annealing enhances structural order and leads to side-chain-dependent changes in molecular stacking. EH-based films show a smaller annealing-induced photoluminescence shift than OD-based films, suggesting less pronounced stacking and conformational rearrangements, consistent with TDDFT-supported exciton analysis. The current-voltage characteristics are analyzed using the space-charge-limited current (SCLC) model. After annealing, both materials exhibit improved vertical electron mobility. The EH-based films reach a maximum mobility of 1.2 x 10⁻⁴ cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹. The combined results suggest that the shorter EH side chains modify the out-of-plane packing environment and facilitate vertical electron transport. These results establish a structure-property relationship between side-chain structure, molecular order, exciton coupling and vertical mobility, providing a molecular design basis for optimising organic semiconductors through side-chain engineering.

articles.title: Effect of oxygen plasma treatment on the structural and superconducting properties of atomic-layer-deposited NbN thin films
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32529v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Surface oxidation is a common concern for ultrathin NbN superconducting devices, yet which superconducting properties it affects has not been established for films grown by plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition. We expose NbN films about 11.4 nm thick to an O₂ plasma for 0 to 60 s, which oxidizes the surface without etching the film, and characterize the same sample series by X-ray diffraction, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), and transport measurements on 500 nm wide nanowires. XPS of the surface and the underlying layer shows that the plasma converts the surface to Nb₂O₅, whereas the bulk of the treated film is chemically identical to that of the untreated film. Crystalline δ-NbN remains intact. During exposure, the total film thickness rises and saturates between 40 and 60 s, indicating self-limiting surface oxide growth. The normal-state resistivity rises by 21% (dc) and 25% (optical) with the plasma dose, while the critical temperature and transition width are unchanged. The switching current densities of 4.9-6.2 MA/cm² at 4.2 K show no systematic dependence on the plasma dose. Their temperature dependence follows the dirty-limit depairing current of Kupriyanov and Lukichev, and the extrapolated switching currents reach 39-46% of the depairing current calculated from the optical resistivity and diffusion coefficient, in agreement with the width dependence reported for nanowires from the same process. The oxygen signature is confined to temperatures near T_c, where the supercurrent of the treated wires vanishes at least 0.5 K earlier than that of the untreated wire, consistent with a partially oxidized surface layer that acts on the film by the proximity effect. At these doses, oxygen narrows the temperature range of the supercurrent from above but does not systematically reduce the low-temperature current-carrying capacity of the wires.

articles.title: Modification of optical properties in ultrathin ALD-grown NbN layers using oxygen plasma treatment
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32553v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: NbN thin films with a nominal thickness of 10 nm were grown by atomic layer deposition (ALD) on Al₂O₃-buffered Si substrates and treated with oxygen plasma for 0 s (untreated), 20 s, 40 s, and 60 s to investigate oxygen-induced changes in their optical properties. Spectroscopic ellipsometry (SE) measurements were performed before and after oxygen plasma treatment over the ultraviolet-visible-near-infrared (1.24-6.20 eV) and infrared (0.041-0.827 eV) spectral ranges. Film thickness determined by X-ray reflectivity (XRR) was used as a fixed parameter in the optical modeling to extract the dielectric function, optical constants, and effective free-carrier concentration. We observed the emergence of a distinct absorption feature near 4.9 eV following oxygen plasma treatment, consistent with the oxidation of the NbN surface and the resulting change in its optical properties. Increasing the treatment time from 0 to 60 s reduced the effective carrier concentration from 1.20 × 10²² to 1.03 × 10²² cm⁻³ and the effective carrier mobility from 2.44 to 2.27 cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹. The obtained results provide a basis for understanding the effects of oxygen plasma treatment on NbN thin films.

articles.title: Probing the limits of forward screening and inverse design of crystal materials
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32678v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Crystal materials are designed either by screening known crystals for a target property or by generating new crystals with that property. Both routes are judged against public databases of known crystals, but these databases name the same crystal differently. Several materials announced as new by recent generative and autonomous discovery campaigns have since proved to be known phases or close variants of them. The limits of both routes remain unmeasured. Here we probe them by matching the crystals of 55 databases by structure into one self-extending database of 14.6 million crystals and 131.8 million property values, each traced to its source. Only 4.5% of its crystal-property pairs carry a value. To fill the empty pairs, we developed CGTNet, an equivariant graph transformer with state-of-the-art accuracy on several tasks of two public benchmarks. Trained on each task, it forms a library of property models whose predictions we release. The reach of forward screening has been underestimated. Known crystals hold tens of thousands of ultra-incompressible candidates without a recorded bulk modulus, and a post hoc audit of synthesis evidence finds among them ReN2, whose bulk modulus was measured at 428 GPa. The novelty claimed for inverse design has been overestimated. At an equal verification budget, a stiffness-conditioned generator returned more stiff hits than screening (100 versus 55), but all contained osmium and 82 repeated recorded compositions. Integrating and completing the databases of known crystals therefore moves the limits of both routes: it widens what screening can reach and sets the reference against which generated crystals are judged new.

articles.title: On the Spontaneous Structural Reconstructions of Chalcogen-Depleted MoS₂, MoSe₂, and Janus MoSSe Monolayers
