Furthermore, we find that spatial correlations in atomic movements across many unit cells play an important role in determining both the static electro-optic coefficient and its attenuation frequency. We tested this hypothesis in tetragonal BaTiO3, where the electro-optic coefficient is experimentally well determined. Molecular-dynamics simulations using a machine-learned HSE potential give a low-frequency electro-optic coefficient of 590 pm/V and an attenuation frequency of approximately 137 GHz, both comparable to the experimental values.

articles.title: The Partial-Accelerator Picture of Magnetic Reconnection in Solar Flares: Four Results from Order-of-Magnitude Physics
articles.abstract: We apply the competing-balance methodology of order-of-magnitude physics to particle acceleration and radiation in solar-flare magnetic reconnection, taking as the unifying basis the fact that flare-accelerated electrons are only a few percent of the total electron population. Four results follow. (1) An explicit scaling of the thick–thin transition energy with plasma beta, Ec ∝ β1/2 B L1/2 T−1/2. (2) An energy-budget check showing that in the best-measured events the nonthermal electrons carry only ~10−3 of the released magnetic energy, so the percent-level efficiency is a supply problem rather than an energy problem. (3) A closure test: with the magnetic field and the reconnection electric field taken from direct measurements, MA ≈ 2 × 10−2 follows, and requiring the inflow to supply the fitted nonthermal injection rate fixes the supply area at 1.3 × 1019 and 8.7 × 1018 cm2—regions 35 and 29 Mm across, i.e. areas agreeing to a factor of 1.45. The constraint on beta is one-sided, since low beta facilitates collisionless reconnection; what replaces the withdrawn lower limit is a budget requirement rather than a ceiling, driving a low-beta source to β ~ 1 calling for the local dissipation of about three quarters of its magnetic energy density. In this reading β is an output of the flare, which quenches its own reconnection once the heated plasma reaches the pinching threshold. (4) A supply-limited Fermi scaling of the hard X-ray photon index, γ − 2 ∝ (MA/10−2)−(q−p), whose normalisation agrees with the fitted kappa index to within a factor of three, which reproduces the slope of the published cross-event regression and predicts its curvature, and which predicts that q − p is of order unity across events but vanishes in time within one event. The results are self-consistent to within one order of magnitude and yield five falsifiable predictions.

articles.title: Neutral Morphological Masking: Constructive Neutral Evolution of Chiral Scaffolds for Information-Maintaining Artificial Cells
articles.abstract: A minimal synthetic cell that completes a full replication–growth–division cycle still demonstrates nothing about self-maintenance unless it also carries a state variable that can degrade under a genuine environmental stress and be actively defended. Our earlier proposal (Sandler, 2026b) specified such a module — chiral order Uχ as a programmable memory, D-glucose glycation as a stress channel, and circular dichroism (CD) as a sensor — but treated the robustness that protects Uχ as a static, hand-designed surface property, uₛ. That is an adaptationist assumption dressed as an engineering parameter, and it is also why the initial submission read as disconnected from current artificial-life research: a designed robustness knob does not need to cite the literature on how robustness actually arises in living systems. This revision addresses both problems by fusing the chiral-order module with Constructive Neutral Evolution (CNE), the framework in which biological complexity accumulates through selectively neutral steps rather than adaptive design (Stoltzfus, 1999), and specifically with the interlocking-masking mechanism recently formalized for multi-subunit complexes in the Quandary Den artificial-life model (Walsh, 2026). In the synthesized framework, random neutral mutations introduce structural protrusions in one subunit of a multi-subunit chiral scaffold; complementary recesses that neutrally arise in partner subunits mask these protrusions to preserve packing order, and the accumulated interlocking geometry incidentally occludes the scaffold's glycation-vulnerable amine sites. Geometric surface uniformity, uₛ, is therefore reframed as an emergent, unselected byproduct of a masking ratchet rather than a design input. We give the resulting multi-subunit dynamical system, retain the original module's mechanistic lattice Monte Carlo and site-diluted XY-model machinery as validation of the underlying stress–state–repair physics, and add a new toy evolutionary simulation demonstrating the internal consequences of the proposed masking rules: a one-directional ratchet in interlocking complexity, an incidental decline in the emergent glycation-rate constant, and accidental cross-protection against a novel stress shock in lineages that accumulated complexity under no direct selection for glycation resistance. We situate the proposal explicitly against current artificial-life and synthetic-biology literature on self-maintaining and homeostatic artificial cells, give an expanded, falsifiable prediction set, and lay out a staged validation roadmap.

articles.title: Satoyama destruction and homogeneity as sources of environmental vulnerability in Tokyo
articles.abstract: Satoyama are marginal areas located between foothills and arable land in Japan. These landscapes support a wide range of species and are regarded as indicators of biodiversity and sustainable agriculture. However, deforestation in these areas has increasingly threatened local ecosystems. This study examined the ecological and environmental effects of Satoyama degradation and urban landscape homogenisation in Tokyo and surrounding areas using a “surface-to-line” analytical framework. Landscape analysis showed reductions in forested and vegetated areas between 1976 and 2024, accompanied by increased urban development and the expansion of concrete-covered surfaces. Meteorological data indicated increasing temperatures and declining humidity in Tokyo since the 1990s. Field observations showed altered behaviour of Japanese pygmy woodpeckers following the removal of large trees. Overall, current urban-development and land-management practices contribute to increasing ecological and landscape homogeneity, potentially reducing environmental resilience. The findings suggest that development projects in Satoyama may be deviating from their original social and ecological purposes.

articles.title: Mn-Driven Structural Modulation and PANI-Assisted Charge Transfer in WO₃-Based Supercapacitor Electrodes
articles.abstract: Electrodes with fast kinetics of electron transfer, many electrochemically active sites and stable structure are needed for fabrication of highly efficient electrochemical energy storage devices. Tungsten oxide (WO₃) can be considered as potential pseudocapacitive material; but rather low electrical conductivity and restricted number of active sites negatively influence on electrochemical properties of this compound. In our work, Mn-doped tungsten oxide nanomaterials were fabricated and studied as electrode materials for supercapacitors. The formation of highly crystalline tungsten oxide with monoclinic structure was proved by X-ray diffraction studies, while the presence of Mn in tungsten oxide structure was confirmed by the structural and vibrational characteristics, observed in FTIR spectroscopy, namely W–O, W = O and Mn–O bonds. The results of electron microscopy studies showed that the particles were uniformly dispersed, with average particle size of 19.86 nm. It should be noted that the electrode showed a high specific capacitance value of 1756 F g⁻¹ with 1 A g⁻¹ current density, along with an energy density of 61 Wh kg⁻¹ and a power density of 1784 W kg⁻¹. Additionally, cycling stability was evident for the electrode, which indicates the capability of the material to function properly in terms of energy storage capacity. The improved electrochemical performance can be associated with the combined effects of Mn doping such as enhanced conductivity, larger electrochemically available surface area, and creation of additional redox centers. Thus, the presented study proves the capability of Mn doping in tuning the structural and electrochemical properties of WO₃.

articles.title: Quantum Algorithms for Computational Economics: A Critical Review of Simulation, Optimization, and Near-Term Evidence
articles.abstract: Quantum computing is increasingly discussed as a possible source of new computational methods for economics, but its relevance depends on whether economic bottlenecks match quantum algorithmic primitives. This critical review evaluates that match for computational economics. It synthesizes work on quantum amplitude estimation and quantum Monte Carlo for simulation and risk measurement; quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO), Ising formulations, quantum annealing, and the quantum approximate optimization algorithm for discrete optimization; and quantum linear-algebra and machine-learning primitives for econometrics and model solution. The review argues that there is no general-purpose quantum algorithm for economics analogous to Shor's algorithm for factoring. Credible claims are problem-class specific and depend on state preparation, output requirements, conditioning, hardware noise, embedding overhead, and comparison with strong classical and quantum-inspired baselines. The most mature economic applications are derivative pricing and financial risk, payment-system liquidity optimization, quantum Monte Carlo for stress testing, and early quantum-annealing formulations of dynamic programming. Transportation and infrastructure applications are relevant mainly as networked economic optimization problems. The article proposes an evidence ladder for quantum computational economics and a research agenda centered on reproducible benchmarks, economically meaningful objective functions, end-to-end resource accounting, and evaluation by economic value rather than hardware novelty. JEL Classification: C02; C15; C61; C63; C88; E37; G11; G17; R41

articles.title: Intrinsic Vectorial Gradiometry via Quantum Control of a Spin-based Sensor
articles.abstract: Gradiometry provides a versatile alternative to passive environmental shielding in quasi-static magnetometry, effectively suppressing background noise through differential signal extraction. Nevertheless, traditional implementations rely on multi-sensor architectures restricted to spatial gradients, where subtracting signals from independent detectors involves imperfect suppression of common-mode noise and artifacts, limiting their sensitivity. To overcome these limitations, we introduce a quantum control sequence that enables intrinsic temporal and spatial vectorial gradiometry of magnetic fields using a single quantum sensor. Our method provides direct access to first and higher-order derivatives of the magnetic field and extended applicability via auxiliary nuclear spin memory. We showcase this protocol on an ensemble of nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond and combine it with mechanical control to realize high-precision differential sensing. Through detailed numerical simulations, we demonstrate the performance of our scheme in two critical DC magnetometry applications: (i) vector magnetic anomaly detection and (ii) non-invasive gradiometry of neuronal action potentials.

articles.title: Physics-Informed AI Surrogate Modelling of Thermal and Hydraulic Losses in Omani Crude Oil Pipelines Using RHLI-Based Analysis, Uncertainty- Quantification, and Explainable AI
articles.abstract: Efficient crude-oil pipeline transportation is central to the energy supply chain, yet thermal and hydraulic energy losses raise pumping-energy demand, operating cost, and associated emissions. Predicting these losses normally relies on high-fidelity Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD), which is too slow for real-time operational decision-making. This study develops a physics-informed artificial-intelligence surrogate that predicts Total Heat Loss, Head Loss, and Total Power Loss for Omani crude-oil pipelines transported under non-isothermal, viscoplastic (Bingham–Papanastasiou) conditions. A dataset of 962 high-fidelity COMSOL simulations across a three-segment serial pipeline was used to engineer physically interpretable features such as Reynolds number, Bingham number, a Thermo-Hydraulic Ratio, and a novel Rheological Heat-Loss Index (RHLI), and to train and cross-validate machine-learning and ensemble models. Under five-fold cross-validation, tree-based ensembles achieved high accuracy, with Heat Loss the most learnable target (cross-validated R² ≈ 1.0) and the Stacking Ensemble providing the most stable performance across all three targets. Uncertainty quantification through quantile regression, conformal prediction, and calibration analysis yielded reliable prediction intervals (Mean Calibration Error 0.0211; empirical 95% coverage 97.4%), while SHAP analysis identified Ambient Temperature as the dominant driver of Heat Loss, consistent with heat-transfer physics. The framework offers a fast, interpretable, and uncertainty-aware surrogate to support energy-efficient pipeline operation and real-time digital-twin monitoring.

articles.title: Can Regulatory Technology (RegTech) Boost Financial Performance? Evidence From Indian Commercial Banks
articles.abstract: This study empirically investigates the impact of regulatory technology (RegTech) adoption on the financial performance of Indian commercial banks. Utilizing a comprehensive panel dataset of 32 listed banks from 2016 to 2025, the research employs Python-based text-mining techniques on published annual reports to construct a novel RegTech adoption index, which is bifurcated into Core Regulatory Technology and RegTech Enabling Technology. To account for the dynamic persistence of bank profitability and resolve potential endogeneity issues, the study utilizes a two-step System GMM estimator alongside baseline Random Effects modeling. The empirical results reveal a significant asymmetrical relationship. Investments in RegTech Enabling Technology such as artificial intelligence and big data yield a strong, positive, and statistically significant enhancement to the Return on Assets (ROA). Conversely, Core Regulatory Technology dedicated strictly to automated compliance acts primarily as a mandatory operational safeguard, demonstrating a statistically insignificant impact on overall profitability. Furthermore, heterogeneity analysis uncovers that the financial benefits of foundational enabling technologies are heavily concentrated among large institutions and private sector banks, whereas the substantial capital expenditures required for core compliance systems actively compress the asset returns of large banks. These core findings are rigorously validated through extensive robustness checks, including the use of alternative dependent variables (ROE), lagged effects, outlier removal, and a Monte Carlo placebo test. Ultimately, this research provides vital strategic insights for bank management and policymakers regarding the operational costs and monetization potential of digital compliance infrastructures.

articles.title: High-Accuracy Prediction of Complex Permittivity in Ternary Composites Using Parameters Provided by Binary Systems
articles.abstract: Accurate prediction of the frequency-dependent complex permittivity of ternary composites remains challenging because constituent parameters obtained through inverse modeling are model dependent and are often re-estimated for different composite systems. Here, a binary-informed mixing-law framework was developed for polyaniline (PANI)/carbonyl iron powder (CIP)/polyurethane (PU) composites over 2–18 GHz. Maxwell–Garnett (MG), coherent-potential (CP), and Bruggeman (BR) models were first compared using the same PANI/PU dataset, and MG provided the most consistent overall performance for retrieving the model-dependent effective constituent response of PANI. The retrieved PANI response was examined using a modified Debye–conductivity model and independently assessed through cross-matrix prediction of PANI/paraffin composites without parameter recalibration. The binary-derived effective constituent responses of PANI and CIP were subsequently used as fixed inputs in an MG-based ternary expression. Without fitting the ternary dielectric spectra, the model reproduced the measured complex permittivity of five PANI/CIP/PU formulations at a fixed total filler loading of 30 wt.% and one PANI/PU binary endpoint with good overall agreement. The resulting R² values were 0.9891–0.9953 for ε′ and 0.9375–0.9963 for ε″. The corresponding NRMSE values were 5.62–11.71% for ε′ and 12.74–18.95% for five of the six ε″ datasets, while one narrow-response dataset exhibited a higher NRMSE of 35.12%. These results demonstrate that binary-derived effective constituent parameters can support forward permittivity prediction without ternary-specific recalibration, providing a practical basis for reducing experimental screening and guiding composition selection along the investigated composition path.

articles.title: SoK: Secure Software-Based Multi-Domain Data Segregation
articles.abstract: Modern mission-critical coordination demands seamless communication across multiple domains. Traditionally, Voice Communication Systems (VCS) have relied on physically separated Red/Black architectures to ensure voice and data segregation. While these hardware-based methods provide strong security assurances and remain foundational in high-security contexts, they can introduce significant complexity and scalability challenges as mission parameters expand into highly dynamic, multi-domain integrations. As defence, emergency response, and critical infrastructure operations increasingly require interoperable, flexible, and cost-efficient communication environments, there is a growing need to understand whether software-based approaches can provide comparable assurance while supporting modern operational requirements. This SoK characterises a transition to software-based Multi-Domain Data Segregation (MDDS) by integrating systems security, networking, and cryptography. Its goal is to consolidate existing research, identify shared architectural patterns, and address the security challenges facing next-generation high-assurance software-based VCS architectures. By assessing software-defined and virtualized approaches, this SoK supports the development of scalable, high-assurance VCS architectures that facilitate secure real-time coordination across diverse operational domains. Specifically, this SoK examines the security implications of Software-Defined Networking, Network Slicing, Separation Kernels, and Cross-Domain Solutions while addressing challenges posed by quantum computing through Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC). As the first comprehensive synthesis of the shift from hardware-enforced isolation to software-based segregation, this SoK serves as an essential foundation for researchers and industry stakeholders seeking to advance secure, adaptable, and future-ready VCS infrastructures for mission-critical operations.

articles.title: Proteomic and functional insights into spinal neuroimmune maladaptation: dual-level modulation of mast cell-neural crosstalk by ultramicronized palmitoylethanolamide
articles.abstract: Repeated morphine administration drives spinal neuroimmune mechanisms contributing to analgesic tolerance and hyperalgesia. We investigated the contribution of mast cell-derived mediators to spinal neuroinflammation and the homeostatic effects of ultramicronized palmitoylethanolamide (PEA) using rat organotypic spinal cord slice cultures. Slices exposed to morphine were treated with conditioned medium from activated RBL-2H3 mast cells. Mast cell-derived conditioned medium induced a robust neuroinflammatory response, upregulating IL-6, IL-1β, CCL2, and PTX3 expression, and markedly enhancing the release of the pro-nociceptive neuropeptide CGRP. These alterations were accompanied by reduced neuronal marker expression and impaired astrocytic reactivity in the spinal dorsal horn. Notably, upstream mast cell pretreatment with PEA modified their secretory activity, blunting subsequent spinal inflammatory cascades. Quantitative proteomic analysis revealed that conditioned medium derived from PEA-treated RBL-2H3 cells extensively reshaped the spinal microenvironment, rescuing extracellular matrix components (such as collagen VI), downregulating neurodegenerative markers (including SIRT2 and BIN1), and inducing protective regulators like LGALS1. Downstream tissue-level application of ultramicronized PEA directly to the spinal slices replicated these beneficial actions, significantly attenuating inflammatory transcription and CGRP release while restoring neuronal and astrocytic homeostatic profiles. Collectively, these findings suggest that mast cell-derived factors promote spinal neuroimmune maladaptation, which is effectively countered by ultramicronized PEA via a dual-level mechanism acting on both the mast cell secretome and the spinal tissue interface. This integrated approach offers a promising translational strategy to preserve opioid efficacy and mitigate central sensitization.

articles.title: Experiment shows when quantum 'cat' states stop bouncing back
articles.abstract: Quantum systems can occupy superpositions, quantum states that combine different possibilities. For instance, a microwave field can be prepared in a superposition of an empty state and a state that contains microwave light.

articles.title: Quantum interference traps electron waves in metal for first time
articles.abstract: Ever since quantum mechanics first described particles, like electrons, as rippling waves, researchers have wondered if those waves could be trapped in place. Writing today in Science a century later, a team of Columbia University researchers reports waves of electrons becoming trapped for the first time in a metal called Pd₅AlI₂.

articles.title: Nature of the bosonic edge phase in a double quantum spin Hall insulator
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30251v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Field-theoretic analysis has predicted that the edge of a double quantum spin Hall insulator (DQSHI) can undergo an interaction-driven transition from a phase with fermionic edge modes into one with only bosonic modes. All single-fermion edge excitations are gapped in this bosonic edge phase, but fermion pairs remain gapless, leading to distinct experimental signatures. We numerically simulate the interacting DQSHI edge and verify the existence of the bosonic edge phase. This calculation requires an explicit bulk embedding of the DQSHI edge, due to its mixed anomaly between charge and S^z conservation. We hence employ segment DMRG on an infinite two-dimensional cylinder, where the DQSHI bulk is modeled in terms of two copies of the spin-up lowest Landau level, combined with their time-reversed counterparts. We find that interactions can open a single-fermion gap at the DQSHI edge while fermion pairs remain gapless, matching the predictions for the bosonic edge phase. We find the scaling of the single-fermion gap with interaction strength to be consistent with field-theoretic calculations, and discuss the relevance of the bosonic edge phase to twisted homobilayers of WSe₂ and MoTe₂. We elaborate on the methodological extension of the segment geometry used here to other topological phases with edge anomalies.

articles.title: Discrete time liquids
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30266v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Discrete time crystals exhibit robust subharmonic oscillations, spontaneously breaking the discrete time-translation symmetry of a periodic drive. Since their emergence, the question of whether other types of temporal many-body order can exist has attracted considerable attention. Here we identify discrete time liquids -- a new form of spatiotemporal order characterized by short-range temporal coherence as a result of time-solitons. We study a two-dimensional spin system coupled to a finite-temperature cavity, whose fluctuations provide a noisy, approximately periodic drive with only finite temporal coherence. Remarkably, the spins nevertheless form a metastable state with robust period-doubled dynamics over an extended parameter regime. Unlike a time crystal, this state has only finite temporal coherence: individual trajectories stochastically switch between the two symmetry-related temporal configurations of the period-doubled response. We identify these switches as time-solitons: topological defects in temporal order that preserve local period doubling while destroying long-range temporal coherence, thereby producing the time liquid state. We propose a minimal model which reproduces the distribution of temporal correlations of the many-body system, suggesting a general description of the time liquid as a time crystal with a finite density of time-solitons. Because these solitons can occur at arbitrary times, ensemble averaging restores continuous time-translation symmetry, raising the intriguing possibility that discrete time liquids can exist in thermal equilibrium.

articles.title: Charge-monitored Luttinger liquid
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30271v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We discuss phases of interacting fermionic Luttinger liquids without particle number conservation, such as those in proximity to a superconductor, subjected to weak continuous measurements of their particle density, in the regime where the bosonization approach is applicable. We show that the phases of these systems are controlled by the competition between measurements, which favor the area-law phase and particle tunneling in and out of the Luttinger liquid, which favors the volume-law phase. The volume-law phase in this system is always charge fuzzy. We show that within this framework, the phase boundary between the two phases is given by a universal dependence of the Luttinger parameter on the measurement rate. This behavior can be contrasted with the non-universal phase boundaries in more generic highly excited one dimensional systems whose behavior is no longer captured by the Luttinger liquid framework.

articles.title: Charge Density Waves and In-Gap States in Coupled Chains and Moiré Superlattices
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30281v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Charge density waves (CDWs) arise from the interplay between electrons and lattice distortions and are a hallmark of low-dimensional systems. Here we study coupled Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chains, both lattice-matched ladders and lattice-mismatched moiré superlattices, and find a rich set of CDW phases together with symmetry-protected bound states. In lattice-matched chains, the competition between electron-phonon coupling and interchain tunneling drives a sequence of CDW phases, including staggered dimers, trimers, and incommensurate states. These phases are generally gapped and host bound states protected by crystalline symmetries rather than chiral symmetry, and are therefore not pinned to zero energy. Lattice mismatch further reconstructs these phases into long-period supermoiré CDWs, with an ordered array of defects, pinned to the moiré length scale, that host localized electronic states. Interchain tunneling and lattice mismatch thus emerge as natural control parameters for CDW order and bound states in one-dimensional chains.

articles.title: Quantum Phases and Structural Transitions of Bosons in Bubble-Shaped Confinements
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30381v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the structural properties and superfluid behavior of soft-core bosons confined in a spherical bubble trap at large particle numbers (N le 1800). Using Path Integral Monte Carlo simulations with worm algorithm sampling in continuous space, we show that increasing N drives a sequence of layering transitions: beyond the established bilayer supersolid, a third concentric layer of clusters emerges at N approx 1800. By analyzing the distribution of permutation cycles distribution, we demonstrate that a finite superfluid fraction (fₛ approx 10%) persists even in this multi-layer regime. These findings clarify the role of particle number in driving layer formation on curved manifolds, offering a concrete guide for future experiments with bubble-trapped bosons.

articles.title: Unrestricted Binary Tree State for the Fermionic Hubbard Model
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30399v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Binary tree states have been introduced as compact correlated pair wave functions that improve upon the antisymmetrized geminal power by adding variational flexibility. Here, we extend the binary tree state to the fermionic half-filled Hubbard model using restricted and unrestricted orbitals. Although the ansatz is seniority zero in its optimized pairing basis, its expansion in the original Hubbard site basis can contain nonzero site- seniority character, while unrestricted orbital optimization provides additional flexibility through independent spin-up and spin-down orbitals. This provides a mechanism for a paired ansatz to describe the singly occupied configurations that dominate the repulsive Hubbard model at large U/t. We find that unrestricted BTS closely approaches optimized DOCI in the repulsive regime, substantially improves upon AGP, and reproduces DOCI density correlations more accurately than pCCD

articles.title: Suppression of Grain Boundary Nitrogen Degradation by Boron in Superalloys
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30451v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Superalloys enable the hottest sections of jet engines to operate at high temperatures, but environmentally assisted degradation limits their lifetime. In polycrystalline alloys, nitrogen penetrates beneath the protective surface oxides, to produce embrittling grain boundary nitrides. Boron is added in trace amounts to improve grain boundary strength, yet its role, if any, in oxidation-related degradation remains unclear. Here we show that boron segregates to an internal nitride--matrix interface in a Ni/Co-base γ/γprⁱme strengthened superalloy. Both B-free and B-containing alloys develop stratified chromia/alumina scales at 800~cⁱrcC in SI100hour, but the B-free variant produces larger, deeper and more elongated Ti/Nb-rich subsurface grain boundary nitrides. Correlative 4D S/TEM and atom probe tomography identify the particle as a chemically complex B1 nitride and reveal interfacial boron segregation. This shows that trace alloying as an alloy strategy can control damaging internal reaction product precipitation and growth by core-shell segregation.

articles.title: Orientation-selective microwave heating of laser-graphitized diamond at 2.45 GHz
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30453v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pristine diamond couples negligibly to a 2.45 GHz field. We show that femtosecond-laser inscription of a buried graphitic (sp2) architecture makes a 4 x 4 x 2 mm³ N-doped (100 ppm) high-pressure high- temperature (HPHT) crystal absorb strongly, and that the absorption is switched by the orientation of the inscribed structure relative to the cavity electric field. With the 1.8 mm depth of a concentric grating along E, stepped power gave a smooth staircase to an indicated ~500C at 80 W followed, at 90 W, by an abrupt excursion to an indicated ~900C with surface roughening and terraced oxidation. Rotating the same sample so that the grating diameter lay along E, and an unmodified crystal in either orientation, gave no signal above the ~40C floor. We account for this by the depolarisation factors L of the sub-wavelength tracks, collapsed into one screening parameter S = Lσ/(ωϵ0ϵh), here, σ conductivity, ω - cyclic frequency, ϵh,0 - permittivity of host and vacuum, respectively. The model turns element length, diameter and writing regime into design variables for microwave absorption in a transparent host.

articles.title: Chiral Cavity Vacua as Local Generators and Probes of Non-Abelian Kitaev Topology
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30502v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show how a gyrotropic cavity vacuum generates, probes, and spatially programs non-Abelian topology in the Kitaev honeycomb model. Gauge-consistent virtual-photon elimination produces a universal helicity-odd interaction i[Pₓ,P_y] alongside same-order even dressing. For the leading bond polarization, this commutator is exactly the Kitaev three-spin mass. Mode normalization imposes a thermodynamic constraint: one extended normalized mode gives a local mass that vanishes with sample area, whereas a localized mode writes a finite topological island and a finite mode density enables a bulk mass. The exact Majorana solution yields helicity-reversed Chern gaps and edge propagation, while integrated circular dichroism exactly measures the mass generator, langlei[Pₓ,P_y]rangle=-sqrt3p²langle O₃rangle. Real-space calculations reveal a non-Abelian island and a helicity wall with two co-propagating Majorana modes. Uniform helicity reversal is a Dirac-mass quench with nᵣₘ ₑₓproptoτ_Q⁻¹, whereas moving a wall localizes the gap closing. The equilibrium vacuum kernel contains sum-frequency rather than resonant denominators. These results establish distinct criteria for local and bulk cavity-induced topology.

articles.title: Cluster property and entanglement in the superconducting state
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30581v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present the conditions for satisfying the cluster property in the superconducting state. Using these conditions, we show that the cluster property employed when deriving the order parameter of the superconducting state (OPSS) holds true, and that the OPSS is given by {}_Slangle Ψ | hatψ(x)hatψ(x') | Ψ rangle_S, where |Ψrangle_S is the superconducting state, and where hatψ(x) is the field operator of superconducting electrons. This provides a resolution to the long-standing concern raised by Leggett et al. regarding particle-number fluctuation in the superconducting state. In addition, by considering the entanglement between two particles composed of the maximum geminal of the BCS ground state [J. Phys. Commun. 5, 095003 (2021)], it is confirmed that the larger the deviation from the conditions for satisfying the cluster property becomes, the greater the magnitude of the entanglement becomes. This shows not only the effectiveness of the conditions for satisfying the cluster property but also the justification of the OPSS that has been commonly used.

articles.title: String Order in Quench Dynamics as a Probe of Quantum Phase Transitions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30647v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the anisotropic XY chain in a transverse field by introducing a global string order parameter and examining its equilibrium behavior and its quench dynamics from a fully polarized initial state. The corresponding string operator is defined as the product of local projected spin operators over the entire chain. The nonequilibrium order parameter is the long-time average of the logarithm of the string-operator expectation value per site after the quench.For the ground state, its field derivative is singular on the Ising critical lines; after the quench, the steady-state response also records the field boundaries and the anisotropy transition. We derive analytically the nonanalytic behavior of the order parameter at the quantum critical lines. Our results reveal a hidden nonlocal order underlying this paradigmatic model of conventional quantum phase transitions. They also connect measurable spin populations with equilibrium and dynamical topological structure.

articles.title: Symmetry-Preserving Local Representation for Short-Range Interaction in Complex Materials
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30726v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modeling short-range interactions in highly disordered materials remains challenging due to the immense configuration space and the disruption of local symmetry in truncated theoretical models. Here, we propose a symmetry-preserving local representation framework that strictly enforces topological continuity and translational invariance via boundary passivation. Applied to high-entropy alloys, this approach autonomously unravels the nonlinear ligand effects modulating local reactivity and accurately captures coverage-dependent many-body interactions without explicit periodic expansion. By resolving the conflict between localized chemical environments and extended periodic boundaries, this framework not only reduces computational complexity by an order of magnitude but also provides a physically transparent paradigm for deciphering short-range order in complex condensed matter systems.

articles.title: Localization Contrast As a Fundamental Limit of Radiative Quantum Efficiency
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30741v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Disorder can localize valence- and conduction-band states to different degrees, yet whether such localization contrast has observable consequences remains poorly understood. Here, we show that localization contrast strongly impacts competing carrier-recombination channels. We illustrate this behavior in random InₓGa₁₋ₓN alloys. Increasing the In content from x=13.5% to x=22% progressively localizes the valence-band maximum state while leaving the conduction-band minimum state comparatively delocalized. This contrasting localization decreases the interband optical momentum matrix element underlying radiative recombination. For Auger-Meitner recombination, however, localization alone does not determine the coupling; atomic-scale disorder also breaks primitive-cell translational symmetry and modifies the momentum-space and phase structure of the states. This generates additional low-Q components and enhances the Auger coupling by more than five orders of magnitude relative to pristine GaN. Thus, we provide a microscopic explanation for the competing trends in radiative and Auger recombination. More broadly, our results establish localization contrast as a mechanism through which disorder can control optical and carrier-carrier interactions in semiconductors.

articles.title: Strain Waves Generate Compression and Trigger Buckling in Active Polymers
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30749v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chemical reactions can sustain polymer motion without necessarily generating the compression required for buckling. Theory and simulations show that tension-dependent chemical transitions coupled to bond elasticity generate finite-wavelength traveling strain waves in a semiflexible polymer. In the straight chain at fixed axial span, the waves reduce mean active contraction while leaving mean elastic tension unchanged, generating compression that drives bending above a threshold. Releasing the mean load allows longitudinal waves to persist while transverse perturbations decay.

articles.title: Universal Synthesis of Large-Area Hybrid Perovskite Monolayers Enabling Lithography-Free, Low-Static-Power Optoelectronics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30764v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Solution-phase synthesis of monolayer hybrid organic-inorganic perovskites is constrained by rapid out-of-plane crystal growth, uncontrolled nucleation, and strong interlayer aggregation, yielding flakes of only a few μm. We introduce a steric-engineering ternary-solvent growth strategy to synthesize monolayer and few-layer A2MX4 hybrid perovskites with exceptionally large surface areas. By combining alcohol cosolvents with an amine additive, out-of-plane stacking is suppressed. Using (PEA)2CuCl4 as a model system, monolayers with lateral areas exceeding 1000 μm2 are achieved, representing a massive dimensional increase over conventional methods. Molecular dynamics and quantum-chemical calculations show that longer-chain alcohols reorganize precursor solvation, while solvent volatility prolongs edge-mediated precursor transport during annealing. This strategy demonstrates universal applicability across diverse organic spacer cations (PEA+, F-PEA+, PentA+), metal centers (Cu2+, Mn2+, Pb2+), and halides (Cl-, Br-, I-). The large lateral dimensions enable direct, solvent-free electrical contact fabrication via physical shadow masking, bypassing chemical degradation from solvents used in conventional lithography. Planar devices fabricated from isolated ultrathin (PEA)2PbI4 channels exhibit ultra-low dark currents down to the 10⁻¹⁵ - 10⁻¹³ A range, enabling femtowatt-to-picowatt static power consumption, ~ 0.2 pW at 5 V, a 250-fold reduction relative to drop-cast films, while maintaining a high light-to-dark current ratio of 4.3 x 102. This work establishes precise steric and solvation control as a paradigm for scalable, compositionally diverse, low-static-power monolayer 2D perovskite optoelectronics.

articles.title: Surface morphology and shear effect on lubricated granular system
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30831v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Improving the particle surface frictional behavior is of considerable importance in several industries so as to manipulate the powder flowability and handling. In this work, we have studied the lubrication phenomena in an assembly of flowing bulk powder particles in presence of a fine powder lubricant. Experiments were conducted in two different shear environments, for two different levels of confinement and using three different bulk powder particles having distinct surface morphology. The added lubricant particles tend to adhere to the surface of bulk particles thereby altering their surface morphology. This results in altered inter-particle friction, which typically reduces for small addition of lubricant, but increases on its excess addition, thereby altering the particle flowability. While this behavior is generally understood through previous studies, the current work explores how the effect of confinement, shear environment and particle surface characteristics combine in a unique manner to provide modified flow behavior for different lubricant concentrations. Extended shear duration seems to extend the range of lubricant concentrations for improved flowability. On the other hand flow confinement seems to limit the extent of lubrication for these range of concentrations. Both these opposing effects also exhibit a unique dependence on the particle surface morphology and its seeming affinity with the lubricant particle. The parameter types and ranges explored comprise most conditions encountered in industrial systems, the outcome thereby providing a basis for designing of applications handling lubricant-particle mixtures.

articles.title: Fit-error corrected auxiliary master equation approach for low-temperature nonequilibrium dynamical mean-field theory
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30846v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The auxiliary master equation approach (AMEA) is a nonperturbative impurity solver for steady-state nonequilibrium dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT). It replaces the physical hybridization function by that of a small auxiliary open quantum system, whose parameters are fitted to reproduce it, and then solves the resulting many-body problem essentially exactly. AMEA's accuracy is thus limited by the quality of this fit: since the fastest-varying part of the hybridization is set by the distribution function, whose Fermi edges sharpen at low temperature, the fit tends to overestimate the temperature, especially for weak reservoir coupling. For the auxiliary hybridization itself, however, AMEA's self-energy is essentially exact. We correct for the fit error by estimating, via an approximate solver applicable to arbitrary hybridization functions, the ratio between the self-energies of the physical and auxiliary hybridizations, and using it to extend AMEA's self-energy from the auxiliary to the physical case. This fit-error correction becomes exact whenever either the fit or the approximate solver is exact. We benchmark the scheme using the nonequilibrium Kajueter-Kotliar iterated perturbation theory (IPT), generalized here to spin-polarized solutions, as the approximate solver; other approximate solvers, such as the noncrossing approximation, can be used as well. Applied to an Anderson impurity model with a spin-polarized bath, and within DMFT to a Hubbard layer weakly coupled to two metallic reservoirs, the correction largely removes the spurious heating from the AMEA fit and from insufficient thermalization by the reservoirs, while preserving the correct description of the Mott insulator, which IPT alone cannot fully recover.

articles.title: Designing sustainable high-entropy alloys directly from mixed oxides: A thermodynamic perspective
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30870v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hydrogen-based direct reduction (HyDR) of mixed oxide precursors offers an alternative route to produce sustainable alloys, bypassing the sequential extraction, refining, and remelting steps that dominate the carbon footprint of conventional metallurgy and individual metal production. However, the thermodynamic limits and most effective H₂/H₂O ratio needed for full metallization of multicomponent oxides are not yet established. This is because the formation of metallic and oxide solid solutions alters the chemical activity of both the reduced metallic phases and the unreduced oxides, coupling their equilibria in ways that cannot be deduced from the stability of the pure individual oxides. Herein, we develop a CALPHAD-based thermodynamic framework to establish the compoistion-temperature-H₂/H₂O window for complete metallization of CoCrFeMnNi-based oxide mixtures. Mn and Cr generally increase oxide stability, while Co, Fe, and Ni decrease it, allowing reduction at lower H₂/H₂O ratios. The effect of each element is not fixed; it depends on the starting mixed oxide composition and can reverse when the last oxide to reduce changes. Furthermore, we show that the reduction pathway complexity does not correlate with the difficulty of removing the final oxygen: a system with few intermediate transformation steps can still terminate as a highly stable residual oxide, whereas extensive partial reduction may leave the stability of the final residual oxide essentially unchanged. By linking residual-oxide stability to the H₂/H₂O ratio, the framework identifies the thermodynamic limits and provides guidelines for designing sustainable multicomponent alloys directly from mixed oxide precursors.

articles.title: Broadband emitter localization and prefabrication two-photon interference from InAs/InP quantum dots monolithically grown on an InGaAsP/InP distributed Bragg reflector
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30905v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We demonstrate a monolithic telecom C-band single-photon platform based on low-density InAs/InP quantum dots grown on an InGaAsP/InP distributed Bragg reflector, with simulated upward light-extraction efficiency exceeding 10% within the 40 nm spectral band. Enhanced light extraction is crucial for wide-field photoluminescence imaging, enabling approximately 3 nm statistical centroid-localization precision of QD emitters due to improved signal-to-noise ratio. The identified charged exciton emitting at 1549.5 nm exhibits single-photon emission purity up to 94.7%, validated by a raw peak-area integration under pulsed quasi-resonant excitation. Under these conditions, photons emitted sequentially from the unprocessed planar structure reveal a raw two-photon interference visibility of 51% of the photon wave packet within the 2 ns time window and 41% over a 4 ns integration window, all without Purcell enhancement typical for cavity-embedded emitters. Combining broadband extraction, high photon coherence, and emitter preselection on a native III-V wafer, this architecture paves the way for marker-based deterministic fabrication of high-quality monolithic nanophotonic devices.

articles.title: Chiroptical Valleytronic in SnSe
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30930v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum geometric properties of Bloch electrons play a central role in governing light-matter interactions and transport phenomena in solids. Here, we report quantum-geometric chiroptical selection rules that generate a helicity-dependent momentum-space population imbalance in the group-IV monochalcogenide SnSe. By combining time- and angle-resolved extreme-ultraviolet photoemission spectroscopy with ab initio real-time simulations of photoexcited carrier dynamics, we identify valley-selective excitation at opposite crystal momenta arising from the breaking of time-reversal symmetry under circularly polarized illumination. We theoretically demonstrate that the magnitude of valley circular dichroism is strongly constrained by crystal symmetry through its influence on the quantum geometric tensor, the key quantity underlying valley optical selection rules. The resulting chiroptically induced valley polarization decays on sub-picosecond timescales through intervalley scattering mediated by electron-phonon coupling. Furthermore, we show theoretically that the population imbalance between valleys at opposite momenta gives rise to a helicity-reversible transient photocurrent. These findings provide microscopic insight into how quantum geometry governs valley-selective light-matter interactions, valley polarization, and photocurrent generation in van der Waals materials exhibiting hidden and transient symmetry breaking.

articles.title: Intensity-driven Mott-like transition in a 2D Ruddlesden-Popper perovskite
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30964v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Two-dimensional Ruddlesden-Popper-type halide perovskites have emerged as promising cutting-edge nonlinear optical materials due to their strong excitonic effects and carrier-density-dependent optical responses. In this work, we investigate the nonlinear optical properties and ultrafast carrier dynamics of (BA)₂PbI₄ under infrared excitation, resonant with the two-photon energy of its excitonic transition. Using a nonlinear femtosecond Z-scan measurement with a 1030,nm pump pulse, we observe a pronounced intensity-dependent evolution of the nonlinear absorption coefficient and the refractive index. With increasing pump intensity, a switch from saturable absorption to reverse saturable absorption emerges, suggesting an intensity-driven Mott-like transition. To elucidate the underlying carrier dynamics, intensity-dependent transient absorption spectroscopy was performed under the same excitation intensities. This reveals a long-lived charge carrier population above the estimated Mott density, reflecting a clear phase transition from an exciton-dominated regime to a dense electron-hole plasma regime. Moreover, such an intensity-driven, high, and switchable nonlinear optical response, along with a Mott-like transition under infrared pulse excitation, makes the 2D (BA)₂PbI₄ perovskites suitable for all-optical operation in the infrared regime.

articles.title: Contact Renormalization of One-Mode Electron Correlation: Validation in Four- and Ten-Electron Systems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31031v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A stationary many-electron eigenstate has one dynamical phase although its internal response can be strongly multimode. We ask whether the stationary Hartree--Fock information carrier contains enough information to determine the scalar correlation energy through one effective return. In regularized Hartree--Fock, Gaussian primitive products fix a minimum-information relative-coordinate mode before any one-mode reduction; virial completion defines the correlation source, while exact contact measures the additional return restriction created by neighboring occupied pairs. The Be-like 1s²²s² sequence establishes the one-valence-pair boundary: with no neighboring occupied valence pair, the source returns through the universal floor D₀=sqrt1+δ². Ten-electron molecules and Ne-like ions then test how finite-pair contact dresses that return. The same parameter-free source--return construction reproduces the established molecular and ionic correlation trends with quantitative accuracy. The numerical agreement therefore serves as validation of a physical separation between source strength and return restriction, rather than as the objective by itself.

articles.title: The often overlooked role of sound in liquid thermal transport
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31127v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Formulated a hundred years ago, the Bridgman formula for thermal conductivity of liquids postulates a proportionality between sound velocity and thermal conductivity. This designates phonons as heat carriers in a liquid. Its empirical success has been under-appreciated and its conceptual implications overlooked. It is not mentioned in well-known condensed-matter textbook. Here, we review its origin, its links to hydrodynamic Euler equations and to the fundamental paradox surrounding the parabolic heat equation and its fate across the quantum-classical crossover.

articles.title: Tracking the Emergence and Persistence of Abnormal Grain Growth in an Aluminum Alloy using Diffraction-Contrast Tomography
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31176v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Abnormal grain growth is inherently three-dimensional, making 3D tracking of grain evolution essential for understanding its underlying mechanisms. This study combines synchrotron-based diffraction-contrast tomography and phase-contrast tomography to characterize the three-dimensional grain structure and quantify the size and spatial distribution of second-phase particles in the aluminum alloy AA5252. Using an interrupted annealing protocol, we tracked the persistent growth of abnormal grains and the emergence of abnormal growth in a grain initially belonging to the matrix. Although second-phase particles effectively suppressed grain growth in the matrix, variations in local particle density showed no apparent correlation with either the emergence or subsequent rapid growth of abnormal grains. Instead, crystallographic misorientation and, more notably, neighboring grain size were identified as stronger predictors of abnormal growth rate. Matrix grains were consumed more rapidly when they were relatively small and shared high-angle grain boundaries with the growing abnormal grain. The same trends were observed for the grain that underwent a transition from normal to abnormal growth. Remarkably, even before the onset of abnormal growth, this grain was surrounded by smaller matrix grains with exclusively high-angle grain boundaries, while the local particle density was slightly higher than average. These findings suggest that the same microstructural characteristics facilitate both the emergence and persistence of abnormal grain growth, although the mechanism triggering the transition to rapid growth remains unresolved.

articles.title: Realization of a Superleak in a Quantum Gas
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31185v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ultracold quantum gases offer a controllable and microscopically accessible platform for understanding and engineering superfluidity. Yet, realizing a superleak that selectively transports the superfluid while suppressing normal flow has remained elusive. Here, we harness an optical superlattice to realize such a superleak through dynamical selectivity. The superfluid undergoes coherent Josephson transport, whereas the normal component exhibits slow, thermodynamically limited response, resulting in a flow-rate contrast of 500(49). Exploiting this contrast, we demonstrate repeated filtering of the normal component and dynamical purification of the superfluid, while sustaining coherent driven oscillations for up to 100 cycles. Our results establish a controllable atomic superleak and open possibilities for manipulating transport and thermodynamics in quantum fluids.

articles.title: Site and bond percolation thresholds of all k-uniform tilings with kle 10
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31190v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the site and bond percolation thresholds of all 23,396 k-uniform tilings of the plane by regular polygons with kle 10, the complete set according to the known enumeration. We use Monte Carlo simulation on tori and the condition that no wrapping and a cross-wrapping cluster are equally probable, the Monte Carlo form of the critical-polynomial criterion, which needs no knowledge of the large-scale anisotropy that most of these lattices have. The 486 thresholds with kle4 have uncertainties of a few units in the sixth decimal and reproduce the 22 Archimedean reference values (rms deviation 0.71 standard errors) and unpublished bond thresholds of the 20 two-uniform lattices (χ²=19.5 for 20 values); the others have median statistical uncertainties of 2×10⁻⁵ (kle7) to 7×10⁻⁵ (kge8) and no detectable finite-size bias. The vertex-type fractions alone fix the thresholds for kge5 to about 2×10⁻³ (linear rule fitted on kle4), while tilings with equal composition differ by up to 6×10⁻³ (site) and 2×10⁻² (bond). In the range of domain sizes covered, descriptors of radius one account for more than half of this difference, and stackings of identical strips have thresholds linear in the fraction of each boundary type. For tilings that differ only by the registry of strips separated by h rows of squares, the bond threshold difference decreases by a factor of 6-8 per row, comparable to the leading momentum-π eigenvalue of the square-band transfer matrix.

articles.title: Spin-Dependent Transport in One-Dimensional Mercury- and Silver-Mediated DNA Nanowires
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31508v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Metallo-DNA nanowires serve as a versatile, programmable scaffold for molecular-scale electronics. In this work, we demonstrate that periodic heavy-metal coordination fundamentally reshapes the electronic landscape of DNA, generating dispersive, metal-centered conduction bands rather than isolated localized states. Driven by enhanced inter-layer coupling, where second nearest-neighbor hopping plays a crucial role: the conduction bandwidth can approach 1 eV, more than double that of canonical DNA. These broad bands suggest enhanced robustness of transport against structural fluctuations. As a result of relativistic effects, in these quasi-one-dimensional materials, spin-orbit (SO) coupling enhances band dispersion and governs spin-dependent transport. We predict that although ligand hybridization reduces atomic SO splitting, the effective SO splitting in these nanowires is comparable to the next-nearest-neighbor hopping strength, which results in considerable spin mixing. We find that Hg2+-coordinated nanowire exhibit pronounced spin-flip conductance comparable to spin-conserving conductance across the LUMO manifold. This efficient spin conversion remains robust over extended molecular lengths and is accompanied by a set of highly delocalized unoccupied states with oscillating nodal structures, readily accessible under low-bias transport measurements. In contrast, the Ag+-coordinated nanowires exhibit weak spin-flip scattering that is more than an order of magnitude smaller than spin-preserving transport. This duality establishes the choice of coordination metal as a decisive parameter to govern metal-metal interaction, electron delocalization, and spin-dependent transport. Overall, our findings demonstrate how relativistic effects and quantum confinement intersect in these bio-templated, quasi-one-dimensional molecular conductors.

articles.title: Sign-problem-free Bosonic Auxiliary Field Quantum Monte Carlo
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31541v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The sign problem poses a fundamental barrier to numerically exact quantum Monte Carlo simulations, severely hindering our understanding of quantum many-body physics across disciplines ranging from condensed matter to particle and nuclear physics. Geometrical frustration makes this barrier especially acute for interacting bosons. Here, we develop a bosonic auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo (BAFQMC) method and rigorously prove that time-reversal symmetry and reflection positivity each provide a general sufficient condition for sign-problem-free simulations. Crucially, under either criterion, BAFQMC evades the sign problem even on frustrated lattices where conventional world-line and stochastic-series-expansion methods fail. Benchmarking our approach on a two-flavor Bose-Hubbard model on the triangular lattice yields excellent quantitative agreement with finite-temperature exact diagonalization. By establishing unifying principles to solve the sign problem in BAFQMC, our work substantially expands the reach of unbiased, numerically exact simulations for frustrated bosonic matter.

articles.title: Breathing and quadrupole modes in squeezed Bose-Bose liquid drops
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31581v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the lowest excitation modes of binary ³⁹K ultradilute droplets confined harmonically in one direction, which reduces the critical number of particles needed to sustain a self-bound state. Using the density functional built from first-principles quantum Monte Carlo calculations (QMC), which incorporates the effects of finite range interactions, we study the crossover of the oscillation modes from three to two dimensions. For weak squeezing, we observe the coupling between breathing and quadrupole modes, resulting from the breaking of spherical symmetry. Increasing the squeezing, the higher-frequency mode corresponding to three-dimensional breathing mode becomes unstable. For squeezings stronger and comparable to experiments, we analyze the dependence of the excitation modes on the droplet size for several interactions and show the reduction of the number of particles needed to sustain stable oscillations. The differences between the results obtained with the QMC functional and the extended Gross-Pitaevskii theory are increased with respect to the case of previously studied spherical droplets.

articles.title: Reentrant d=2+1 Superfluidity at High Temperature
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30236v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a UV-complete model with a global U(1) symmetry in d=2+1 dimensions that exhibits a Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) ordered phase at arbitrarily high temperatures. A careful separation of scales yields a two-dimensional Euclidean effective field theory whose construction remains perturbatively controlled even when its soft modes become strongly coupled. We determine the BKT phase boundary by carefully matching this theory to existing lattice Monte Carlo results. The high-temperature phase supports gapless static modes and algebraically decaying correlations even as T→infty.

articles.title: Maxwell-Chern-Simons-Matter in AdS₃
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30260v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study Maxwell-Chern-Simons theory on AdS₃ coupled to N complex scalars or Dirac fermions, including sextic and Gross-Neveu interactions, respectively. First, we derive the bulk Maxwell-Chern-Simons propagator, clarifying how Dirichlet boundary conditions fix the contributions of the massive and flat sectors. Upon coupling to the matter sector, we work at large N with κ=k/N and α=Ne² fixed, where k is the Chern-Simons level. We determine the corresponding phase diagrams, and we resum matter insertions to obtain the photon propagator at leading order in large N, exactly in α and κ. Its poles determine the spin-one boundary spectrum, split into two helicity sectors by the Chern-Simons interaction. With Dirichlet boundary conditions, the unHiggsed scalar phase contains a protected chiral current, which is lifted by Higgsing. In the fermionic phases, the current persists for nonzero effective Chern-Simons level, with helicity determined by the induced level shift. At bulk conformal points, we extract large-N BCFT data for the critical and tricritical scalar theories, as well as for the regular fermion and Gross-Neveu theories.

articles.title: Robust topology optimization of isogeometric Kirchhoff--Love shells by the Speed Method
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30389v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper presents a framework for robust topology optimization of Kirchhoff-Love (KL) multi-patch shells using isogeometric analysis and non-matching meshes and provides a CAD-compatible method. The material distribution is optimized via a NURBS-based level set method, enabling accurate boundary representation and seamless export to standard CAD/CAM workflows. The shape derivative is computed using the speed method, yielding a volume-based formulation that avoids boundary approximations and aligns with the isogeometric principle of coarse, high-order discretizations. This eliminates the need for local refinement, adaptive quadrature, or trimming as the descent direction for the compliance and volume objectives are obtained through a biharmonic equation. The framework is extended to robust optimization under uncertainty, accounting for stochastic loading and material properties via Monte Carlo sampling and Gaussian Random Fields. Numerical examples demonstrate the method's efficiency and robustness across single- and multi-patch shells, reproducing literature results with fewer elements than traditional FEM or refined IGA approaches. The developed methods and tools can be directly extended to problems involving stress-based optimization and risk-averse metrics. The numerical implementations are open-source and available on GitHub.

articles.title: Memory--Transport Competition in Physical Two-Bath Quantum Reset Dynamics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30457v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Coherence preservation and environmental renewal offer competing ways of controlling quantum memory and transport. We show that a seemingly natural protocol which exactly replaces the bath occupations while preserving arbitrary system--bath coherences need not correspond to a physical fermionic state. We instead construct a two-reservoir protocol with independent, number-conserving thermal attenuators, for which complete positivity and fermionic admissibility hold by construction. Physical attenuation necessarily modifies bath populations as well as cross correlations; the coherence control is not an independent hard-reset knob. Quadratic dynamics reduces the stroboscopic problem to an exact matrix fixed-point equation without a weak-coupling or Markov approximation. Analytically, coherence retention enhances the leading short-cycle transfer rate, including the complete-erasure limit; no general endpoint-vanishing theorem exists. An exact stationary continuity theorem forces the through-current to vanish whenever either reservoir is left entirely unrefreshed, although no analogous theorem suppresses it at complete erasure. For biased structured reservoirs, exact finite-chain calculations display distinct coherence-, current-, and signed energy-transfer operating points; a resolved high-retention boundary layer exposes strong finite-size sensitivity of the coherence peak. The model provides a microscopic, fermion-admissible benchmark for the interplay of reservoir coherence, particle transport, and energetic exchange.

articles.title: Probing quasiperiodic spectral accessibility with a finite-rate quantum Otto cycle
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30555v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quasiperiodic systems combine sharply different spectral and localisation regimes with a dense hierarchy of dynamical time scales. We show that a finite-rate quantum Otto cycle can use this structure as a thermodynamic probe, revealing which parts of the spectrum become dynamically accessible and thermodynamically relevant during a driven transformation. For a generalised Aubry-André-Harper chain, the resulting response is not determined by the static quasiperiodic regime alone: extended, near-critical, and crossing protocols do not exhibit universal ordering of work fluctuations. Instead, the statistics reflect transition pathways that are simultaneously dynamically coupled, thermally occupied, and energetically significant. The same spectral accessibility separates thermodynamic recovery from microscopic adiabatic recovery. Positive mean work can reappear while the population transfer dynamics remain strongly nonadiabatic because finite-rate population transfer is redistributed toward energetically less costly channels rather than suppressed. The full work distribution reveals a further separation, with a finite rate window in which positive-work cycles form a majority although the mean work remains negative. This behaviour persists in finite-size analysis. A thermally weighted spectral susceptibility connects these effects to a distributed hierarchy of dynamically active spectral regions rather than to a single minimum-gap bottleneck. Finite thermal contacts preserve this picture while introducing a second time scale and intercycle memory. Quantum Otto cycles can therefore provide a fluctuation-resolved thermodynamic probe of quasiperiodic spectral accessibility, complementary to direct spectroscopic and eigenstate-resolved diagnostics.

articles.title: Supercoiling Drives DNA-Protein Co-Condensation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30588v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The co-condensation of DNA and proteins plays an important role in genome compaction, including heterochromatin formation and chromosome segregation. Meanwhile, transcription and replication continuously generate DNA supercoiling, yet how the resulting torsional stress affects co-condensation remains poorly understood. Here, by coupling DNA elasticity to a protein concentration field, we show that supercoiling acts as a topological catalyst for co-condensation through a mutually reinforcing interplay with protein wetting. Specifically, protein wetting facilitates twist-to-writhe conversion, generating highly writhed DNA conformations that in turn promote capillary collapse into a protein-rich droplet. In the absence of supercoiling, DNA remains kinetically trapped in metastable extended states within our model, whereas sufficiently strong supercoiling removes the nucleation barrier and enables spontaneous co-condensation. These results establish topology as a distinct control parameter for biomolecular condensation and provide a mechanical framework for how active genomic processes can dynamically regulate large-scale genome organization.

articles.title: Time-reversal-based quantum metrology in a central-spin architecture: from SATIN to butterfly echo
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.30686v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate quantum-enhanced time-reversal-based metrology using the central spin model, in which a single ancilla spin of magnitude Sᵣₘ cₑₙ mediates interactions between N bath spins through a star-graph topology. We demonstrate that the SATIN (Signal Amplification Through Time-reversal Interaction) echo protocol can be implemented in this setup to achieve a Fisher information of N²/e with the collective langle J_yrangle readout, corresponding to a 4.34,dB offset from the Heisenberg limit. Furthermore, we establish that this platform provides a pathway to perform the butterfly echo protocol by conjugating each evolution step with a random collective bath rotation, thereby achieving axis-agnostic Heisenberg-scaled sensing. Crucially, with a small N-independent number of random steps, the butterfly echo reaches a Fisher information of N²/4 (6,dB below the Heisenberg limit) for any unknown encoding axis, with the plateau gain tracking the Haar limit. Finally, we demonstrate that the central-spin magnitude Sᵣₘ cₑₙ provides a powerful knob to reduce the optimal protocol timescale without altering the metrological ceiling or the circuit depth required to reach isotropy. The proposed scheme is relevant to cavity QED and NMR quantum processors, where the central spin architecture arises naturally.

articles.title: Scale-free localization in pseudo-Hermitian quantum walk
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31067v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Scale-free localization is a distinctive phenomenon in non-Hermitian systems, where specific eigenstates, known as scale-free localized states (LSs), possess localization lengths that scale linearly with the system size. Here, we show that a single non-Hermitian defect in one-dimensional quantum walks (QWs) induces scale-free localization. Driven by non-Hermiticity, the QW system undergoes a pseudo-Hermitian (PH) phase transition and the PH symmetry breaking is accompanied by the emergence of scale-free localization. As non-Hermiticity is further increased, the system undergoes a second phase transition, marked by the emergence of two pairs of bound states. Crucially, we identify the critical points of both transitions using localization properties. Furthermore, we extend our investigation to two-dimensional QWs, where a single non-Hermitian defect also induces scale-free localization, thereby demonstrating the universality of this phenomenon. Our work provides a valuable perspective for further exploring defect physics and a type of novel LS in non-Hermitian quantum systems.

articles.title: Fluctuation-free Quantum Battery Charging Enabled by Bell-like Entangled and Separable Charger States
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31242v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The implication of entanglement in quantum battery charging remains poorly understood. In addition, intrinsic quantum randomness poses a fundamental challenge to charging uniformity across distinct trials. To address these issues, we study a three-qubit system within a cascaded collision frame, with two qubits acting as the charger and the third serving as the battery. After each collision, an adaptive measurement is performed on the charger, yielding four conditional post-measurement battery states with identical expected stored energy. For arbitrary fixed charger states, we derive analytical expressions for the recurrence relation of stored energy. We find that stored-energy fluctuations depend on whether the dynamics relies on the battery phase (γₙ). For two Bell-like families of entangled states, together with their computational basis states termed Bell-like separable states, the dynamics is (γₙ)-independent and fluctuations vanish, whereas for other entangled and separable states, fluctuations emerge. These insights establish a paradigm for engineering charger states to design uniform-charging quantum-battery architectures despite inherent quantum randomness.

articles.title: Mixed State Deep Thermalization under Generic Quantum Errors
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31580v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Pure-state deep thermalization predicts that, after sufficient scrambling, projected ensembles approach universal distributions that contain information beyond the reduced density matrix. In realistic quantum systems, however, noise is unavoidable and the projected states are generally mixed. Whether mixed-state deep thermalization admits an analogous universal limiting distribution has remained unclear. Here we answer this question for quantum dynamics containing local quantum channels, i.e., errors. We show that the late-time mixed-state projected ensemble is completely determined by the normalized Choi state of the error channel and is universal, independent of the microscopic details of the underlying unitary dynamics. We establish this result analytically for dual-unitary circuits, global Haar-random dynamics, and local Haar-random circuits at large local dimension, and verify it numerically in qubit circuits and kicked Ising dynamics. In a solvable setting, we further find exponentially fast convergence to the limiting ensemble. Our results extend deep thermalization to noisy quantum dynamics and establish a direct correspondence between quantum errors and universal random mixed-state ensembles.

articles.title: The ideal limit of rhombohedral graphene: Dynamical skyrmion lattices and their excitations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2511.07402v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce an interacting ideal limit of rhombohedral graphene in which interactions spontaneously generate a correlated Chern insulator. Our analysis reveals that this Chern insulator can be understood as a layer-pseudospin skyrmion lattice stabilized by electronic interactions, and that it gives rise to genuine skyrmion lattice physics, complete with dynamics. This dynamical skyrmion lattice naturally leads to experimentally measurable consequences. In particular, we identify new collective excitations corresponding to chiral shape deformations of the skyrmions, and propose a new positively charged quasiparticle, the skyrmion vacancy. These results establish a qualitatively new form of moiré Chern physics in rhombohedral graphene: an interaction-generated skyrmion lattice whose skyrmions are dynamical low-energy degrees of freedom.

articles.title: Order-Disorder in Fe-Si Alloys: Implications for Seismic and Transport Properties of Earth's Inner Core
articles.abstract: arXiv:2511.22899v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Understanding the structure and dynamics of Earth's inner core is essential for constraining its composition, thermal evolution, and seismic behavior. Silicon is widely considered a major light element in the core. Here, we use first-principles molecular dynamics and thermodynamic modeling to investigate the structural, elastic, and transport properties of iron-silicon (Fe-Si) alloys under inner-core conditions. By computing the Gibbs free energies of multiple solid phases, including ordered B2, hexagonal close-packed (hcp), face-centered cubic (fcc), and body-centered cubic (bcc) Fe-Si, we construct a phase diagram relevant to inner-core pressures and temperatures. We identify a pronounced miscibility gap between hcp and cubic Fe--Si phases, with phase coexistence over approximately 6--11 wt% Si at 6000 K. The cubic phase exhibits a strong order-dependent elastic response, with disordered bcc showing a large intrinsic shear anisotropy (22.9% at 6000 K), in contrast to the nearly isotropic hcp phase (0.6%). Meanwhile, disordered bcc Fe--Si produces shear wave velocities (V_S=3.73 km·s⁻¹) and Poisson's ratios comparable with seismological constraints. In addition, disordered bcc Fe--Si exhibits a lower thermal conductivity than hcp Fe--Si, providing a quantitative constraint on phase-dependent electronic heat transport. These results demonstrate that chemical ordering strongly controls the stability and physical properties of cubic Fe--Si alloys, and suggest that metastable or localized cubic Fe--Si phases may contribute to the structural and transport complexity of Earth's inner core.

articles.title: Electrostatic edge effects versus edge doping in graphene nanoribbons: a scanning gate microscopy and modelling study
articles.abstract: arXiv:2602.12944v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The charge neutrality point (CNP) of graphene nanoribbons (GNRs) patterned by oxygen plasma etching moves towards zero as the ribbon narrows and, on 300 nm SiO2, changes sign below a crossover width of ~ 50 nm: an observation previously attributed to n-type edges surrounding a p-type bulk. We test this edge-doping hypothesis in three ways.
