articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.10787v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Language models trained with long-horizon agentic reinforcement learning can generalize knowledge through reasoning, express precise actions, and pursue goals over many steps, raising the ceiling on what an embodied agent can understand and decide. Physical interaction, however, remains the domain of action policies, which provide dense, low-latency control. We present NavGPT-3, a harness that connects the two models, with an OS-like runtime built above it: reasoning, acting, and monitoring run as threads with their own context, tools, and permissions, while the runtime schedules them and decides which thread controls the robot's motion, so that the robot can react to sudden real-world events through interruption and thread switching. Beneath it, our action policy NavGPT VLA, trained on 19.28M examples, allocates visual tokens using codec allocation, in proportion to scene change; its 8B model alone reaches 74.51 SR on R2R-CE and leads RxR-CE with 78.19 SR. With the complete harness, NavGPT-3 sets the state of the art on R2R-CE (81.51 SR) and, for the first time, brings an autonomous agent to human level: on RxR-CE it matches human followers in success (90.43 vs. 90.4 SR) and path fidelity (78.47 vs. 77.7 nDTW) at 1 min 22 s per episode, versus roughly 3 min for a human. We comprehensively ablate the harness design and the interaction between the two models, showing how tools and the action policy shape the path from language-model reasoning to physical control: when NavGPT VLA executes the route, the reasoning loop shortens and the system's minimum reaction time falls from 3-19 s per language-model decision to 0.5-1 s per action-policy step (1-2 Hz). These results show that designing this embodied interface is central to connecting frontier language-model intelligence with low-level physical control. We will release all models, code, and evaluation records.

articles.title: Transformed Samplers with Variance Reduction
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.10870v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods are the standard tool for computing expectations under complex probability distributions. Control variates reduce the variance of the resulting estimates, but a good control variate requires solving the Poisson equation of the sampler, which rarely admits a closed-form solution. Exact solutions are available when the sampler's kernel has a known spectral decomposition on a simple reference density. In our work, we extend these solutions to general targets through a learned change of variables. A bijection, such as a normalizing flow, is trained so that the target becomes close to the reference in a latent space, and we show that Markov kernels and their Poisson solutions are transformed by any bijection. Running such samplers in the latent space then yields explicit control variates, and the estimator is consistent under mild tail conditions on the map and target. Importance sampling (IS) from the flow is the limiting case of the same construction and the control variates apply to it as well. Experiments on synthetic targets and real posteriors compare the procedure against state-of-the-art samplers and control variates.

articles.title: Differentiable Systematic Resampling for Variational Sequential Monte Carlo
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.12094v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Particle filters are a standard tool for nonlinear state estimation, but their resampling step is discrete, preventing gradient-based learning in variational sequential Monte Carlo. We introduce Differentiable Systematic Resampling (DSR), a temperature-controlled relaxation of systematic resampling, that preserves the CDF-ordered, banded structure of systematic resampling while enabling full gradient flow. DSR converges to exact systematic resampling as the temperature vanishes, and we prove a pointwise exponential convergence rate for the induced bias. Compared to optimal-transport-based differentiable resampling, DSR avoids iterative solvers and has substantially lower computational overhead. Experiments on stochastic dynamical systems and real-world handwriting data show that DSR achieves comparable or superior filtering and dynamics learning performance.

articles.title: One Permutation Is All You Need: Fast, Deterministic Feature Importance and Model Stress-Testing
articles.abstract: arXiv:2512.13892v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Reliable estimation of feature contributions in machine learning models is essential for transparency, algorithmic fairness, and regulatory compliance. While permutation feature importance is widely used, classical implementations rely on repeated Monte Carlo shuffling, introducing significant computational overhead and stochastic instability. In this paper, we show that replacing B random permutations with a single, max-min rank-optimal deterministic permutation maintains or improves correlation with ground-truth importance while eliminating estimation variance and reducing complexity from O(B · n · p) to O(n · p). Under location-scale feature distributions, we formally prove exact recovery of scale-adjusted linear regression coefficients, alongside improved importance estimation under concave model sensitivity. We extend this deterministic framework along two complementary dimensions. First, Systemic Feature Importance (SFI) integrates empirical feature correlations to quantify indirect feature reliance through proxy variables. Second, Importance Direction extends scalar importance to a signed, directional representation by measuring concordance between covariate displacements and output shifts. Extensive empirical validation across nearly 200 simulation scenarios demonstrates superior bias-variance trade-offs in high-dimensional and low signal-to-noise regimes. Finally, two real-world credit risk case studies show how coupling SFI with Importance Direction enables practitioners and regulators to audit models for both the magnitude and net sign of hidden reliance on protected attributes, delivering a principled, transparent, and scalable framework for model governance.

articles.title: Kähler landscapes for complex neural network descents and guarantees including a search and destroy of the Calabi-Yau manifold
articles.abstract: arXiv:2608.19584v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study landscapes for complex-parameterized networks. Our approach is motivated with an information-theoretic manifold perspective of the parameter and via classical optimization guarantees although of complex geometric variety such as through Dolbeault asymptotics. The descent path admits a Kähler information metric under a cross-entropy via the Wirtinger Hessian on the log-likelihood potential. We restrict attention to a descent update rule with natural gradient descent via a differentiated loss scaled by the inverse metric, so the descent path remains in the holomorphic tangent bundle. We emphasize Calabi-Yau information manifolds which profane theoretical guarantees via an ill-curvature-conditioned landscape. We focus on Calabi-Yau metrics specifically in a non-compact setting with a global potential, so defined geometrically rather than invoking the topological requirements of the Calabi conjecture. In non-compact settings, we can write the metric determinant with respect to a background in terms of a pluriharmonic or real-valued function. Under bounded, nonuniform, and almost low-rank assumptions, we get a partial eigenvalue blow-up effect. In an empirical setting, a Ricci-flat metric will not form, but the blow-up effect is a local condition and can partially hold empirically on open sets. We isolate the Calabi-Yau case in a theoretical setting, and we counteract the corrupted geometries under regularization. Moreover, it has been discovered that negative curvature subverts the loss landscape, specifically sectional curvature, so we expand on this and draw interconnections to negative-definite Ricci curvature. Our arguments primarily exist via geometric analysis, although we establish roots in deep learning theory such as through asymptotics at initialization and connections through failure modes of neural network guarantees under vanishing and negative Ricci curvature.

articles.title: EvoSim: Learning to Model, Modeling to Learn
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.11344v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Physics-based models connect scientific explanation with quantitative prediction. Constructing them requires selecting physical processes, defining states and governing equations, specifying couplings, and identifying parameters from experiments. Existing AI systems remain limited in making these model structure decisions autonomously. We introduce EvoSim, a self-evolving AI scientist for physical modeling. It uses experimental discrepancies to drive mechanism and equation revisions and held-out experimental data to test physical plausibility. Exploration traces make updates to knowledge, skills, and multi-agent orchestration. This co-evolution improves physics-based models and EvoSim's ability to select mechanisms, diagnose failures, and coordinate research. We evaluate EvoSim on two industrial battery modeling tasks. It predicts lithium-metal-plating onset from 25 to 45 degrees Celsius and 2 C to 6 C with a mean absolute error of 1.79% in state of charge. Dynamic voltage prediction under vehicle driving conditions achieves a root mean square error of 7.62 mV, surpassing the reported accuracy of models developed by human experts. Self-evolution reduces model and physics errors by approximately 36% relative to baseline, demonstrating improved scientific modeling capability. EvoSim turns experimental observations into validated models and cumulative research expertise.

articles.title: PulseBound: Future-Beat State Forecasting Under an Explicit Information Boundary
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.12010v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Predictive representation learning from photoplethysmography (PPG) can violate causal information access even with causal attention, as normalization, nonlocal transforms, or companion views may depend on withheld samples. We introduce PulseBound, a PPG representation learner combining physiologically structured future-beat prediction with an explicit stored-window information boundary. A content-independent cutoff separates the visible prefix from the prediction target. Prefix-only normalization, suffix replacement before derived-view construction, and aligned masking ensure that encoder inputs depend only on the visible prefix and cutoff. This yields stored-suffix invariance: with fixed model state, randomness, prefix, and cutoff, changing the stored suffix cannot change the forecast context. A shared horizon-conditioned head predicts nine rhythm and morphology descriptors for up to four extractor-valid future beats, using elementwise validity masks; optional ECG-derived pulse-arrival-time supervision is restricted to training. On MIMIC and VitalDB groups held out from PulseBound backbone pretraining, PulseBound reduces nine-state transformed-space MAE relative to last-visible-beat persistence by 28.06% and 22.22%, respectively, with gains in MAE, MAE-Skill, and Spearman correlation across all 40 source-cutoff-horizon cells. In a separate comparison of seven models on 13 downstream tasks, PulseBound achieves the best mean on nine frozen linear-probe and seven full-fine-tuning tasks. Stored-suffix interventions cause zero recorded changes in forecast contexts or predictions, with zero suffix-input gradients at audited precision under the stored-window interface. These findings separate three testable aspects of predictive physiological representation learning: information access, supervised future structure, and transfer.

articles.title: Instruction-Conditioned Electromagnetic Spectrum Understanding via Budget-Adaptive Signal Tokenization
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.12142v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Electromagnetic spectrum monitoring increasingly requires flexible analysis beyond task-specific recognition and detection. Multimodal large language models offer a unified interface, but extending vision-language models (VLMs) to raw I/Q signals requires tokenization that balances fidelity against a strict budget. For signals, dense encoding causes token costs to grow with observation length, whereas fixed-resolution compression may discard short-duration or localized signal evidence. Thus, we propose BATok, a budget-adaptive signal tokenizer that adjusts token capacity to the input length while allocating that capacity according to the signal content. BATok constructs candidate representations from signal-derived features using lightweight multi-resolution branches, then combines a local energy prior with learnable queries to resample these representations into compact signal tokens. The number of tokens adapts to the input length while remaining strictly bounded. The resulting tokens are projected into the language embedding space of VLMs. We further introduce EMSpec-Instruct, a multimodal instruction dataset aligning raw I/Q signals, waterfall images, and language supervision for modulation recognition, structured detection, and language-conditioned signal grounding. Experiments show that BATok learns effective signal representations and achieves competitive performance across all tasks.

articles.title: When Has a Bayesian Neural Network Sampled Enough? Adaptive Inference Time with Statistical Guarantees
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.12212v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bayesian neural network predictions are commonly approximated using a fixed number of Monte Carlo samples per input, without controlling the resulting error that comes from this finite sample. We propose the use of confidence sequences to dynamically determine how many samples are needed while maintaining statistical guarantees. We consider several ways in which predictive probabilities are used, including identifying the most likely class, approximating the full predictive distribution, and resolving probability-threshold decisions. Sampling stops once the corresponding decision can be made with the desired guarantee. Experiments show that the method allocates the computational budget efficiently, assigning more samples to ambiguous inputs than to easy inputs while preserving reliable decisions and reducing overall latency relative to a fixed Monte Carlo budget.

articles.title: Identification and transference of candidate semiochemical volatile organic compounds (VOCs) from feed to the circulatory system in pigs
articles.abstract: Background Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) present in feeds contribute to sensory cues involved in dietary recognition and appetite in pigs which play a crucial role in the post-weaning transition. However, the feed volatilome and the patterns of absorption and potential transference to and stability in the circulatory system dietary VOCs remain poorly understood. The objectives of this study were to characterise the volatilome of common feed ingredients and determine which feed-associated VOCs can cross the gastrointestinal barrier and become detectable in blood. It was hypothesised that some dietary VOCs can be transferred to and show persist long enough in the circulatory system to play a potential semiochemical role.Methods Volatile profiles of 29 feed ingredients were characterised using headspace solid-phase microextraction coupled with gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (HS-SPME–GC-MS). Six catheterised piglets received oral gavage solutions containing a group of selected feed VOCs (~ 2.5 ppm per compound) in a repeated crossover design, and serial blood samples were collected up to 180 min after administration.Results A total of 569 VOCs were identified across feed ingredients, revealing specific volatilome signatures and common chemical group patterns characteristic for cereals, legumes, plant or animal-derived ingredients. Several feed-associated VOCs were detected in plasma before the experimental administration of the oral gavage, suggesting that dietary exposure contributed to the circulating volatilome. Following oral administration of the selected VOCs by gavage, pyrazine, 2-ethyl-3,5-dimethylpyrazine, nonanol, and 2-acetylfuran showed significantly greater plasma abundance than the control treatment (P < 0.05), demonstrating that feed-derived volatiles can become systemically detectable after ingestion persisting in circulation over extended periods of time. These findings are compatible with potential roles of some dietary VOCs as semiochemicals relevant to physiological mechanisms such as maternal imprinting which warrant further investigations.Conclusion Feed ingredients are associated to complex volatilomes. Some individual VOCs showed the ability to crossing the gastrointestinal barrier remaining systemically available for prolonged periods of time, establishing physiological links between feed and circulating volatilomes, unveiling a hypothetical role of feed-associated VOCs as semiochemicals in pigs.

articles.title: A geophysically constrained Transformer model for tropical cyclone track and intensity simulation over the western North Pacific and its contribution analysis
articles.abstract: Tropical cyclone represents one of the most devastating natural hazards in global coastal zones, inflicting massive economic damage and loss of life annually. Precise multi-step tropical cyclone forecasting is still confronted with great challenges, primarily attributed to intricate ocean-atmosphere interactions governing tropical cyclone movement. Here, we propose a geophysically constrained Transformer model to jointly predict tropical cyclone tracks and intensity using historical best-track records over the western North Pacific and reanalysis data, benchmarked against conventional XGBoost and LSTM models. Experimental results show that the geophysically constrained Transformer model realizes stable tropical cyclone forecasting, with track RMSEs of 200.72 km (6 h) and 357.02 km (36 h), and intensity RMSEs of 2.59 m/s (6 h) and 7.54 m/s (36 h). When compared with LSTM and XGBoost baselines, it reduces 6-hour track RMSE by 30% and 55%, and intensity RMSE by 23% and 36%, respectively, maintaining better accuracy over most forecast periods for both tasks. SHAP analysis further reveals that surface air pressure (contributing 32%) and wind speed (contributing 25%) are the dominant predictive variables for tropical cyclone track and intensity forecasting. By contrast, large-scale circulation and sea surface temperature function as secondary influencing factors, which further validates the physical interpretability and rationality of the developed model.. Overall, our findings advance the integration of deep learning techniques with meteorological and geophysical datasets for real-time operational tropical cyclone prediction, yielding critical implications for tropical cyclone monitoring and disaster risk governance.

articles.title: Second-Harmonic Generation Through Backward Raman Scattering in Magnetized Plasmas Driven by Circularly Polarized Intense Lasers
articles.abstract: The nonlinear dynamics of backward Raman scattering (BRS) in a magnetized plasma channel driven by an intense circularly polarized laser pulse are investigated through a combined analytical and numerical approach, with emphasis on the emergence and controllability of a secondary spectral peak. The analysis is performed in the relativistic laser–plasma interaction regime under experimentally relevant plasma densities and axial magnetic-field strengths. A fluid-based theoretical framework is developed to describe the nonlinear cascade linking primary BRS-driven plasma wave amplification, oscillating two-stream instability (OTSI), nonlinear current generation within a self-formed ponderomotive channel, and radiation of the secondary electromagnetic mode. Systematic parameter studies reveal a strong sensitivity of the entire cascade to the relative handedness of laser polarization and axial magnetic field direction, as well as to cyclotron resonance strength. Resonant right-handed circular polarization significantly enhances ponderomotive expulsion, channel depth, BRS and OTSI growth rates, nonlinear current density, and the amplitude of the secondary harmonic, whereas non-resonant left-handed polarization effectively suppresses these processes. Fully kinetic particle-in-cell simulations using EPOCH, together with macroscopic finite-element modelling in COMSOL Multiphysics, corroborate the polarization- and magnetization-dependent wake modulation and channelling efficiency across a wide range of laser wavelengths, pulse durations, and plasma densities. The temporal evolution and saturation of OTSI, resilience to density inhomogeneities, and wavenumber-resolved resonance tuning illustrate axial magnetization as a flexible control mechanism for adjusting the intensity, spectral position, bandwidth, and stability of multi-peak Raman spectra. These findings demonstrate that cyclotron resonance and polarization control are effective methods for manipulating nonlinear Raman emission in high-intensity laser–magnetized plasma interactions, offering predictive insights for forthcoming kinetic simulations and experimental implementations. PACS: 52.38.-r, 52.35.Mw, 52.65.Rr

articles.title: Structural Construction of the Uniqueness Statement for the Riemann Hypothesis A Chain Map between the Additive and Multiplicative Sides, a Well-Defined Obstruction Functional, and a Spectral Uniqueness Theorem
articles.abstract: The Riemann zeta function admits two presentations whose equality is pure arithmetic: the additive Dirichlet series ∑₍ₙ ≥ ₁₎ n⁽⁻s⁾ and the multiplicative Euler product ∏ï¿¿(1-p⁽⁻s⁾)⁻¹ coincide, for Re s > 1, by the fundamental theorem of arithmetic alone. Yet the free structures that carry the two presentations have different rank — rank 1 for the additive side, rank |ℙ| = ∞ for the multiplicative side — so the numerical identity of the two presentations is not accompanied by any structural identity. This rank gap is the precise locus at which the Riemann Hypothesis (RH) acquires structural, as opposed to merely numerical, content. We carry the corresponding structural programme to completion and isolate a single remaining item. Six constructions are established. (i) A chain map. Using the fundamental theorem of arithmetic we construct the explicit map φ(n) = ∑ï¿¿ vï¿¿(n)[p] from the multiplicative side into the free abelian group on the primes, and prove that it is a group homomorphism and an injection but not a surjection. Whence the rank-gap theorem: no chain map between the two sides induces an isomorphism on homology, so the requirement that the two sides be homotopy equivalent is not merely unproven but impossible. (ii) A well-defined obstruction functional. The obstruction δ_ζ, previously written as the pointwise series ∑ï¿¿(log p)θï¿¿/π, which diverges on the critical line, is redefined in the cumulative form δ_ζ(x) = ψ(x)-x + log 2π + 1/2log(1-x⁻²) =-∑_ρ x^ρ/ρ. Its two sides — primes and zeros — agree numerically, with relative residual decaying from 1.64 × 10⁻² at x = 10² to 1.06 × 10⁻⁴ at x = 10⁵. (iii) A spectral uniqueness theorem. If a self-adjoint operator H has the non-trivial zero ordinates as its spectrum, then H is unique up to unitary equivalence; a Jordan-block counterexample shows that self-adjointness is load-bearing, and the eigenvalue counting function is locked to the Riemann–von Mangoldt density, so the operator carries no continuous free parameter. (iv) A topological bridge. The Chern character ch = (rank, c₁) maps both sides into a common cohomology ring and satisfies a discrete Gauss–Bonnet identity, providing the topological dual of the analytic (explicit-formula) bridge. (v) A structural baseline. The critical line is not assumed. The value 1/2 is returned independently by the reflection symmetry of the completed zeta function (analytic route) and by the self-normalisation exponent of the quadratic Gauss sum, |G(p)| = √(p) (arithmetic route, using no analytic input); the two coincide, so Re s = 1/2 is a structural output rather than a convention. Moreover the discrete reciprocity character lifts to the continuous local Euler phase only at this baseline — the seam lift — which closes the apparent type mismatch between the discrete symbol ± 1 and the continuous angle. (vi) A dynamical route. The critical line is characterised dynamically as well as geometrically: the de Bruijn–Newman backwards heat flow Hï¿¿(z) = ∫₀^∞ e⁽tu²⁾Phi(u)cos(zu)du (with H₀ = 1/8ξ(1/2 + iz/2)) has all real zeros exactly for t ≥ Λ, with RH ⇔ Λ = 0; and its zero dynamics is the gradient flow of the logarithmic Hamiltonian H(t) = ∑_(j ≠ k)log(1/| xï¿¿-xï¿¿|), whose energy E(t) = ∑₍ⱼ ≠ ₖ₎| xï¿¿-xï¿¿|⁻² is monotone non-increasing, so that least dissipation forces the configuration to an equal-spacing equilibrium (Rodgers–Tao; Polymath 15). The route is read in reverse: the flow necessarily possesses a baseline, but it moves in the real variable and cannot select the vertical line — that baseline is the value 1/2 already fixed, independently, by the spatial argument of §7.7, so the dynamics meets it rather than deriving it. This localises the open item to a single real number, bracketed unconditionally by 0 ≤ Λ ≤ 0.22, and reduces it to the assertion that the arithmetic datum already sits on the baseline (§6.7). The two quantities this reading rests on are formalised in §6.8: the dissipation work W = ∫ Edt = 1/4Δ H, and the reciprocal efficiency η = Eï¿¿ₐï¿¿/E₍ₐcₜ₎ ∈ (0,1], maximal (η = 1) exactly at the density-matched equal-spacing ground state. The remaining item — the Hilbert–Pólya existence statement — is shown not to be a notion without content: it is equivalent to the Li positivity criterion λï¿¿ ≥ 0 for all n and to Weil positivity, and the Li partial sums are numerically positive for n ≤ 20. It is moreover localised, not left as an unlocated gap. In two directly comparable structures — function fields (Weil 1948) and compact hyperbolic surfaces (Selberg 1956) — the analogue of RH is a theorem, because there the relevant operator is self-adjoint for free, by a positive-definite pairing (an ample polarisation, a Riemannian metric). The arithmetic case has the same schematic form with that positivity missing, and supplying it is exactly RH (§6.6). It is localised a second time, dynamically, to the single scalar Λ = 0 of de Bruijn–Newman, bracketed unconditionally by 0 ≤ Λ ≤ 0.22 (§6.7). The discrete zero positions on those structures are computed and compared: for 123 elliptic curves over í µí´½ï¿¿ every Frobenius eigenvalue satisfies |α| = √(p) and every zero lies on Re s = 1/2 (worst deviation 1.1 × 10⁻¹⁶), matching the line and the mechanism, while the density laws differ (Weyl r² against Riemann–von Mangoldt). Every item recorded as a gap in an earlier treatment is accounted for: eleven of twelve are closed by a named theorem or proposition — including the items earlier described only as "limitations", which are upgraded to non-decidability theorems — and the twelfth is ES itself, now localised (§10.11). The paper therefore reduces RH, along this route, to one sharply stated existence problem with a computable positivity form, a named localisation, and a two-sided bracket, and reports the exact boundary of what the construction does and does not settle.

articles.title: A simple 2,4-dihydroxyacetophenone based fluorescent chemosensor for detection of copper(II) ion: An Experimental and DFT study
articles.abstract: The detection of copper ions is of significant importance due to their widespread use and potential toxicity at elevated concentrations. In this study, a bis Schiff’s base compound; 4-(1-(cyclohexylidenehydrazono) ethyl) benzene-1,3-diol (BS) was used for the first time as a “Turn off” fluorescent chemosensor of Cu(II) ion in water samples with characteristics of aggregation induced enhanced emission (AIEE) at 510 nm upon excitation at 405 nm. BS showed high selectivity towards Cu(II) ions with considerable fluorescence quenching and was found interference free in the presence of other metal ions in mixed solution of methanol-water (v/v,1:9) at pH 8. Fluorescence intensity of BS was observed to decrease due the formation of non-fluorescent complex (Cu@BS) due to the paramagnetic effect from spin-orbit coupling and partial d shell of Cu (II). DFT simulations were performed to gain theoretical insight into the interaction of Cu(II) with BS. The value calculated for limit of detection (LOD) was 0.26 µM, and percent recovery of above 90% was achieved from spiked water samples. This novel turn-off fluorescent sensor offers a simple, cost-effective, and reliable method for the rapid detection of copper ions, making it a valuable tool for environmental monitoring and ensuring the safety of water resources.

articles.title: Numerical investigation on the heat and mass transfer enhanced by Triply-Periodic-Minimal-Surface (TPMS) configuration in flow chemistry
articles.abstract: The continuous flow reaction technology has been widely recognized and developed due to its inherent safety, process control, reaction efficiency, etc. But the consistency of heat and mass transfer during the scale-up of continuous flow reactors remains a major challenge, and few reliable evaluation methods are currently available. In this work, a novel TPMS-based flow reactor is developed with characteristic length of 6mm, utilizing interconnected flow passages to enhance flow mixing and heat transfer. The flow pattern in the TPMS reactor is experimentally analyzed to exhibit near-ideal plug flow. Based on the decoupled CFD framework proposed in the present study, the flow, heat and mass transfer, and reaction kinetics in the TPMS reactor are numerically analyzed and compared with the traditional tubular flow reactors (diameters of 3mm and 6 mm). The TPMS reactor is demonstrated with superior heat transfer performance to maintain expected temperature and to achieve high selectivity. Under the condition of hypothetical pilot-scale extremely exothermic reaction, the advantages of the lab-scale TPMS reactor are further highlighted, especially for the increasing dominance of the side reactions. Therefore, the TPMS reactor is much potentially applied to nitration, lithiation, diazotization, etc., with few scale-up effects on the heat and mass transfer, and reaction performance. The numerical method provides a practical and effective solution for industrial scale-up design and optimization, with reasonable computational resources and efficiency.

articles.title: Out-of-plane orbital torque from orbital-to-spin conversion in a low-symmetry system
articles.abstract: Orbitronics has recently emerged as a focus of intensive research toward energy-efficient magnetic memories. A pivotal process in this field is orbital-to-spin conversion, which is indispensable for the electrical manipulation of local magnetic moments. However, this conversion is fundamentally governed by crystal symmetry, which forbids any out-of-plane spin response in high-symmetry systems. Here we demonstrate that this restriction can be lifted in A1-CoPt/Ru bilayers with three-fold mirror symmetry at the interface. The broken mirror symmetry allows an unconventional orbital-to-spin conversion process, giving rise to an out-of-plane orbital torque from in-plane polarized orbital current and enabling deterministic field-free switching of perpendicular magnetization. First-principles calculations reveal that this unconventional conversion originates from the swapping effect in low-symmetry systems and its efficiency is substantially enhanced at the CoPt/Ru bilayer compared with the bulk CoPt. Our findings generalize symmetry-tailored torque generation from spintronics to orbitronics and identifies orbital injectors combined with low-symmetry conversion layers as a materials-design route towards field-free and energy-efficient magnetic-memory devices.

articles.title: BTELab, a MATLAB Programme Code for solving Quantum Boltzmann Transport Equation with all Collision Terms within Trapping Potential
articles.abstract: This paper presents Quantum Boltzmann Transport Equation Laboratory (QBTELab), an advanced easy-to-use toolbox to solve many complex problems related to Bose-Einstein Condensate (BEC). The model equation that BTELab solves is the Quantum Boltzmann Transport Equation (QBTE) with all collision terms within trapping potential. Inelastic scattering (Exciton-phonon collision), elastic scattering (exciton-exciton collision), Auger decay and radiative non-radiative decay are included here as the collision terms. The programme code has been written in MATLAB. From the results it can be said that the programme is working properly and it has enough numerical stability. The aim of this paper is to provide programme code to solve the full QBTE. QBTE is a powerful tool for investigating the transport phenomena in various systems like semiconductors, plasmas, nuclear reactors, heat transfer process, fluid dynamics etc and specially different problems related to BEC.

articles.title: Reinforcement Learning-Based Real-Time Control of a Photovoltaic-Integrated Welding Power Supply: Experimental Validation and Performance Benchmarking
articles.abstract: The integration of photovoltaic (PV) generation with industrial arc welding equipment offers a pathway toward sustainable manufacturing, but the intermittent nature of solar power and the highly dynamic, nonlinear behavior of the welding arc pose significant control challenges. This paper presents the design, hardware implementation, and experimental validation of a PV-integrated, high-frequency welding power supply governed by a hierarchical control architecture: a fast inner-loop proportional-integral (PI) controller regulating arc current, and a slower outer-loop reinforcement learning (RL) policy that performs adaptive gain scheduling in response to time-varying arc length and PV availability. The hardware prototype, built around silicon carbide (SiC) MOSFET conversion stages, was validated on both a laboratory-scale bench and an industrial-scale 5 kW test bed under variable arc lengths, pulsed welding loads, and PV-emulated intermittency. Experimental results show that the proposed system achieves an energy efficiency of approximately 90%, a total harmonic distortion (THD) of approximately 4%, a dynamic response time improvement of up to 33% relative to a conventional PI controller, and reduced energy consumption per weld cycle, outperforming battery-buffered, PI-only, and rule-based baselines across all benchmarked metrics. To complement the hardware results and provide a fully reproducible definition of the RL control methodology, a simulation-based study was additionally conducted, explicitly modeling arc-length-induced process-gain variation as documented in the welding literature. Across multiple independent disturbance realizations, the trained RL policy reduced mean tracking error by approximately 25% relative to a fixed-gain PI baseline, with efficiency comparable to the best baseline and a modest trade-off in switching-related harmonic content. These findings demonstrate that RL-augmented control offers measurable advantages for renewable-energy-powered industrial power electronics under realistic operating uncertainty.

articles.title: Analytical Study of Rotating Mhd Flows Through Porous Materials With Constant Inclination by Complex Variable Techniques
articles.abstract: The steady, two-dimensional, incompressible, electrically conducting MHD fluid flows through porous media in a rotating reference frame in a magnetic field environment are taken into consideration in this work. This particular instance involves the magnetic field being constantly inclined toward the velocity field. Using complex variable technique by employing the variables (z=x+iy)and (bar z=x - iy)to recast the equations in solvable form an analytic solution for parallel flow and radial flow are obtained while the non-existence of steady vortex flows is established. Using this hybrid framework, exact solutions for MHD planar flows through a porous structure under non-zero constantly angles are obtained. Specifically, two forms of the complex variable technique representing radial flow and parallel flow are considered as applications with corresponding exact solutions for velocity, magnetic field, vorticity, stream function, and pressure for constantly inclined MHD flows in porous formation. The results function as benchmark solutions, establishing an objective point of reference for validating the accuracy of approximation models and mathematical simulations of MHD porous formation. The streamlines and each case's velocity profile are graphically depicted. Additionally, the variations in pressure concerning the parameter for porous formation with a fixed density and concerning density at a constant porous media parameter are graphically analyzed for both forms, leading to suitable conclusions.

articles.title: High-power ultrabroadband electro-optic frequency combs in thin-film lithium niobate
articles.abstract: Coherent conversion between microwave and optical fields underpins technologies ranging from high data-rate optical communications and photonic computing to precision sensing, frequency metrology, and emerging quantum networks that link superconducting quantum processors over optical fiber. Non resonant electro-optic (EO) modulation provides a deterministic, broadband, chip-scale route to such conversion, coherently bridging microwave signals in the gigahertz domain with optical fields at hundreds of terahertz for signal transduction and coherent frequency comb generation. However, compared with all-optical nonlinear interactions, the inherently weak EO interaction demands substantially long effective interaction lengths for efficient conversion, placing stringent requirements on microwave attenuation, phase matching, and optical propagation loss to maintain coherent phase accumulation. Here, we overcome these challenges by extending coherent traveling-wave EO interactions to unprecedented lengths on ultralow-loss thin-film lithium niobate EO circuits. Our 9 cm traveling-wave modulators achieve sub-volt half-wave voltages up to 23 GHz and below 1.5 V up to 38 GHz. Cascaded and folded recycling architectures extend the EO interaction length to 36 cm within a 2.4 cm2 footprint, enabling a phase-modulation depth of 86.6π and 32% comb efficiency. The resulting cavity-free EO comb comprises more than 550 lines within a 52 nm (6.5 THz) 10-dB bandwidth at an 11.78 GHz line spacing, with a single comb spectrum extending across the S-, C-, and L-bands. In a complementary 30.7 GHz-drive architecture, an optical loss per modulation depth as low as 0.02 dB/π enables 187 mW of comb power with 77% pump-to-comb conversion efficiency, while wavelength multiplexed operation further extends the accessible coherent bandwidth to over 23 THz. Together, these results establish a scalable traveling-wave architecture for extending coherent microwave optical interaction toward the meter scale, opening new regimes of EO transduction, frequency synthesis, and quantum networking.

articles.title: Intelligent Test Case Scheduling Using Multi-Criteria Decision Making for Human–Machine Interface Testing
articles.abstract: Factory testing of industrial human–machine interface (HMI) system is typically conducted under stringent constraints: a fixed and non-extendable time budget, limited test resources, and zero tolerance for undetected critical failures. Under these conditions, the order and selection of test cases constitute a quality-risk decision rather than a mere efficiency concern. In practice, however, test case selection relies largely on engineers' experience and ad-hoc checklists, resulting in inconsistent coverage, inefficient resource use, and poor reproducibility across releases. To address this gap, we propose a Time-Weighted Utility Scoring Model (TWUSM) for automated test case prioritization and selection. The model evaluates each test case along three dimensions (risk impact on system safety, functional importance, and testing cost) and combines them into a single utility score that is updated with historical execution feedback. Test cases are then assigned to priority tiers: those above a predefined threshold are deterministically included as mandatory tests, while the remainder are admitted by probabilistic sampling with probability proportional to their normalized scores. This hybrid scheme enforces quality first by guaranteeing complete verification of critical functionalities, and then, subject to this constraint, maximizes fault detection per unit of testing time. Evaluated on an industrial HMI system, TWUSM achieves 100% detection of critical failures and an APFD of 0.9987. Compared with full test-suite execution (425.9 s), it reduces testing time to 174.9 s (− 58.9%) without any loss of failure coverage. The results show that utility-based prioritization can provide a reproducible, resource-aware basis for inspection planning in safety-critical industrial software, assuring product quality while substantially reducing test duration.

articles.title: Determination of Intermolecular Potential Parameters: Theory and Applications
articles.abstract: In this study, advanced quantum-mechanical methods are employed to determine the fundamental parameters of intermolecular interaction potentials with high accuracy. Based on the intermolecular potential energy surface data, the parameters for the Lennard-Jones (12 − 6), Morse, and Kihara potentials for the Ar-Ar and Kr-Kr dimers were determined through a fitting procedure. In order to assess the accuracy and reliability of the derived potential parameters, the second and third virial coefficients were calculated. To verify the accuracy of the proposed method, the intermolecular potential energy surface (PES) for Ar-Ar and Kr-Kr dimer molecules was calculated using quantum chemical ab initio methods. Interaction energies for various configurations of the Ar-Ar and Kr-Kr dimers have been evaluated at the CCSD(T) level of theory, employing the aug-cc-pV5Z basis set, extended with bond functions. The results demonstrated a high level of agreement with the experimental data reported in the literature.

articles.title: The Manifold Mismatch: Topological Constraints and Non-Human Agency in Complex Adaptive Urban Systems
articles.abstract: Urban space has historically been constructed through specific representational frameworks, measurement technologies, and regulatory instruments. Across centuries, cities have been planned, analyzed, and governed according to Euclidean geometries and rational, property-oriented terrestrial imperatives that presuppose the human actor as the sovereign agent of spatial production. Computational design methods have largely perpetuated this anthropocentric comfort, functioning as passive instruments that optimize human utilities rather than interrogating the ontological assumptions underlying urban form. However, this study introduces the concept of the Manifold Mismatch — defined as the structural ontological tension between top-down human geometric ordering and the bottom-up non-Euclidean manifolds generated by ecological, geomorphological, and algorithmic forces. Drawing on posthuman theory, actor-network theory, and assemblage thinking, it subjects the problem of coding urban knowledge to a fourfold methodological genealogy: (1) rule-based and generative systems, (2) topological and relational analyses, (3) dynamic and complexity-based simulations, and (4) probabilistic and artificial intelligence-driven models. The anthropocentric limitations of this genealogy are then systematically expanded through the lens of posthuman urbanism, validated through a comprehensive compendium of 29 historical and contemporary empirical cases drawn from global contexts. The analyses confirm a tripartite taxonomic matrix of non-human urban agency: Algorithmic Subjects, Sensing Infrastructures, and Ecological Actants. The paper concludes by proposing a synthetic meta-methodology that redefines urban design not as a top-down imposition of rational form, but as a continuous, negotiated, multi-species assemblage in which human and non-human actors co-produce the city.

articles.title: Soft-x-ray free-electron laser pulses stabilize a competing order in helimagnet
articles.abstract: Intense light pulses can drive quantum materials away from equilibrium and access states that are absent under ordinary conditions. Whether resonant soft-x-ray free-electron laser (XFEL) pulses can persistently modify an ordered phase, rather than merely probe or damage it, remains an important question. Here we show that soft-x-ray XFEL exposure stabilizes a short-range incommensurate order in the itinerant helimagnet CrAs. Pristine CrAs exhibits only the native helical magnetic reflection, whereas after XFEL irradiation a second Cr-resonant peak appears at a distinct wave vector and remains observable by synchrotron resonant soft-x-ray scattering. This induced order develops below T∗ ≈ 230 K, has a correlation length of approximately 4 nm, and exhibits polarization-dependent resonant scattering with a modified Cr 3d spectral fingerprint. X-ray absorption and electron microscopy show that the CrAs framework is largely preserved while the near-surface lattice environment is locally modified. Time-resolved measurements further show that the induced order is optically suppressible and recovers on a picosecond timescale. These results establish soft-x-ray FEL pulses as an active perturbation for selecting competing orders in fragile correlated magnets.

articles.title: Disentangling the Coupled Origins of Li+ Ion Transport in LATP through Hierarchical Modeling
articles.abstract: Aliovalent substitution in solid electrolytes simultaneously modifies carrier concentration , framework chemistry, structure, and disorder, hindering mechanistic understanding of ion transport. Here, we combine a fine-tuned machine-learning foundation potential, energy-landscape analysis, and molecular dynamics simulations to investigate Li + ion diffusion across the full compositional range of the NASICON electrolyte Li1+x Alx Ti2−x(PO4)3 (0 ≤ x ≤ 2). A MACE foundation model trained on a single composition transfers across the substitution range, enabling efficient simulations of large disordered systems. By systematically separating carrier-concentration, framework, and structural contributions, we identify the mechanisms governing transport across the LATP composition range. Al substitution reshapes the framework potential, producing trapping at low Al content and connected low-energy pathways at high Al content , but does not itself explain the transport trend. Instead, additional Li lowers effective barriers through ion–ion interactions and drives the initial increase in diffusivity. The decline at high substitution emerges only when composition-dependent cell relaxation is considered together with framework dynamics and is associated with reduced cell volume and stronger Li–O interactions. Beyond explaining the non-monotonic transport behavior of LATP, this work shows how computational models of increasing physical complexity can isolate mechanisms that are difficult to disentangle experimentally or in fully coupled simulations. This hierarchical strategy offers a broadly applicable approach to composition–structure–transport relationships in configurationally complex materials.

articles.title: A barrier shielding geostationary orbit from relativistic killer electrons
articles.abstract: The transport, confinement, and accessibility of energetic charged particles in magnetized plasmas are fundamental problems spanning laboratory, space, and astrophysical environments. Earth's radiation belts provide a natural laboratory for investigating these processes, hosting relativistic ("killer") electrons that pose significant hazards to spacecraft systems and human activities in space. Plasma injections in the nightside magnetosphere transport substantial electromagnetic energy and are widely recognized as a major source of seed populations for radiation-belt acceleration. However, it remains unclear whether relativistic electrons accelerated during these injections can directly access and replenish the radiation belts. Determining whether energetic electrons can be accelerated outside the radiation belts and subsequently penetrate into the inner magnetosphere is therefore central to understanding radiation-belt variability and the broader question of how magnetic topology regulates energetic-particle transport. Here we combine multi-platform observations with advanced magnetic field modeling to show that relativistic electrons can form outside the radiation belts yet remain excluded from them by a magnetic transport barrier. Our results reveal a previously unrecognized constraint on magnetosphere-radiation belt coupling, demonstrating that particle acceleration and particle accessibility are distinct physical processes.

articles.title: Spatially Correlated Measurement Error: Bias Amplification and Identification via Higher-Order Spatial Lags
articles.abstract: Measurement error in spatial data is often cross-sectionally dependent. While the classical errors-in-variables literature assumes independence, this paper shows that spatial dependence fundamentally changes both the magnitude of attenuation bias and the validity of standard spatial instrumental-variable strategies. We characterize how spatially correlated measurement errors amplify attenuation bias through network propagation. Under a spatial moving average (SMA) structure with finite memory, and under an explicitly maintained geometric α‑mixing condition on the joint random field (Assumption A), spatial lags beyond a threshold become approximately orthogonal to the measurement error, with the approximation error decaying geometrically in the lag order. Building on this result, we develop a plausibly exogenous GMM estimator based on higher-order spatial moments. Monte Carlo simulations show bias reductions of 70‑80%, RMSE reductions of 45‑60%, and coverage close to nominal levels relative to OLS and conventional spatial IV estimators. An application to regional infrastructure and development in Tunisia illustrates the methodology, with explicit discussion of the severe limitation of n = 24 spatial units. All theoretical results are derived under increasing-domain asymptotics with bounded-degree graphs and rely exclusively on the maintained geometric mixing assumption (Assumption A). JEL Classification : C13, C21, C26, R15

articles.title: Bacterial-dominated niche partitioning and metabolic plasticity are associated with phosphorus acquisition in pure and mixed Cotinus coggygria forests
articles.abstract: Aims Cotinus coggygria, a pioneer tree species in the Three Gorges Reservoir Area, is increasingly constrained by progressive phosphorus (P) limitation under long-term monoculture. Mixed-species plantations may alleviate this stress by reshaping the root–soil microbiota, but the underlying microecological mechanisms remain unclear.Methods Here, we examined soil properties, extracellular enzyme stoichiometry, and microbial community assembly across bulk soil, rhizosphere, and endosphere niches in pure C. coggygria stands (C) and two mixed stands (C. coggygria + Quercus acrodonta, CQ; C. coggygria + Pinus massoniana, CPM).Results Mixed stands had lower total P but 99.64% (CQ) and 82.72% (CPM) higher specific phosphatase activity (SPA) than pure stands, driven mainly by downregulation of C- and N-acquiring enzymes and enhanced acid phosphatase (ACP) investment. Enzyme stoichiometry indicated stronger P limitation in CQ than in C and CPM. Along the root–soil interface, bacteria in mixed stands re-established a clear bulk soil–rhizosphere–endosphere filtration gradient, whereas fungi showed strong host conservatism, with dark septate endophytes (e.g., Cladophialophora) dominating the endosphere. The two mixing patterns differed: CQ featured lower bulk soil pH and elevated ACP activity, whereas CPM developed a more complex and connected bacterial co-occurrence network with high average degree and low competitive antagonism.Conclusions These results suggest that mixed planting, especially conifer-broadleaf mixtures, may enhance microbial investment in phosphorus acquisition through bacterial niche differentiation and increased network connectivity. However, direct measurements are needed to determine whether these responses increase phosphorus mobilization and plant phosphorus uptake.

articles.title: Improvement of the fatigue strength of high-strength steels by post-weld treatments for weld geometry optimization
articles.abstract: High-strength steels offer considerable potential for lightweight welded structures, but their increased base material strength is not apparent in the fatigue strength of welded joints. This study investigates the influence of weld geometry optimization by post-weld treatment on the fatigue behaviour of high-strength steel butt joints. The experimental programme compares the base material, the as-welded condition, and different post-weld treated conditions, including tungsten inert gas (TIG) dressing, burr grinding, and flush grinding. Fatigue tests were evaluated together with weld geometry measurements, residual stress analyses, and fracture surface investigations in order to identify the dominant mechanisms controlling crack initiation and fatigue strength improvement. The results show that the base materials exhibit fatigue strengths up to FAT classes of FAT434 far above commonly assumed design values, whereas the as-welded joints remain governed by the weld toe notch and achieve substantially lower fatigue classes according to current guidelines. Post-weld treatment significantly improves fatigue performance, although the effectiveness depends strongly on the treatment method and execution quality. Flush grinding achieves the highest improvement with a FAT260 by removing the weld reinforcement and shifting crack initiation from the weld toe to the base material. Tungsten inert gas dressing also increased fatigue strength, but crack initiation was displaced to the transition of the remelted zone. Burr grinding showed only moderate improvement due to remaining local surface notches. The findings demonstrate that high-strength steels require a differentiated fatigue assessment that accounts for post-weld treatment quality and local weld geometry.

articles.title: Phonon-mode-specific spin-flip scattering dictated ultrafast demagnetization in a van der Waals ferromagnet
articles.abstract: Ultrafast spin relaxation in van der Waals magnets is central to high-speed spin-based memory technologies, however, the mode-specific role of phonons in spin relaxation remains unresolved. Here, we investigate the temperature-dependent ultrafast demagnetization of van der Waals ferromagnetic CrTe₂ films using time-resolved magneto-optical Kerr effect measurements and Raman spectroscopy. By integrating Allen’s electron–phonon coupling theory with Koopmans’ microscopic three-temperature model and mode-resolved Raman spectroscopy, we uncover a temperature-dependent redistribution of phonon contributions to spin-flip scattering. Specifically, E₂g-associated scattering predominates at low temperatures, whereas the relative participation of the A₁g mode increases at elevated temperatures. Spin–orbit-coupling inclusive real-time time-dependent density functional theory calculations further show that the E₂g mode induce greater spin moment loss and stronger population transfer between spin channels than the A₁g mode, establishing the higher efficiency of E₂g-associated scattering in driving ultrafast spin relaxation. Combined with the experimentally observed redistribution, this mode-specific difference accounts for the lower spin-flip probability and slower spin relaxation at elevated temperatures. By resolving the lattice contribution into distinct phonon channels, our results establish a phonon-mode-specific framework for understanding Elliott–Yafet spin relaxation in van der Waals magnets, moving beyond the conventional treatment of phonons as an undifferentiated bath.

articles.title: Topological Data Analysis combined with Machine Learning for Predicting Permeability of Porous Media
articles.abstract: Flow in porous media is challenging to address using standard analytical or numerical methods due to the geometrical complexity. However, since synthetic representations of porous media are easy to produce and data from physical experiments are becoming more widely available, the problem is well-suited to studies that include machine learning (ML) techniques. We discuss a number of features that can be extracted from such synthetic or experimental data, and their utility as input variables into a standard ML algorithm. These features include structural measures describing the geometry of the porous media, topological measures describing the connectivity, and network measures obtained by modeling the porous media as simplified pore networks. These features enable the prediction of the permeability of the considered (synthetic) porous materials using ML techniques that also leverage the separately computed exact permeability (ground truth). Comparing results obtained using different input variables helps develop a better understanding of the utility of various measures for predicting permeability based on the porous media structure. We show, in particular, that topological data analysis (TDA) provides a useful set of features that can be easily combined with ML to yield meaningful results.

articles.title: Ultrafast core-level spectroscopy reveals elusive precursors of exciton condensation in quantum materials
articles.abstract: Many fascinating phases in quantum materials emerge when electrons, atoms and other microscopic components begin to act collectively. But these phases do not necessarily appear out of nowhere when a material crosses a transition temperature. Before long-range order develops, microscopic fluctuations can already be present.

articles.title: Superconducting circuit links smaller photon groups into larger entangled states
articles.abstract: Quantum computers, computer systems that leverage the laws of quantum mechanics, store and process information using qubits (i.e., quantum bits). In many quantum computers, qubits are linked via entanglement, a quantum mechanical effect that connects particles in such a way that their shared state cannot be described as separate, independent states.

articles.title: How researchers tell different quantum excitations apart in individual molecules
articles.abstract: Molecules can be placed in a wide variety of quantum states. How can these states be distinguished in measurements when theoretical models are unreliable? Which excitation process lies behind which measurement signal?

articles.title: Gravity and light reveal how liquids turn into thin fibers
articles.abstract: From spiders spinning their webs to the manufacturing of textiles, the formation of fibers from liquids plays an important role in both nature and industry. Yet accurately predicting the properties of such fibers remains a challenge. The fiber is often much thinner than the nozzle from which a polymer or solution is extruded. Factors such as temperature, flow conditions and chemical reactions ultimately determine a fiber's thickness and strength.

articles.title: Efficiency fluctuations in quantum heat engines with non-quasi-static adiabatic strokes
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.10647v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We have presented an analytical and numerical study of efficiency fluctuations in quantum Carnot and Otto engines with pistons operating under non-quasi-static adiabatic expansion and compression processes at constant speed, along with quasi-static isothermal (for the Carnot engine) or isochoric processes (for the Otto engine). We have considered the two-point measurement scheme during the adiabatic strokes in this regard. By considering each of the pistons as a single quantum particle in a 1-D box with a non-quasi-statically movable boundary, we capture the stochastic nature of the work output resulting from the unitary evolution of the quantum mechanical state of the system during non-equilibrium processes. Furthermore, we have explicitly shown how the piston speed during quantum non-equilibrium strokes introduces additional quantum fluctuations that modify the average efficiency of both the engines.

articles.title: SC^sharp: superconductivity intertwined with topological order
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.10679v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Superconductivity and intrinsic topological order can intertwine in ways that go beyond simple coexistence. Here we develop a classification framework for (2+1)D gapped superconductors with condensate charge 2ne. By focusing on the topological properties of superconducting vortices, we precisely characterize this interplay. We obtain a classification with increasing levels of intertwinement, from the well known invertible superconductors without topological order, to untwisted and twisted SC^ast, and finally to SCsharp. Our main finding is the family SCsharp, in which the elementary vortex carrying h/(2ne) flux cannot be factorized into an invertible superconductor vortex dressed by bulk anyons, and every elementary vortex is necessarily non-Abelian. For such phases, we also obtain no-go results: the elementary vortex sector has quantum dimension at least sqrt6 and cannot satisfy Fibonacci fusion rules. We develop a systematic algebraic framework to obtain all these superconducting phases through anyon condensation, allowing us to construct several infinite families of examples and make connections to anyon superconductivity. Finally, we introduce primitive SC^sharp phases for which factorization of every nontrivial vortex sector is obstructed, and argue that they cannot arise by disordering the relative phases of lower-charge superconducting condensates. Our classification scheme based on vortex properties allows us to uncover new distinctions between topologically ordered superconductors and constrain how they can be realized.

articles.title: Spin Chain with Continuous Exponential Symmetry: Topological Phase and Beyond
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.10682v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study symmetric gapped ground states of one-dimensional spin S chains with a continuous exponential symmetry U(1)rtimesmathbb Z₂ with integer base q, where the U(1) charge has a modulated unit of charge qL⁻j decaying exponentially with site j. The simplest model is a quantum breakdown model that can be viewed as a q-deformation of the XXZ Haldane spin chain. We show that the topology of their symmetric ground states crucially depends on S and q. For integer S, odd q allows a nontrivial mathbb Z₂ Haldane-type symmetry-protected topological (SPT) phase with protected edge modes, while even q allows no nontrivial SPT phase. For half-odd integer S, odd q prohibits any unique symmetric gapped ground state due to a Lieb-Schultz-Mattis obstruction, whereas even q enforces a novel symmetric gapped phase which we name as the ``half-SPT" phase. Unconventionally, the half-SPT phase only has a symmetry protected edge mode on one edge, and has half of the string orders of an SPT phase. Our results uncover a new type of symmetry-protected gapped phases beyond existing classification schemes.

articles.title: Millisecond phonon lifetimes in piezoelectric nanomechanical resonators
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.10700v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Piezoelectric nanomechanical resonators operating at gigahertz frequencies are a promising platform for quantum information processing and precision sensing, but phonon lifetimes have been limited to the microsecond range, widely attributed to the higher intrinsic loss of piezoelectric materials. Here we show that this limitation is not fundamental. Using a fabrication process informed by recent studies of defect-mediated loss in lithium niobate, we combine chemical restoration of ion-milled surfaces with a shadow-mask metallization process to produce lithium niobate phononic crystal resonators with inferred internal phonon lifetimes of up to 21 milliseconds at 3.6 gigahertz, corresponding to quality factors exceeding 4×10⁸ (f· Qᵢ > 10¹⁸) at millikelvin temperatures. By systematically varying the electrode-to-resonator spacing, we demonstrate that the measured lifetime is set by external coupling between the device and the measurement circuit rather than material loss. This establishes that lithium niobate, once fabrication-induced surface damage is removed, achieves an intrinsic quality comparable to the best mechanical materials while remaining an intrinsically piezoelectric platform with strong electromechanical coupling.

articles.title: Beyond Dry Flocking: Shape-Dependent Hydrodynamic Alignment
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.10709v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Flocking results from dynamical alignment among neighbors in a collection of active self-propelling objects. The intervening medium, typically a fluid, however, is not considered to be important for alignment, except for acting as a momentum sink. The flocking system is therefore described as momentum nonconserving "dry" active matter. Here we investigate a confined system of self-propelled Marangoni swimmers where feedback from the fluid medium, which crucially depends on the shape of the swimmers, influences their alignment. Using up to thirty partially camphor-coated triangular paper boats as polar swimmers, we uncover a disorder-to-order transition, and an unusual re-entrant order-to-disorder transition, as functions of camphor concentration and swimmer density, respectively. We reproduce these transitions by formulating a reaction-diffusion model for the camphor field, coupled to the swimmer dynamics, where propulsion forces arise from surface tension gradients. The shape-dependent hydrodynamic interaction discussed here could be central to efficient flocking in living organisms too.

articles.title: Resolving the interfacial mechanical landscape of monolayer NbSe2 grown by confined epitaxy
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.10725v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Confined epitaxy has recently emerged as a novel methodology for controlled growth of high-quality monolayer two-dimensional (2D) materials. However, mechanistic understanding remains limited to analysing nucleus adsorption and diffusion barriers. Here, I discover that van der Waals (vdW) confinement not only affects the specific adsorption and diffusion of nuclei on confined substrates but also induces strong coupling to atomic forces at the interface. Using artificial intelligence (AI) assisted density functional theory (DFT) calculations, I study how vdW confinement couples to the atomic motion of monolayer NbSe2 grown between c-plane sapphire and hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN). The calculated force-electronic landscape yields large mechanical forces of +0.070 and -0.04 eV per Angstrom on Nb and Se, respectively, giving rise to a unit-cell interfacial interaction energy up to 2.4 eV, comparable to reported adsorption and diffusion energies on similar substrates. The results indicate that interfacial mechanics may explain the success of confined epitaxy. The findings suggest that tuning interfacial mechanics, and related vdW mechanochemistry, could be a promising route to high-throughput, high-quality materials synthesis.

articles.title: Hierarchical Relaxation in Large-twist-angle Moire Drives Supermoire Formation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.10817v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Supermoire lattices in large-angle twisted bilayers have recently been shown to emerge from periodic arrangements of commensurate stacking motifs, yet the microscopic structural mechanism governing their formation has remained unresolved. Here, we uncover the microscopic origin of supermoire order as a hierarchical lattice relaxation process. Combining force-field simulations with experimental validation via super-resolution, layer-resolved multislice electron ptychography, our results identify interlayer Se-Se repulsion at the picometer scale as the driving force, giving rise to coupled short-range (about 1 nm) moire relaxation and coexisting long-range (about 10 nm) supermoire modulation. These findings demonstrate that even picometer-scale lattice relaxation remains critical in large-angle moire systems and must be explicitly considered in understanding their emergent electronic and quantum phenomena.

articles.title: Amplitude mode in Eliashberg superconductors
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.10826v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the BCS theory of superconductivity the amplitude (Higgs) mode is degenerate with the pair-breaking threshold: its frequency coincides with 2Δ, so it is an edge singularity rather than a true collective mode. This is why after a sudden weak perturbation at t=0 its oscillations decay algebraically as 1/sqrtt. We show that the retardation effects due to the phonon dynamics in the strong-coupling theory lift this degeneracy. The Higgs mode detaches from the pair-breaking edge 2Δ_g, set by the spectral gap, and becomes a sharp subgap excitation. We determine its frequency from the longitudinal pair susceptibility evaluated directly on the real frequency axis, using the Eilenberger equations for Migdal--Eliashberg theory with the Einstein phonon spectrum. The response of the mass renormalization supplies at least two fifths of the displacement, and possibly all of it: with it switched off, the binding falls below the resolution of the calculation. Its consequences, however, are significant because a percent-level shift transfers about a quarter of the spectral weight of the amplitude channel out of the two-quasiparticle continuum into a discrete energy level. What experiment sees is therefore not the displacement itself but its consequence: amplitude oscillations that persist instead of decaying as 1/sqrtt.

articles.title: A nonclassical law of the wall in superfluid helium-4
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.10923v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The logarithmic law of the wall is one of the most robust scaling laws of classical turbulence, yet whether it survives in a quantum fluid such as superfluid ⁴He (He II) remains unknown. At a solid wall, the viscous normal-fluid and inviscid superfluid components of He II obey fundamentally different boundary conditions, yet their motions can be coupled through quantized vortices. How these competing effects organize the near-wall flow remains an open question in quantum-fluid hydrodynamics. Here we visualize the near-wall velocity field in mechanically driven He II pipe flows at Reynolds numbers up to 1.26×10⁶ using molecular tagging velocimetry and independently determine the wall shear stress from pressure-drop measurements. We find that the normal-fluid velocity develops a robust logarithmic profile, showing that a law-of-the-wall description persists despite the two-fluid nature of He II. Strikingly, however, the resulting wall law is distinctly nonclassical: the effective Kármán constant is less than half its classical value and remains nearly unchanged across the temperature range studied. This invariance, despite substantial changes in the relative fractions of the two components, indicates strong dynamical coupling between them. These results not only reveal how a universal law of classical turbulence is transformed by quantum hydrodynamics, but also provide valuable guidance for the design and operation of cryogenic cooling systems involving He II transport.

articles.title: Three-dimensional dopant distribution from a single, out-of-focus spectroscopic image
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.11053v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Increasing miniaturization of nanoscale devices makes determining the three-dimensional distribution of dopants increasingly important. In out-of-focus spectroscopic scanning transmission electron microscopy images, we show that dopant atoms appear as disks with radii relating to dopant depth, allowing the three-dimensional distribution of dopants to be determined from simple geometric analysis of a single out-of-focus image. Through numerical experiments on Si-doped graphene we validate statistical detection and Bayesian inference methods to quantify confidence and uncertainties while making the analysis more robust at lower dose. We present proof-of-concept experimental data from an Fe-doped spinel, retrieving dopant depth to within around 2 nanometres.

articles.title: Probing and Manipulating Quantum Materials with Strong-field Terahertz and Mid-infrared Radiation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.11126v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Emergent phenomena in quantum materials arise from interactions among different degrees of freedom. Identifying these interactions and establishing their roles in ordered states are central problems in condensed-matter physics and provide a basis for controlling material properties. Many relevant low-energy excitations and gaps lie in the terahertz (THz) and mid-infrared (MIR) range, where intense phase-stable fields can both interrogate nonlinear dynamics and drive selected degrees of freedom far from equilibrium. This review surveys recent progress in probing and manipulating quantum materials with strong-field THz and MIR radiation, with emphasis on nonlinear electronic dynamics, collective-mode coupling, symmetry-sensitive responses and field-induced changes in electronic structure and ordered states. Particular attention is given to developments enabled by the Synergetic Extreme Condition User Facility (SECUF).

articles.title: Light-induced interlayer spacing dynamics via orbital phonon coupling
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.11212v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Interlayer coupling controls the electronic properties of layered van der Waals transition metal dichalcogenides. We investigate light-induced control of the interlayer spacing through orbital-selective excitation in trilayer 1T'-WSe2 and 1T'-WS2. Real-time time-dependent density functional theory simulations show that the interlayer spacing contracts or expands depending on whether chalcogen p-orbital density is depleted from or accumulated in the interlayer region. Effective Lindblad models coupled to the lattice dynamics reproduce these contrasting responses with simplified dynamics. A single effective excited state captures the cosine-like displacive motion in trilayer 1T'-WSe2, whereas the shift of the equilibrium spacing in trilayer 1T'-WS2 requires two excited states with different electron-phonon couplings and relaxation channels. Static calculations at varied interlayer spacings indicate that these spacing changes modify the electronic gaps and could access different electronic phases. These results connect orbital redistribution, carrier relaxation, and interlayer breathing motion, and establish orbital-selective optical excitation as a route to tuning the electronic properties of layered materials.

articles.title: A hinged honeycomb with zero bulk modulus retaining more than four-fifths of its constituent's shear modulus
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.11280v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A Poisson's ratio near -1 indicates only that the bulk modulus is small compared with the shear modulus. In solid-void structures, the mechanism that frees the dilation usually weakens the resistance to shear as well, resulting in both moduli becoming small. In two-dimensional linear elasticity, we demonstrate that this loss is not inevitable. We consider a honeycomb of regular hexagonal blocks of a single incompressible isotropic elastic solid, joined along their whole edges by ideal interfaces that allow relative sliding along a direction inclined to the edge normal. Collective infinitesimal block rotations produce an exact dilational mechanism, so the effective bulk modulus vanishes, while sixfold symmetry ensures isotropy. The interfaces, however, transmit traction along their whole length. In a solid-void realization, each interface is replaced with fine solid plates separated by void, which bend easily yet retain their capacity to transmit axial force. Such dilational materials, which expand or contract freely while resisting every change of shape, could serve as interlayers that accommodate thermal or swelling mismatch while still transmitting shear, and as components in stents and deployable structures that change size without changing shape. An explicit, statically admissible stress field and the complementary energy principle yield a rigorous lower bound on the retained shear modulus, and a limiting argument transfers this bound to the solid-void mixtures. The honeycomb retains more than four-fifths of its constituent's shear modulus at zero bulk modulus: the supremum S of the normalized shear modulus of such mixtures satisfies S > 0.8528 > 4/5, exceeding the value attained by Milton's construction.

articles.title: Displacement-Field-Induced Ionization of Defect States in High-Quality hBN
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.11297v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Encapsulation of two-dimensional (2D) materials with hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) is widely used to fabricate ultraclean van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures for optoelectronic and quantum transport studies. These devices are often operated under strong out-of-plane displacement fields that tune the electronic properties of the active 2D material, while the surrounding hBN is typically assumed to remain electronically inert. This assumption, however, neglects defect states that are present even in high-quality hBN crystals. Here, we probe their response to the applied displacement field using monolayer graphene encapsulated between hBN crystals as a sensitive charge sensor. Increasing the displacement field induces notable charge transfer between graphene and hBN, producing additional electron doping of 10-20x10⁹ cm⁽⁻²⁾ even at the moderate displacement field (~0.5 V nm⁽⁻¹⁾), while simultaneously increasing carrier-density inhomogeneity of the graphene layer. Both effects are consistent with ionization of defect states within the hBN bandgap, with the bulk density ~1-7x10⁽⁻⁵⁾ nm⁽⁻³⁾ varying across different hBN crystals. Our results show that displacement-field-induced defect ionization in hBN can modify the electronic response of vdW heterostructures, with direct implications for device design and interpretation of experiments.

articles.title: Laser fragmentation in liquid - constructing a generic reaction map
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.11494v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Excitation of absorbing colloids in liquid by pulsed laser irradiation creates highly non-equilibrium states of matter that relax via defined pathways of thermal and non-thermal dissipation channels. The structural fingerprint of these channels can be probed by ultrafast it in situ x-ray scattering methods and classified as a function of temporal delay of excitation excitation density, or specifically laser fluence. We study the example of photo-excitation of a gold colloid by picosecond laser pulses at the interband absorption band at 400 nm in water.
